[Objective: Talk to Mornye]
Worried Researcher: Professor Mornye! Where are you? If possible, please return at once! Ahhh, Dr. Anslem, please calm down!
Mornye: What's happening?
Worried Researcher: It's about the  launch process. The professors are arguing again...
Mornye: That's the second time this month.
Worried Researcher: We can't get a word in. We need you here…
Mornye: …Not that my being there will help.
Mornye: I'll be there shortly. And you... Remember to breathe.
Mornye: Sorry. There's an urgent matter I need to attend to.
[Dialogue Option]  It's fine. I'll head back now then.
[Dialogue Option]  I could wait for you here.
Mornye: Oh, there's no need to shy away. If you're free, you can accompany me.
Mornye: The Research Institute is open to Startorch students. Walking around here might give you some useful insights.

title: What Burns Beneath Frostlands
subsection: Head to the Artificial Sun Lab
content:
[Objective: Head to the Artificial Sun Lab]
Rover: That artificial sun they spoke of...
Mornye: In simple terms, it's our plan to replace the "sun" you see in the sky.
Rover: You're planning to replace the Exostrider's Drive? Is that what the New Solar Ceremony is about?
Mornye: You remember...? Did the Black Shores tell you this?
Rover: It's the talk of the Academy now.
Mornye: Right. Replacing it is critical to reactivating the Exostrider. And really, we can't stay wrapped in its warm light forever.
Rover: How far along is the research on the Exostrider? How much do we really know?
Mornye: ...
Mornye: More than you'd expect... fellow researcher.
Mornye: I'll show you the details once we are in the lab.
Mornye: Almost there. Hope they've reached a consensus.
Mornye: ...I guess not.

title: What Burns Beneath Frostlands
subsection: Find out what the researchers are arguing about
content:
[Objective: Find out what the researchers are arguing about]
Flustered Assistant: Professor Mornye! What a relief to see you—
Mornye: Actually—
Mornye: Well then...
???: I appreciate your perspective, Professor Anslem.
???: But according to Royan calculations, this launch window is the best we've had in decades.
Anslem: How can you be so certain, Warren? Their "optimal window" is derived from those indecipherable runes, with no methodology disclosed. Even our most advanced computational systems have failed to decipher their process!
Warren: The Roya are our partners, Professor.
Warren: Their calculations are unquestionable. All we can do is uphold our side of the bargain and make sure the New Solar Ceremony goes off without a hitch.
Warren: Well then... I believe counsel from a third person may serve us well at this point.
Mornye: I'm inclined to proceed with the original plan.
Mornye: But given the unsatisfying results from the last simulation, I understand Professor Anslem's concerns. I'll go to Bjartr Woods to consult with the Heliodic Six and reverify the parameters.
Warren: What matters now is ensuring that the Institute can calculate and calibrate the Reactor Drive's data in time for the launch of the new sun.
Warren: We all know the importance of Hyvatia in this process, and I sincerely hope you'll place more trust in it, Anslem.
Warren: This is a shared achievement between the Collective and the Roya, the very future of Lahai-Roi. I respect your caution and the pride you take in your work. But please, don't let past failures hold you back now.
Anslem: Hmph, fine words… Just don't forget that I warned you.

metadata.subsection: Find out what the researchers are arguing about

title: What Burns Beneath Frostlands
subsection: Find out what the researchers are arguing about
content:
Anslem: Hmph, fine words… Just don't forget that I warned you.



Warren: Sorry if I'm being blunt. I'm sure Professor Mornye has her reasons for bringing someone into the lab.
Warren: But I recognize every face here, except yours. Mind telling me who you are?
[Dialogue Option]  Rover. I'm a freshman.
Warren: Ah, so you're here to record your Cassette? Though, with the Void Storm in full force…
Mornye: He comes recommended by the Black Shores.
Warren: The Black Shores... I see.
Warren: So you came here by the same means as Miss Chisa, correct?
Warren: Her sudden appearance in the Academy caused quite a stir that day. Would you mind sharing how you made it here?
Warren: I don't deal with the Academy all that much. All I heard was that someone appeared out of nowhere outside the gates.
Mornye: This may not be the right time for such questions, Professor Warren.
Warren: Oh... forgive me. Curiosity has always been my second nature.
Warren: Well, if you have the Black Shores' recommendation, you're certainly a student here.
Warren: Allow me to introduce myself: I'm Warren, supervisor of this lab.
Warren: Aside from the rooms marked "No Entry," the rest of the facility is open for student visits.
Warren: I'm sure Professor Mornye will give you a thorough tour, but please don't take too long. A key member like her needs to focus on our project.
Warren: Alas, my work calls. I'll leave you two to it.

Worried Researcher: That last proposal... can we even make the final testing window? Isn't it a bit too conservative?
Careful Researcher: But Professor Anslem just said it was too radical. He told me to revise it again.
Worried Researcher: Ugh... Fine. I'll go refine the backup plan on my end. There are still a few data points I need to recalculate.
Artificial Sun - Helios Status Log

Massive cultivation tanks house many ancient plant species you've never seen on the surface. Life was once scarce in these underground caverns, until the Reactor Drive ignited here. In its relentless pursuit of progress, the Spacetrek Collective did not forget to retrieve the dormant seeds that slept beneath the Roya Frostlands.
"From a single drop of water, a single seed, a single torch... life will find its way."

Angry Researcher: Hah, Warren? That sanctimonious bastard is just reveling in the spotlight. Is even half his mind on the actual research?
Anxious Researcher: Come on, that’s not fair… He did secure last quarter’s funding. And he’s mediated plenty of project disputes…

subsection: Return to the hall of the Lab
content:
[Objective: Return to the hall of the Lab]
Mornye: Now that you're caught up, may I ask you a question?
[Dialogue Option]  Yes, Professor.
Mornye: Would you like to attend the New Solar Ceremony?
Rover: Me? But... I'm just a freshman.
Mornye: Consider this my personal invitation.
Mornye: I… I'd want you there to witness it. The rise of the new sun, and humanity taking their first steps into the future they've built with their own hands.
[Dialogue Option]  Since you put it that way...
[Dialogue Option]  Of course.
Rover: I'd be honored to witness the rise of Lahai-Roi's new sun.
Mornye: Then it's settled.
Lab Researcher: Void Storm detected near Sundermere... Readings rising rapidly!
Lab Researcher: The source is... the Hyvatia Detector?!
Mornye: Give me a full report.
Lab Researcher: Yes, Professor. Hyvatia's been compromised by the Void Storm. It's gone rogue. The Defense Array is activating...
Lab Researcher: Their target is... the Institute itself.
[Dialogue Option]  What happened?
Mornye: The Void Storm has corrupted the Hyvatia Detector, a critical sensor for the Reactor Drive. It's off course and now targeting us.
[Dialogue Option]  Hy-what-tia?

content:
[Objective: ]
Lynae: How did... Never mind. Now's not the time for questions. Careful, Hyvatia's gone haywire. We need to stop it before it reaches the Institute!

title: What Burns Beneath Frostlands
content:
Lynae: See that spot? That's its weak point! ...Watch out for its attacks! I'll handle things here!



Lynae: Barely made it. Thanks for the help.
Rover: So... why were you here?
Lynae: I...
Warren: W-what happened here?!
Warren: Seal off the area immediately. Pull the system logs and report all damages to the Institute. Check the Reactor Drive as well. We need to raise our security levels.
Warren: If I recall correctly, you're supposed to be in class, Miss Lynae. Why are you here?
Warren: I expect a proper explanation.
Lab Researcher: Professor Warren, they're just students—
Warren: Quiet. I'm asking her, not you.
Lynae: I... I noticed that Hyvatia was out of control, so I tried to stop it.
Warren: A malfunction in the Institute's primary Detector is no small matter for a student to handle. You should have notified the Academy or the Institute immediately, not thrown yourself into danger alone.
Lynae: I just acted before I could think.
Warren: Acted before you could think? Regardless of your circumstance, if you can't provide a reasonable explanation, we've reason to believe you're involved in this "incident," directly or indirectly.
Lynae: Its malfunction had nothing to do with me.
Warren: Denial won't get you anywhere. If you don't tell us exactly what happened, I'll have no choice but to expel you under the Academy's confidentiality clause.
Warren: Do you even remember what Startorch stands for, Miss Lynae? What our mission is?
Rover: Please calm down, Professor Warren.
Warren: Ah, Rover... Didn't expect to see you again so soon. You must be feeling unsettled after such an incident on your first day.
Warren: Of course, I don't mean to put the blame on a student, but her actions clearly violated Academy regulations.
Rover: (Lynae's behavior is suspicious… but judging by what I just saw, she didn't seem like she was trying to damage the Detector.)
Rover: (There must be another reason. Besides… it seemed she was about to tell me something before.)
Rover: It was Lynae who protected me from Hyvatia's attack.
Rover: If she were the culprit, she could've slipped away in the chaos, but she didn't. She worked with me to contain the damage.
Rover: Until we know the cause for certain, punishing her is... premature.
Warren: My apologies for the tone. But we must inform the Academy and investigate every possible angle behind this.
Warren: The Institute has poured everything into this Ceremony. If something has gone wrong, we need to uncover who is responsible. Miss Lynae, please come with me. We'll address this with the faculty.
Warren: And as a witness to the incident, I'm afraid you'll need to come as well, Rover.
Lynae: ...
Warren: After you.

title: What Burns Beneath Frostlands
content:
Warren: And as a witness to the incident, I'm afraid you'll need to come as well, Rover.
Lynae: ...
Warren: After you.



Academy Instructor: The Academy has reviewed the incident, Professor Warren. While we share your concern over the Institute's loss, blaming a single student...
Warren: What were you doing when Hyvatia lost control, Miss Lynae? Why were you at the Institute during class hours?
Lynae: I was escorting Rover to burn his Cassette at the Institute.
Lynae: On my way back to the Academy, I noticed abnormal frequency spikes and contaminated Exoswarm near Sundermere.
Lynae: Before I could act, I was surrounded. I tried to contact the Academy, but the Void Storm blocked communications.
Lynae: Exoswarm remains should still be there. I assume... you are already investigating them?
Warren: No such remains were found, Miss Lynae. Making things up won't help you.
Lynae: That was quick.
Lynae: What about the surveillance cameras? They're equipped to handle Void Storm interference. They should've captured the Exoswarm before things escalated.
Warren: They didn't. And in fact, you aren't in the footage at all. I wonder what you were doing at that time. Avoiding the cameras, perhaps?
Rover: What if the footage was tampered with? Her presence could've been erased.
Warren: Possible. But only if she and the Exoswarm were truly there.
Academy Instructor: Since neither side can confirm that, how about we start by verifying if the footage was altered?
Warren: We should expand the scope of the investigation. Remember the security breach in the database? There might be more compromised than just today's feed.
Academy Instructor: You mean the breach that exposed a flaw in the system? Fair enough.
Ms. Voss: Do you have anything else to add, Miss Lynae? Don't worry, we're here to help you.
Lynae: ...No.
Academy Instructor: Then please remain on Academy grounds until the investigation is concluded.

title: What Burns Beneath Frostlands

Lynae: ...No.
Academy Instructor: Then please remain on Academy grounds until the investigation is concluded.



Warren: One last thing, Miss Lynae. You're from the New Federation, right?
Lynae: What do you mean?
Warren: Nothing. I just noticed you stay at the Academy even during breaks. Never thought of going home?
Lynae: Thanks for asking, Professor. I keep in touch with my parents whenever I can. If you're implying I have some secret agenda, you'll be disappointed.
Warren: Not at all. I simply wonder if you don't want to return.
Lynae: I don't think that's something you should concern yourself with, Professor.

Lynae: Phew...
Lynae: Thanks… for speaking up for me.
[Dialogue Option]  Why not tell them the truth?
Rover: What was that device you had when Hyvatia went berserk?
Lynae: Straight to the point, huh? I thought you'd let it slide, like they did.
Rover: Highly unlikely.
Lynae: Good... you're still you.
Rover: What's your real purpose?
Lynae: Let's talk somewhere else. This place is suffocating.

title: What Burns Beneath Frostlands
content:
[Objective: Follow Lynae]
Rover: You're not just a student, are you?
Lynae: I've always wished I were just an ordinary student. But… well.
Lynae: Ever thought about throwing everything away? The responsibilities, the secrets you can't share, the constant weight on your shoulders… just letting it all go, and living a carefree life like the rest of them?
Rover: ...
Lynae: Heh, just a passing thought. I know it's not something you'd admit to, whether you've ever wished for it or not. Not someone like you.
Lynae: But we're not the same. I just… really want to be like the other students here.
Studenet: Oh, Lynae! I haven't had the chance to thank you yet. The material you gave me boosted the device's power by 35%! That's amazing!
Lynae: No big deal… I just got lucky, really.

title: What Burns Beneath Frostlands
content:
Lynae: No big deal… I just got lucky, really.



Lynae: Ha... this place always brings me peace.
Lynae: You want to know who I really am so you can connect the dots on that incident, right?
Lynae: I can tell you... but only if you promise me one thing: Let me stay here. At the Academy. As a student.
Rover: Is it really so important to you?
Lynae: ...Yeah. More than I can say.
Rover: ...
Lynae: I'll take your silence as a yes then.
Lynae: So, you've heard those old "pulling a switcheroo" stories, right?
???: HQ... this is Lynae...
???: Sorry Overseer... we were... ambushed...
???: Don't worry... I'll make it to Startorch Academy in Lahai-Roi in time...
???: I'll complete the mission... assigned by the Grand Architect...
Lynae: Spoiler alert: their mission wasn't completed.
[Dialogue Option]  Overseer...?
[Dialogue Option]  The Fractsidus...?
Lynae: Professor Warren knows I'm from the New Federation, but not exactly which part.
Lynae: It's called the Lawless Zone. Let's just say... you'd see blood spilled every three days, on average. That's where I grew up.
Lynae: I had talent, and the New Fed saw it. Put me to work. Off the record. Dirty jobs.
Lynae: Then that day happened… It was an accident, but I saw my chance.
Lynae: ...An admission letter to Lahai-Roi's Startorch Academy.
[Dialogue Option]  So that was your "switcheroo."
Lynae: I found that recording I played you on the real Lynae's liaison at the Academy.
Lynae: So I quickly learned she wasn't just a regular student from the start.
Lynae: Even so, I came to Lahai-Roi.
Lynae: Everything here… It's nothing like the New Fed. People don't question themselves when they wake up, brush their teeth, and look in the mirror. They just know who they are.
Rover: And you want to be one of them.
Lynae: Look, as far as I'm concerned, the Fractsidus threatens my school life. They're your enemy too.
Lynae: We have shared interests. That's a solid basis for us to cooperate.
Rover: ...A "student" wouldn't talk like that.
Rover: Even if we solve this, do you think you'll be able to look at yourself in the mirror afterward?
Lynae: ...
Rover: That being said, I do know what matters most now.
Rover: I stood up to Warren for you because I chose to trust you. And I'll own that choice.
Lynae: Ha... you know, sometimes you really do sound like a teacher.
Lynae: Alright then, let me rephrase.
Lynae: I like this school. I've met good people here, people who treat me like their friend. People worth protecting.
Lynae: That's why I hope you'll help me find out why the Fractsidus are here in Lahai-Roi, Rover.
Rover: Let's do this. Together.
Lynae: I've been holding in these words forever. Ahh.. Feels good to finally get 'em out.
Lynae: As for our first lead...
[Dialogue Option]  Any ideas?
Lynae: What we do know is... Hyvatia's malfunction and the contaminated Exoswarm are definitely connected to this device I found.
Lynae: It looks like Academy tech... maybe the Department of Engineering's lab can shed some light.
Rover: But why would the Academy allow something this dangerous to circulate freely?
Lynae: Maybe its appearance is just a disguise. Or maybe it means its maker had free access to the Department's resources.
Lynae: After all, that "contact" who's been feeding me orders might still be inside the Academy.
[Dialogue Option]  Makes sense. Then we start with the Department of Engineering.
Lynae: If you're ready to start making moves, I know a shortcut.
[Dialogue Option]  How short?
Lynae: Right this way!

subsection: Investigate the manufacturing record of the Department of Engineering
content:
[Objective: Investigate the manufacturing record of the Department of Engineering]
Lynae: Found it. It was hiding pretty deep.
Lynae: Like I thought, the record isn't in the ordinary directory. It's triple-classified, disguised as regular system data.
Rover: Which means… someone hijacked the Department's equipment to make this?
Lynae: Correct. I just scanned the device itself. It looks like a basic calibrator, but the inside is completely different.
Lynae: Long story short, it stores and amplifies a tiny slice of Void Storm frequency, just enough to make stuff designed from Exostrider tech lose control.
Rover: Stuff designed from Exostrider tech…
Lynae: And here's the kicker—whoever made this can control it remotely.
Rover: So it can be activated again at any time.
Lynae: Exactly. It's literally a ticking time bomb.
Lynae: You're probably wondering why I didn't hand this over to the Academy, right? Before we identify the Fractsidus "contact," I'm not letting it out of my sight.
Lynae: So first, we've gotta neutralize the threat. With the production records and device data, I can try to overwrite the device's permissions. Get it to only activate if it resonates with me.
Lynae: It'll reboot during the process, though... and, uh, there might be some noise.
Rover: You mean the mechs here will be affected?
Lynae: Yes. That's why I'll need you to… keep them in check during the process.
Rover: Sure, I've got you.
Lynae: Alright—Starting now!
Lynae: Having someone cover my back like this... Hm, not too bad.

[Dialogue Option]  You look nervous.
[Dialogue Option]  Your hands are shaking.

[Dialogue Option]  How do you know that's Hyvatia's waveform?
Lynae: Um... Heh, just by, uh... browsing the Academy forum.
Lynae: Mm, alright, I was once tasked to hack into the Institute's database and tamper with Hyvatia's calibration data.
Lynae: But I didn't change anything. Just threw in a few emojis and left a note telling them to upgrade their encryption.
Lynae: That backfired though. Got me flagged.
[Dialogue Option]  So that's how it happened.

Lynae: Let's head to the Spacetrek Archive then.

Lynae: You look beat. Everything okay, Miss I.R.I.S.?

[Dialogue Option]  Maybe next time.

title: What Burns Beneath Frostlands
content:
[Objective: Look around the room]
Comfortable Sofa
The room is a comfortable mess, where you can almost see vignettes of its occupant’s life—curled up with a soft pillow, diving into studies or hobbies with bright-eyed focus, chasing down every curiosity, big or small, or weathering the occasional speedbumps of frustration over grades and credits. She lives every moment of her Academy life in earnest, just like any other student here.
Lynae's desk
A desk in organized chaos. Several spray cans in various colors sit in one corner. They were clearly used for spraying designs on models.
Acceptance Letter
A meticulously preserved Startorch Academy acceptance letter. It seems to hold extraordinary significance for her.
Snacks on the desk
An assortment of “limited edition” snacks sits on the desk: “Mint Current” Flavor Squeezy Jelly, “Herald of Yore” Canned Cake, and pies with mysteriously sourced ingredients. It’s hard to imagine what state of mind led her to purchase these… unique flavor profiles.
Statement of Accountability
The Terminal shows several letter drafts, each heavily marked with revisions.  “To the esteemed Academy leadership and faculty: I am writing with a heavy heart and sincere remorse to submit this formal statement of accountability.” “This month marks the third time I have performed a full, borderline-non-compliant custom wrap on my vehicle, alongside unsanctioned performance modifications. I also swapped the horn for the Academy’s class dismissal bell and took the vehicle for a test drive during class hours…” “...Such behavior violates the Academy’s rules and sets a bad example for the student body. It is most definitely unacceptable!” “I now fully grasp the severity of my actions. I promise to immediately remove all non-compliant parts and restore the vehicle to its OEM-spec condition. I will study the traffic regulations again, and I solemnly swear that no such violations will occur again…” “The teacher was right. The Academy roads serve as our means of transit, not as a proving ground for the Department of Engineering. Under no circumstances should they be used for vehicular  dynamics experiments…” “̶R̶e̶g̶a̶r̶d̶i̶n̶g̶ ̶t̶h̶e̶ ̶“̶R̶a̶i̶n̶b̶o̶w̶ ̶E̶x̶h̶a̶u̶s̶t̶ ̶T̶r̶a̶i̶l̶s̶”̶ ̶m̶o̶d̶i̶f̶i̶c̶a̶t̶i̶o̶n̶,̶ ̶g̶i̶v̶e̶n̶ ̶h̶o̶w̶ ̶e̶f̶f̶e̶c̶t̶i̶v̶e̶ ̶i̶t̶ ̶i̶s̶ ̶i̶n̶ ̶a̶l̶e̶r̶t̶i̶n̶g̶ ̶t̶r̶a̶i̶l̶i̶n̶g̶ ̶v̶e̶h̶i̶c̶l̶e̶s̶ ̶t̶o̶ ̶m̶a̶i̶n̶t̶a̶i̶n̶ ̶a̶ ̶s̶a̶f̶e̶ ̶d̶i̶s̶t̶a̶n̶c̶e̶…̶ (Don’t include this. It will just sound like I’m making excuses…)  …The subsequent drafts contained similar content, just dated differently.
Lynae: Well, look who's here! How's everything going?
Rover: I've informed Dr. Herssen and Professor Mornye about the situation. Once the Institute gets the warning, they'll prepare accordingly.
Rover: The Fractsidus's plan is still unclear, so it's best not to act rashly. Any investigation, leave that to me.
Lynae: Mm, nothing urgent for now. But since you're here, maybe we could talk a bit.
Lynae: Sorry about this mess. I really should've cleaned up.
Lynae: You know, back in the New Fed my room was just a bed, a chair, a desk… and my weapons.
Lynae: Mercenaries? We don't know what a "real life" is. We only know survival. That's why we never settle down. Everything that isn't gear or a weapon is just dead weight.
Lynae: But… the more "dead weight" I pick up here, the more I realize how much this place means to me.
Lynae: At first, I only saw the Academy as a way to outrun my merc past. Didn't care about the cost. I took the chance, no hesitation.
Rover: Startorch Academy... It's really important to you, isn't it?
Lynae: Yeah, every day here is a blessing! I get to splash color around, cruise under the sun, and learn stuff I never even knew existed.
Lynae: This place may be buried under frost, but it feels brighter and freer than anywhere I've been.
Rover: About that anonymous report on "Lynae's" criminal records and prison history… Who are they really talking about?
Lynae: The Fractsidus's "Lynae."
Lynae: Mercs in the New Fed are essentially government contractors. After I took her identity and faked my death, they wiped all my merc records clean.
Lynae: Now that I think about it, it's kind of funny… I can't even prove who I really am anymore.
Lynae: ...Whichever "Lynae" I am, I don't belong here.
Lynae: But still… I truly appreciate what you've done for me.
Lynae: Thank you. For speaking up for me, more than once. And… thank you for trusting me.
Lynae: It's rare to have trust unbound by contracts.
[Dialogue Option]  Isn't it a bit early to give up?
[Dialogue Option]  The Fractsidus won't quit just because you walk away.
Lynae: I'm not a student here anymore.
Lynae: The Academy let me know the result of their investigation.
Lynae: They're kicking me out, sending me back to the New Fed. Then it's either back to the old work... or spend my life behind bars.
Lynae: Not like I'd choose either one of those.
Lynae: So… before the Academy locks me down for good, this is my last chance to run.
Lynae: I've never belonged here. This stolen school life was always gonna end, sooner or later.
Rover: Is that what you really believe?
Lynae: Sorry, but I have to go.
Announcement: Attention all faculty and student. Voidstorm activity detected. Seek immediate shelter nearby. Do not leave Academy grounds.
Announcement: The Voidstorm will cover the entire campus in five minutes. Initiate emergency Protocol 5, now.
Rover: The Voidworm. And the target is... No, not the Research Institute. It's heading for the Academy.

(Cutscene plays)
Lynae: Dark alleys. Hushed whispers. Greedy eyes hiding behind masks...
Lynae: That was everyday life for a mercenary.
Lynae: I used to wonder, what if the sky above me wasn't always black?
Lynae: What if there really was another life I could choose?
Lynae: Even if the price would forever haunt me from the shadows...
Lynae: ...I'd still take the deal. No question.
Lynae: Every day at the Academy has been more than I ever let myself hope for.
Lynae: The bright halls. Charging into the unknown with people who had my back. Eyes locked on the edge of the world. Those "good mornings" at dawn...
Lynae: Moments that don't just shine, but burn.
Lynae: Now I know that living, really living, has colors I didn't even know existed. So bright... you'd bleed to hold onto it.
Lynae: But just like the stories in all those old comics...
Lynae: Stolen time always comes knocking.
"Is it really okay... to run away?"

content:
[Objective: Head to the garden]
Lynae: You're here!
[Dialogue Option]  How've you been the last two days?
Lynae: The Fractsidus investigation is still dragging on. And since I'm technically not enrolled yet, no classes for me. Ugh... They even confiscated my ride, too. Professor Mornye dumped a ton of homework on me to keep me busy.
[Dialogue Option]  So, you're dodging your homework now?
Lynae: Not really. It's just that, ever since that news piece I sent you, people won't stop coming up to me for selfies.
Lynae: Some even ask for my autograph. Stuff like this is a first for me, I'll tell you that.
[Dialogue Option]  So that's why you're hiding out here?
Lynae: Yeah...
Lynae: The Academy still hasn't revealed my past identity. Feels wrong accepting praise from people who don't know the full story.
Lynae: It's kind of... unreal. Like, even after everyone finds out who I really am, I still get to stay. Makes me feel stupidly lucky.
Lynae: Anyway, enough about that. I just got notified—the entrance exam is tomorrow.
[Dialogue Option]  Good luck.
Lynae: Thanks, I'll need it! It had better go smoothly!
[Dialogue Option]  Feeling nervous?
Lynae: I'm not worried about the grades.
Lynae: It's just... the school will send me a new admission letter. I'll be starting all over again as a first-year in the Prep Program.
[Dialogue Option]  So we're in the same class now?
Lynae: Hmm? Come to think of it... That's not so bad, after all.
[Dialogue Option]  This time, the admission letter will be your own.
Lynae: My own letter... Yeah, you're right.
Lynae: It all feels kind of unreal.
Lynae: There's still a lot I need to do and face, but for the first time, I can actually breathe.
Lynae: I've had good times before, but there was always that weight in my chest.
Lynae: Now, I've lifted that weight off with my own hands. And maybe... just maybe, it's 'cause you were there that I could.

content:
[Objective: Talk to Lynae]
Lynae: Whew... Can't remember the last time I felt this refreshed. Before you rush off to save the next crisis, care to hang around a bit?
[Dialogue Option]  I was meaning to ask you about something...
[Dialogue Option]  I have something else to attend to.
Lynae: Hehe, good! I'm in the mood to chat.
Lynae: Anything you wanna know? Fire away!
[Dialogue Option]  About that Voidworm...
Lynae: The Academy has recycled that Voidworm's debris. The Research Institute is dismantling that metal chunk as we speak, in case it's engulfed again by the Void Storm.
Lynae: The Spacetrek Collective is also working on plans for better defenses against this kind of attack. After all, as long as the Threnodian and the Void Storm remain, the threat of the Voidworms isn't going anywhere.
Lynae: Speaking of... You said your frequency loss may be related to the Voidworms? How are you feeling now? Did you get another check up?
[Dialogue Option]  I've restored some of my frequencies...
[Dialogue Option]  But not quite fully recovered.
Lynae: I see. I Hope you find out the root cause of your symptoms soon.
[Dialogue Option]  About the inquiry...
Lynae: Well, it was more of a "mental health" counseling session than an inquiry. The staff were really thoughtful... which caught me by surprise.
Lynae: My mercenary past, the whole fake Fractsidus operative act... This time, I spilled everything. No point hiding anymore.
[Dialogue Option]  How did you deal with the Fractsidus device?
Lynae: The Academy had to forfeit it as a key exhibit. But the one who built this device—and caused the Voidmatter Barrier breach—still hasn't been unmasked. Fractsidus moles may still lurk within the Academy.
Lynae: And that "liaison"... No way the Fractsidus will just fold and walk away. It's no time to let our guards down. I'll keep an eye out for anything suspicious.
[Dialogue Option]  About your future plans...
Lynae: My future plans? Hmm... Well, first on the list is to pass the entrance exam and join Startorch officially as a student.
Lynae: As for what comes next...
Lynae: ...I haven't planned that far ahead. I never felt I belonged here. So I was taking things one day at a time...
Lynae: But now... It seems like I get to choose a future I want. I'm still wrapping my head around all the choices I have.
[Dialogue Option]  I'm here if you ever need someone to help you sort things out.
[Dialogue Option]  I believe you'll find the choice for you.
[Dialogue Option]  I've got nothing else. Wish you every success.
Lynae: Thank you for being there for me... time after time.
Lynae: I wish the best for you! Next time we meet, we'll be classmates!

title: What Burns Beneath Frostlands
content:
Voidworm - An amalgamated horror that often emerges alongside Void Storms. During lulls between Storms, it primarily inhabits the highly concentrated Voidmatter environment of the Mawburrow Desert. The Voidmatter Regulators on its head serve as both its power source and its weakness.
Infirmary - Officially the "Resonator Nursing Unit," the infirmary is a clinical-research hybrid facility overseen by Rabelle College. Managed by Academy physician Luuk Herssen, it utilizes Frequency Therapeutics to provide comprehensive healthcare for the students and faculty of Startorch Academy.

[Dialogue Option]  Congrats on a successful enrollment.
[Dialogue Option]  So when’s our next joyride going to be?
Lynae:  Ugh, I really wanna hit the road with you again, but I'm kinda on a "mental health watchlist." If I break even one tiny rule on day one, Miss Lucilla will be dragging me in for a "friendly chat."
Lynae:  I gotta hold out until I figure out a route that slips past the cameras.
Lynae: Oh, but hey, you got Mornye's email about the , right? It's almost go-time. How about we hang by the entrance, and then we—
Mornye:  Material fatigue... thermal cycles... boundary conditions... initial stress states...
"TARD-E Unit"::  Infraction detected. High-wattage devices are strictly prohibited in dormitory zones.
Mornye:  The core differential equation is... elastoplastic transition... cyclic strength coefficients...
"TARD-E Unit"::  Please comply with the "Startorch Academy Dormitory Code of Conduct"! Issuing first warning. Issuing second warning!
Mornye:  Coefficient correct. Units mismatch? Recalculating...
"TARD-E Unit"::  Noncompliance confirmed. Initiating restraint protocol.
Mornye:  Conclusion: material upgrade required. I'll add it to the agenda for tomorrow's meeting.
Mornye:  Right. Now, time for the scheduled meeting with Rover and Lynae.
Mornye:  I'm sorry. Did I keep you waiting?
Lynae:  Ah, haha! Not at all. Actually, you noticed us right as the clock struck the hour. Perfect timing, Professor.
[Dialogue Option]  Are you all right?
Mornye:  I’m fine.
[Dialogue Option]  Is the robot going to be okay?
Mornye:  Just a minor short circuit. It triggered a restraint protocol. I assumed it was malfunctioning.
Mornye:  Oh... I forgot to disable the reactor emitter in my weapon system. That's probably what it was referring to...
Mornye:  Apologies. After this meeting, I need to return to the Spacetrek Collective for a presentation. I had hoped to finish some calculations first.
[Dialogue Option]  If that’s the case, let’s begin now.
Mornye:  I do have other appointments today, but... I believe there is time for some light conversation.
Mornye:  I wasn't sure what you meant by "delicious," so I brought samples from my latest food research.
Abby:  YESSS! I knew it! Professor Mornye's a real gem!
Abby:  Let's get started! We can eat while we talk!
Lynae:  Of course, come on in. I already tidied up my dorm, so sit wherever you like!

title: Ode to the Second Sunrise
subsection: Head to the Academy Dormitory at 09 : 00 the next day
content:
Abby:  Let's get started! We can eat while we talk!
Lynae:  Of course, come on in. I already tidied up my dorm, so sit wherever you like!



Abby:  Ugh... the smells are all mixing together. It's kinda fishy, and the texture is wet and gooey.
Lynae:  So it's true, huh? You guys actually made food that tastes awful but keeps you running for three days straight. I thought that was just a joke.
Mornye:  It's a scientific breakthrough using energy-compression tech. It's one of Collective's most iconic achievements.
Mornye:  Rover, do you... also not like it?
[Dialogue Option]  This is peak science.
Mornye:  Yes! I knew you would understand.
Mornye:  In fact, its energy compression efficiency exceeds 95%. That exceeds the benchmarks set by both the New Federation and Huaxu Academy, even nearing the theoretical limit.
Mornye:  From a scientific standpoint, it's a far greater achievement than taste.
[Dialogue Option]  If this is what progress tastes like, I want to go back.
Mornye:  I... see...
Mornye:  I'll... raise the priority level of flavor optimization for the next iteration.
Mornye:  Now, I'd like to review the incident with the Hyvatia Detector.
Mornye:  Lynae, Rover, can you walk me through exactly how you managed to contain it?
[Dialogue Option]  (Describe how you contained the Hyvatia incident)
Mornye:  To summarize, your method of stopping the Hyvatia included blade slashes, repeated shots with coated rounds, and physical force—stomping, striking—until it was rendered inoperable and immobile.
Mornye:  Did I miss anything?
Lynae:  Uh... Professor Mornye, you're not here to...
[Dialogue Option]  …Make us pay for it, are you?
Lynae:  I mean, it all happened really fast! We didn't have any other way to stop it!
Lynae:  Besides, we're just students! We couldn't afford that even if we wanted to...
Mornye:  No. You're misunderstanding.
Mornye:  Different damage mechanisms cause distinct failures, and require specific repair methods.
Mornye:  Damage from certain special Resonance abilities is hard to detect through standard diagnostics without prior data. So, you two did well to suppress it physically.
Mornye:  During the , the Hyvatia Detector is essential in monitoring environmental parameters. I've already passed your report to Professor Anslem. He should complete repairs soon.
Mornye:  At the upcoming meeting with the Roya, the Spacetrek Collective will need to present a full restoration plan to keep our partnership intact.
[Dialogue Option]  There's a third party involved in this “New Solar Ceremony”?
Mornye:  Yes, though it's a long story. Where do I even begin...
"TARD-E Unit"::  SCANNING FOR OFFENDERS! VIOLATION DETECTED: Unauthorized high-wattage device in the dormitory. An offender has assaulted this unit. If sighted, report immediately!
Lynae:  Pfft... Even Professor Mornye isn't safe from TARD-E's wrath, huh?
Lynae:  No worries, I got this. I'll draw its attention while you two make for it.
Lynae:  Three, two, one—
[Dialogue Option]  That’s our cue.
Mornye:  Mm.

title: Ode to the Second Sunrise
content:
[Objective: (Idle dialogue)]
Lynae:  Hey, TARD-E. How much power do you run on?
“TARD-E Unit”:  Standard output: 200 units. Compliant with dormitory safety protocols.
Lynae:  Uh-huh. And when you’re chasing down a student?
“TARD-E Unit”:  To ensure the successful apprehension of a rule-breaking student, my output increases to 1,200 units.
Lynae:  I guess that makes you the high-wattage device.

title: Ode to the Second Sunrise
content:
Lynae:  I guess that makes you the high-wattage device.



Mornye:  Thank you. You don't need to go any further. I can head back to the Research Institute by myself.
[Dialogue Option]  Stay safe.
Mornye:  Mm, you too.
[Dialogue Option]  No more rule-breaking, alright?
Mornye:  That was... an accident...
Mornye:  Huh?
Rover: Something wrong?
Mornye:  It's a notice from the Collective. The Royan delegation canceled the meeting. The ceremony is now on hold. That's odd...
Mornye:  Warren handles Royan communications. I'll ask him what's going on when I'm back at the Institute.
Mornye:  Since that slot is free now, I can use the time to recalibrate...
[Dialogue Option]  What don't you give yourself a little break?
Mornye: Hm, that isn't on the list.
Mornye: The New Solar Ceremony is nearly upon us. It's the culmination of decades of work. Everyone at the Collective is giving their all to realize it.
Mornye:  Last time we met at the Institute, I... we made each other a promise. Do you still remember?
[Dialogue Option] I remember.
Mornye: Would you like to attend the New Solar Ceremony?
Mornye: I… I'd want you there to witness it. The rise of the new sun, and humanity taking their first steps into the future they've built with their own hands.
Mornye (Flashback): Would you like to attend the New Solar Ceremony?
Mornye (Flashback): I… I'd want you there to witness it. The rise of the new sun, and humanity taking their first steps into the future they've built with their own hands.
Rover: We did promise to witness it together, didn’t we?
Mornye:  Yes.
[Dialogue Option]  A promise?
Mornye:  That's all right. Consider this my official invitation, then.
Mornye:  I hope to attend the ceremony together with you.
Mornye:  As the ceremony draws near, the Spacetrek Collective will become increasingly occupied. Opportunities to meet like this will be rare. But this promise will still stand.
[Dialogue Option]  Then it’s a promise.
???: Before my power is spent, I have little time left.
???: The only choice now is to force the Heliogyre to a standstill.
???: The last of its strength I will share with you, so fade you will not. But you must hurry.
???: Before that, take this memory to him.
???: Take it to the one they call "Arbiter."
Mornye:  Rover, what happened? Are you alright?!
Rover: I... saw someone's memory.
Abby:  Whoa, you scared me! And just now, a frequency jumped into your Tacet Mark! It felt like... some kinda connection?
Rover: Can you trace where it came from, Abby?
Abby:  Sniff, sniff, sniff...
Abby:  I smell it coming from over there!
Rover: Good. Let's go check it out.

title: Ode to the Second Sunrise
subsection: Trace the frequency back to its source
content:
[Objective: Trace the frequency back to its source]
Rover: I'm fine now, Mornye. Sorry to worry you. You must need to get back to the Spacetrek Collective, right?
Mornye:  That's okay.
Rover: But you just...
Mornye:  You looked... shaken just now. I'll stay with you. If it involves more frequency loss, I'd like to stay close to transport you to the infirmary.
Rover: Transport me?

metadata.subsection: Trace the frequency back to its source

title: Ode to the Second Sunrise
content:
[Objective: Talk to Fjnora and Svanar]
Fjnora: You saw it too? It went in this direction.
Svanar: Yes. Strange though. Why here?
[Dialogue Option]  What are you two looking for?
Svanar: Oh, you must be from Startorch Academy. Have you seen a Soliskin? White. About the size of a pumpkin.
[Dialogue Option]  Can’t say I have.
Fjnora: Actually, we did see one flying this way while we were setting up at the market. IfSvanar hadn’t seen it too, I would’ve thought I was imagining it.
Fjnora: If you happen to spot it, please tell us.

title: Ode to the Second Sunrise
content:
Fjnora: If you happen to spot it, please tell us.



Abby: Hmm... the frequency that connected with you was coming from here. But now, I don't smell a thing.
Rover: (The voice from earlier said it would share the last of the Heliogyre's strength so it wouldn't fade. It must be that Soliskin. Did it eventually vanish here?)
Mornye: Did you find what you're looking for?
Rover: No. The trail ends here. But I saw other things in that memory.
[Dialogue Option]  Mornye, do you know of a “Heliogyre”?

Mornye: The "" is one of the most important components of the New Solar Ceremony.

title: Ode to the Second Sunrise
content:
[Dialogue Option]  Mornye, do you know of a “Heliogyre”?

Mornye: The "" is one of the most important components of the New Solar Ceremony.



Mornye: Hyvatia can monitor environmental data, but raw observational data on the Reactor Drive can only be obtained from the Heliogyre—a component of the Exostrider itself.
Mornye: Only the Roya tribe can discern the Heliogyre's readings. That's why the Collective needs their cooperation during the New Solar Ceremony.
Rover: In that memory, I heard a voice say he would force the Heliogyre to a standstill.
Mornye: A standstill?
[Dialogue Option]  (Describe what you saw to Mornye)
Mornye: You're saying you heard a voice asking for help, saying he would stop the Heliogyre's workings.
Mornye: Could that be why the meeting was cancelled?
Rover: (When I handled the Voidworm, a voice told me to protect the sun. Whoever she is, I don't think she intends harm. She offered to help. For now, I'll do what she suggested.)
Rover: (And one thing is certain. The one who knows me by my "Arbiter" title needs my help.)
Rover: (Hm. Yet another problem tied to the Research Institute. We shouldn't reveal our plans to them just yet.)
[Dialogue Option]  (Black robes with golden embroidery…—)
[Dialogue Option]  (A headpiece shaped like two horns…)
[Dialogue Option]  (And those unusual eyes…)
Rover: I need to find out who he is, Mornye. Do you know any Roya who are familiar with the tribe's inner workings?
Mornye: Hmm... I do have some Royan students. They might know who he is.
Mornye: It's class hours at the Academy. Should we head back?
Ovid: Help! Help! Maja—Maja, she... Someone, please help!
Ovid: Otherwise, our thesis data will disappear entirely!
Mornye: Don't worry, Rover. If you see a student shouting "help" and "thesis" in the same breath, no matter how loudly they scream, it's never really an emergency.
Mornye: But Maja is one of the Roya students I mentioned. Since you're looking for her, we might as well see what it's about.

title: Ode to the Second Sunrise
content:
Mornye: But Maja is one of the Roya students I mentioned. Since you're looking for her, we might as well see what it's about.



Maja: Calm down, Maja, calm down... Good, they've stopped for now. Maybe I should just shut them down?
Maja: No, if I force the shutdown, I'll lose the data. Our thesis! Oh, somebody help!!
Mornye:  Ugh...
[Dialogue Option]  Is she in a bad situation?
Mornye:  No. It's just a routine malfunction. But...
Maja: Huh? Professor Mornye?!
Maja: Oh no, I've been caught out of class! Wait, wait, let me explain! I wasn't skipping class! I'm here for a very good reason! It's not that I don't respect the class, o-or my teachers!
Maja: So, uh... can you just...
Mornye:  Even if you beg me, credits will still be deducted.
Mornye:  Why don't you start by explaining yourself?
Maja: Well, these are probe robots from a few days ago. We sent them out to measure Voidmatter concentrations in the tundra.
Maja: We thought we'd finish collecting the data before class, but when we tried to approach them, they started attacking us.
Maja: I chased them all the way here. That's why I missed the class today...
Mornye:  The internal  was eroded by Voidmatter. That's what caused the malfunction.
Mornye: This should have been covered in your Material Science coursework. Such material is inherently unstable and can only be used in controlled environments.
Maja: I'm so sorry...
Mornye:  For safety reasons, you'll need to shut down the units first, then clean the contaminated parts with Voidmatter.
Mornye:  But approaching them right now may lead to further damage. We need a pulse generator to stun them from a distance. I'll submit a request.
[Dialogue Option]  There’s a simpler solution.
[Dialogue Option]  (Unsheathe your sword.)
Mornye:  No wait, that's against protocol...
Probe Robots: ￥#&@... Scanning... Target... Eradication...
Mornye:  Never mind. I'll think about how to write the review report later.

title: Ode to the Second Sunrise
content:
[Objective: Defeat the malfunctioning probe robots]
Mornye:  Now, they're back to normal.
Maja: Great! Do you think the data...
Mornye:  It's still there.
Mornye:  But sending the robots out there broke the experiment protocol. Even if you got the data, it won't count in your thesis.
Maja: What?!
Maja: But... Oh, well. Thanks anyway for helping out. Professor Mornye, and—
[Dialogue Option]  You can call me Rover.
Mornye:  Maja, we do have something we'd like to ask you.
[Dialogue Option]  (Describe the vision you saw.)
Maja: You want to find a Roya in black robes with gold embroidery, wearing a headpiece shaped like two horns?
Maja: The horns are a symbol of the Exostrider.  wear them, but no Shepherd would wear a robe like that...
Maja: Could be someone higher up. Like the  from the Solisylum, or even one of .
Mornye:  The Heliodic Six... They're the ones who are supposed to give us the Heliogyre's readings during the New Solar Ceremony.
Maja: That's right. They're the six most powerful members of the Roya tribe. The highest in rank, too.
Maja: I've heard they use the Heliogyre to predict everything, from bird migrations to Void Storms. They know it all.
Rover: How do I meet with one of them?
Maja: Huh?! That might be hard.
Maja: They never leave the Solisylum. It's surrounded by light all year round. Very few Roya are even allowed to enter.
Maja: But maybe you could try meeting with one of the unappointed Heliodic Six?
Maja: Sigrika is currently out researching in the frostlands. The only other one around is Foreseer Yngvar, but he doesn't show himself much.
Maja: If you want to find him, my mam might be able to help. She's a Royan Shepherdess over at Atuja camp. Name's Astrid.
Maja: Now then, I'd better get back to my class before I lose all my credits. Who knew I'd run into trouble today? I even asked my mam to help me with the robot.
Mornye:  Very good. Good luck with your thesis paper.
Mornye:  Phew... I'm better at talking with students in class.
Mornye:  Rover, did you learn what you needed?
Rover: The last person that those robots likely saw before they lost control was Maja's mother.
Rover: I think we can talk to her under the guise of a friendly house visit.
Mornye:  Hmm... In that case, I can accompany you as a Professor from the Academy. As for your identity, Rover...
Mornye:  It's okay. It will simply be a convenient title.
[Dialogue Option]  Mornye?
Mornye:  Would it be okay for you to act as... my mentor?
[Dialogue Option]  You mean, act as a Professor too? Sure.
Rover: But aren't you going to tell me I should report this to the Academy to handle?
Mornye:  I was just thinking of ways to help you find who you're looking for.
Mornye:  Your reasons are your own. I trust your judgement, and you can tell me later.
[Dialogue Option]  I hope I act the part of Professor well.
[Dialogue Option]  Feel free to give me pointers, Junior Professor.
Mornye:  Yes, feel free to give me pointers too, Mentor.
Mornye:  I think the person I am now... can be of help to you.

title: Ode to the Second Sunrise
content:
[Objective: Head to Atuja Camp]
Mornye:  I'm Mornye, and this is my mentor... Uh, let me try that again...
Rover: What are you...?
Mornye:  Just practicing. I'm not very good at speaking with parents. And this time, I don't have an assistant to help write a script for me.
Rover: Why don't you leave it to me? You just focus on what you're good at.
Mornye:  Alright.
Mornye:  Ready to go to Atuja camp to find Astrid?
[Dialogue Option]  Let’s go.
Mornye:  Okay, let's go together... Mentor.
[Dialogue Option]  Let’s go a bit later.

title: Ode to the Second Sunrise
content:
[Dialogue Option]  Let’s go.
Mornye:  Okay, let's go together... Mentor.
[Dialogue Option]  Let’s go a bit later.



Resident: Chuuu...
Rover: Hi, are you Astrid, Maja's mom?
Astrid: Hm? Greetings. Yes, I am. And you two are?
[Dialogue Option]  This is Professor Mornye, Maja’s teacher.
Mornye: Yes, and this is Rover, a senior professor at the Academy.
Mornye: We've come for a home visit.
Astrid: A home visit...? Has the girl broken any school rules?
[Dialogue Option]  Yes. She severely violated the experiment protocol.
[Dialogue Option]  She created a robot that caused significant damage to the Academy.
Astrid: What?! H-How could she...
Astrid: I am deeply sorry! I should have taught her better. Whatever she has done, I offer my apologies to the Academy on her behalf.
Astrid: Is the punishment severe? If compensation is needed, I will pay for it myself—
[Dialogue Option]  No compensation is necessary.
[Dialogue Option]  But we’ll need your cooperation in the handling of this case.
Rover: Professor Mornye, could you explain how Maja's robot caused the damage?
Mornye: Y-yes, as my mentor just explained...
Mornye: She... failed to follow the proper protocol. She used unstable Exoswarm material in her design, which led the robot to act unpredictably.
Mornye: I've already spoken to her about the dangers of using materials susceptible to Voidmatter during field research.
Astrid: Voidmatter?
Astrid: What... exactly are you asking? I am sorry, I've not studied at your Startorch Academy. I'm not familiar with your terms.
Rover: (Her demeanor changed just now. She's hiding something. Maybe more pressure.)
Rover: We need to understand the full scope of the robot's malfunction. We understand that this morning, it was you who helped Maja activate the robots and enable auto-run.
Mornye: Yes. Exactly what my mentor said.
Mornye: Please, lead us to the site of the incident. Once we're there, I'll reconstruct the robots' actions from the trace evidence.
Astrid: N-No. We can't. If the robots' path is traced, it will expose that thing—
[Dialogue Option]  “That thing”?
[Dialogue Option]  What are you hiding?
Astrid: I am deeply sorry! Yes, help Maja activate the robots I did, but I... I can't remember the exact location. Please, you must return—
Mornye: That's a Void Storm. How can this be? The Collective hasn't received any recent warnings.
Rover: We need to ensure the safety of those here first.
Rover: Questions can wait. Let's go.

title: Ode to the Second Sunrise
content:
[Objective: Head to the Shimmer]
Mornye: That looks like the center of the storm ahead. Let's see what we're dealing with.

title: Ode to the Second Sunrise
content:
Shocked Roya: Am I seeing things? Is that… a Void Storm? But the Solisylum did not sound the alarm!
Shocked Roya: Could the Solisylum’s predictions of the Void Storm be wrong?
Anxious Roya: Impossible! The predictions of the Heliodic Six are never wrong! We must have missed the warning!
Anxious Roya: Wait, I remember now! Astrid just returned from Bjartr Woods! As a Shepherdess, she must know more. We will go ask her!
Shocked Roya: Yes. Let us hope she simply forgot to tell the rest of us…
Scared Roya: Are you alright?!
Injured Roya: It’s nothing. It was but a moment in the Void Storm. Some components of the Exoswarm I carry… it was some protection.
Injured Roya: See? Still flesh and blood. I have not faded into a frequency…
Scared Roya: Frightful for a Void Storm to strike so suddenly…
Scared Roya: I remember, the healers at Startorch Academy can check for frequency sickness! It is not far. We should go there now!

title: Ode to the Second Sunrise
content:
Scared Roya: I remember, the healers at Startorch Academy can check for frequency sickness! It is not far. We should go there now!



Mornye: We're in the Void Storm's range now. Check that your FCR is working.
Mornye: Don't stray too far from me.

title: Ode to the Second Sunrise
content:
[Objective: Defeat the contaminated Exoswarm]
Mornye: Be careful. The Exoswarm here have been contaminated.
Mornye: There's something over there…

title: Ode to the Second Sunrise
content:
[Objective: (Investigate the Voidmatter contamination)]
Rover: Down here. It’s some kind of weird device.
Mornye: A device? Leave the mechanical work to me. Steady now.

Mornye: Looks like it was this.

Unsettling Device
image
A device found in the eye of a Void Storm, emitting an unsettling aura. It seems linked to the probe robots’ malfunction.

title: Ode to the Second Sunrise
content:
Unsettling Device
image
A device found in the eye of a Void Storm, emitting an unsettling aura. It seems linked to the probe robots’ malfunction.



Mornye: With this shut down, the Void Storm is gone.
[Dialogue Option]  Was that one of your Resonance Abilities?
Mornye: Eh? No, I–I just read a lot about this...
Mornye: From its structure, it looks like a canister that can both store and emit energy.
Abby: Ugh, it's so stinky!
Abby: It smells just like that giant worm you fought! Didn't we deal with it already?!
Mornye: Giant worm... You mean the ?
Mornye: I see. It's capturing frequencies with high precision, storing energy data.
Mornye: It's based on ecological models, tracking activity in natural environments, and reconstructing that data mathematically.
Mornye: A field modulator, parametric projection...
[Dialogue Option]  ???
Mornye: Oh, sorry.
[Dialogue Option]  Can you try a version that I can understand?
[Dialogue Option]  Explain it so Abby understands.
Mornye: Right. Simply put, this device extracted the Voidworm's frequency and used itself as the epicenter to spread Voidmatter. That storm just now was artificially created.
Mornye: Maja's probe got contaminated because they likely made contact with it by accident.
Abby: Eh? Did you guys just hear something?
???: Chuuu… Chuuuu…
Mornye: It's coming from under that heap of Exoswarm material. Let's go take a look.

title: Ode to the Second Sunrise
subsection: Find where the "Chuu" noises are coming from
content:
[Objective: Find where the "Chuu" noises are coming from]
Mornye: It's a .
[Dialogue Option]  So this is what they look like.
Mornye: Yes, these special creatures typically linger around the Roya tribe.
[Dialogue Option]  I’ve seen one of these before.
Mornye: You've seen one? So you've done some exploring already.
Mornye: Royan records state that Soliskin first appeared in Lahai-Roi the day the Exostrider fell from the sky.
Mornye: They're believed to be fragments of the Exostrider's consciousness. The Shephards protect them, shielding them from Void Storm contamination until they mature and return to the Solistrees in Bjartr Woods.
Mornye: This one must have hidden under the Exoswarm wreckage when the Void Storm broke out.
Soliskin: Chuuu…
Rover: (This... feels like what happened back at the Academy.)
Rover: I just saw this Soliskin's memories.
Rover: That Royan woman planted the device here and triggered the Void Storm. This Soliskin is the only survivor.
Mornye: So our suspicions about Astrid are confirmed. Should we go back to the camp and talk to her?
Astrid: No need. I heard everything.
Astrid: I did place this device here.
[Dialogue Option]  Tell us what happened.
Astrid: A few days ago, I was shepherding mature Soliskin to  when I met Foreseer Yngvar.
Astrid: He looked tired, like he had just finished speaking to someone. When he saw me, he looked shocked and left quickly.
Astrid: I saw the device fall from his sleeve.
[Dialogue Option]  Why did you take it?
Astrid: I did not think much of it. I planned to return it to him the next time we meet.
Astrid: But... the Soliskin did not like it. It had an... unnatural energy.
Astrid: I did not want to keep it at the camp, but I also did not want Yngvar to know I had taken it.
Astrid: So I buried it here. The rest, you already know.
Mornye: So, this device is Foreseer Yngvar's. Mentor, what do you make of this?
[Dialogue Option]  She doesn’t seem to be lying.
[Dialogue Option]  We need to verify this ourselves.
Mornye: Hmm... I trust your judgement.
Mornye: This Foreseer Yngvar is the one Maja mentioned before, the unappointed member of the Heliodic Six. Could it be an attempt to tighten his grip on power?
Astrid: No. That is impossible.
Astrid: Each of these successors (the Solsworn) is chosen when their Resonance Ability first awakens. Even if someone desired the position, it is impossible to change the appointment.
Mornye: Hmm... meaning no one can threaten Yngvar's position.
Rover: (But he could harbor animosity toward the current Heliodic Six. Yngvar is still our lead to find them.)
Rover: (Things are getting more complicated. A direct approach with Yngvar might not be a good idea.)
[Dialogue Option]  Where can we find him?
Astrid: The Solisylum's people usually abide in the village bordering Bjartr Woods, called Haldarheim.
Astrid: It is the time of the . The Soliskin will return to the Solistrees and to the Exostrider. As is tradition, Foreseer Yngvar will attend the rite.
Astrid: But you are not Roya. You may not be allowed to witness the rite.
Soliskin: Uuu...
Mornye: Huh? Wait, but we did find this little one here.
Astrid: Is this the Soliskin you saved? Well... Perhaps you may attend as "Shepherds."
Astrid: Soliskin have been companions to the Roya for hundreds of years. If they hear that you saved one, they will be grateful.
Soliskin: Chu... Chuuu!
[Dialogue Option]  We’re in this together now.
Mornye: I've never been this close to a Soliskin before. Please let me know if I'm doing something wrong.

metadata.subsection: Find where the "Chuu" noises are coming from

title: Ode to the Second Sunrise
content:
[Objective: Talk to Mornye]
Mornye: So we need to find Foreseer Yngvar at Haldarheim's Rite of Return, is that right?
Mornye: Do you want to leave now?
[Dialogue Option]  Let’s go.
[Dialogue Option]  I still have something to attend to first.
Mornye: Okay, let's be on our way then.
[Dialogue Option]  I still have something to attend to first.

title: Ode to the Second Sunrise
subsection: Head to the entrance to Haldarheim
content:
[Objective: Head to the entrance to Haldarheim]
Aksel: You two. Please halt.
Aksel: From your clothing, I see of my people you are not. What brings you to Haldarheim?
Aksel: Oh? A Soliskin...
[Dialogue Option]  We are shepherding it home.
Soliskin: Chuuu! Chuuu!
Aksel: Heh. How interesting... Soliskin trust only those they feel safe with. Its trust you have earned. My thanks for guiding it back.
Aksel: But I must ask, I sense one of you carries the aura of the Spacetrek Collective. The other, from the vast world beyond the frostlands. Why come under the guise of Shepherds?
Rover: (Not sure who here knows what Yngvar did. Best not to mention his name. Don't want to stir things up.)
Rover: We rescued this Soliskin from a Void Storm. We were told it needed to return here for the Rite of Return.
Aksel: Void Storm? You mean, the one just before?
Aksel: Haha! Then grateful I must be to you both!
Aksel: But ask I must—the Void Storm, it happened near Atuja camp, yes?
Aksel: A Shepherdess named Astrid abides there. Saved the stray Soliskin you did, yet entrust it to a true Shepherdess you did not. Why come all this way?
Rover: (I forgot about that. Without a solid reason, he might start to suspect something.)
Mornye: Because... Astrid has been hiding something from you.
Aksel: Your meaning?
Mornye: Astrid's daughter, Maja, is a student at Startorch Academy. She conducted experiments that broke protocol and caused damage to school property.
Mornye: Maja is now facing harsh punishment. Astrid is busy handling the consequences and cannot fulfill her duties as a Shepherdess.
Mornye: According to the Startorch Academy Faculty Code, as Maja's teachers, it is our duty to address the repercussions of a student's actions.
Mornye: Since Astrid can't shepherd this Soliskin, we must step in to do so ourselves.
[Dialogue Option]  Exactly what Professor Mornye said.
Aksel: I should have known Astrid's daughter would stir such trouble! A tangled weave this time, but she will go to great lengths for her girl.
Aksel: The Academy's willingness to come this far is unexpected. Forgive my earlier words. You saved the Soliskin and helped our people. The title of "Shepherd," you have earned.
Aksel: Tonight, we hold a feast for tomorrow's . Join us, as a gesture to make amends for my earlier rudeness.
Aksel: Come. From this day forth, the Roya call you friends.
Aksel: Rest at the camp if you wish. The feast will begin at the eighth hour of the night.

metadata.subsection: Head to the entrance to Haldarheim

title: Ode to the Second Sunrise
subsection: Join the feast held before the Rite of Return at 20 : 00
content:
[Objective: Join the feast held before the Rite of Return at 20 : 00]
Oh, guest from afar… You carry an aura not unlike that of the Soliskin.

Is it true that you come from the "World Above"? What is it like there?
Joachim! Don't nose around in another's business...

Where is Foreseer Yngvar? Isn’t he the Eye’s successor?
Hush… That is not something we should speak of.

Rover: (There's still some time before the feast begins. Maybe someone here knows something about Foreseer Yngvar.)

title: Ode to the Second Sunrise
subsection: Inquire about Foreseer Yngvar’s whereabouts in the village
content:
[Objective: Inquire about Foreseer Yngvar’s whereabouts in the village]
Layla: You made an error. If we follow your calculations, the Reactor Drive’s rotation angle stands at four point zero six thousandths of a turn.
Sander: No, no, no! It is you who is mistaken. I’ve recalculated it eight times, and it is four point zero eight thousandths of a turn!
[Dialogue Option]  Excuse me. Have you seen Foreseer Yngvar around?
Sander: Foreseer Yngvar? Ha! We’d have no chance of such a meeting.
Sander: In the history of the Heliodic Six, those like Yngvar seldom walk among us. If you seek him, your best hope lies in the Rite of Return on the morrow.
Sander: Ah, I still remember how the current “Eye” joined us in such spirited debates of umbers before taking her seat. Mmm, she would.
Sander: If she were here now, she would agree that…
Layla: She would agree that it is four point zero six thousandths.
Sander: No, it is four point zero eight thousandths!

metadata.subsection: Inquire about Foreseer Yngvar’s whereabouts in the village

title: Ode to the Second Sunrise
subsection: Inquire about Foreseer Yngvar’s whereabouts in the village
content:
[Objective: Inquire about Foreseer Yngvar’s whereabouts in the village]
Tove: It’s time to part, Marigold…
Marigold: Chuuu…
Tove: Foreseer Yngvar… Yes, with the Rite of Return on the morrow, we will likely meet him.
Tove: Truth be told, the Soliskin do not favor him much. We Shepherds have little contact with him.
Marigold: Chuuu-um.
Tove: Though as one of the successors to the Heliodic Six, his standing is not for us to question.
Tove: Still, I would hope that the future Heliodic Six is one favored by the Soliskin… someone like Sigrika, perhaps.

metadata.subsection: Inquire about Foreseer Yngvar’s whereabouts in the village

title: Ode to the Second Sunrise
subsection: Inquire about Foreseer Yngvar’s whereabouts in the village
content:
[Objective: Inquire about Foreseer Yngvar’s whereabouts in the village]
Herja: The feast tonight brings new faces. Seems we’ll need to prepare enough for two more…
Herja: Yngvar? That boy doesn’t come round here anymore.
Herja: I will speak the truth. After his parents were caught in a Void Storm when he was a boy, ‘twas Aksel and I who raised him.
Herja: A quiet child was he. Few were his friends. When his Resonance Ability was discovered and the Heliodic Six chose him as a successor, he was overjoyed. “No longer will the other children pick on me,” he said.
Herja: But somewhere along the way, he changed. No longer did he wish to take the mantle of the Six. He grew distant, with nary a visit home.
Herja: Ah, well… Even if it’s but for a meal, it warms the hearth when he returns.
