title: Ode to the Second Sunrise
content:
[Objective: Head to the feast]
Aksel: Friends—it is time we feast!
Aksel: Tomorrow marks the Rite of Return, where we send our beloved Soliskin back to the great body of the Exostrider. Into radiant light they will transform to join its sacred form.
Aksel: Farewell it will be, yet a new beginning as well! For when the Exostrider wakes, we will reunite in its body!
Aksel: Now, let us put aside the sorrow of parting and embrace the joy of new life with good food and drink!
Aksel: But heed this, my friends. Too much drink you will not have. Should you make a fool of yourself in tomorrow's Rite, help I will not give.
[Dialogue Option]  What is it? Are you feeling nervous?
Mornye: We will face Foreseer Yngvar tomorrow.
Mornye: I've simulated seventy-three possible outcomes, but even so, I can't cover every scenario.
Mornye: If I could build a model that covers all possible outcomes, considering the target system, the chaotic conditions, and the necessary compensations...
Rover: You were quick on your feet earlier. You've already got this.
Mornye: That's because I believed your approach was effective. I tried to follow along.
Mornye: Did I really do well?
[Dialogue Option]  Of course. Give yourself more credit.
Mornye: Good. Phew...
[Dialogue Option]  Yes. Keep practicing and it’ll come more easily.
Mornye: Understood. I'll make sure to do better next time.
Rover: With that in mind, you can relax a bit now, right?
Soliskin: Chuuu! Chuuu-chuuu!
[Dialogue Option]  What’s this cutie trying to say?
Abby: Ah, I know! It wants us to give it a name.
Mornye: Well, since it's really trying to buddy up to us, how about we call it "Buddy"?
Abby: Oh? It seems to like it.
Rover: Then it's settled.
Mornye: Well... that's a relief.
Dagna: Hello, will you dance with us and the Soliskin?
Stian: Grandfather Aksel says the Soliskin are happiest when dancing with Shepherds!
Mornye: Oh, but I'm not good at dancing.
Rover: I'll join you. Let's dance with Buddy. What do you say?
Children: HOORAY!
Rover: Our real battle starts tomorrow.
Rover: Tonight, let's relax a little, Mornye.
Mornye: Yes. My mentor should take his} own advice, too.
Distressed Soliskin: Chu... Chu... Uuuugh...
???: Hmph...
???: Some uninvited guests have arrived.

title: Ode to the Second Sunrise
content:
Distressed Soliskin: Chu... Chu... Uuuugh...
???: Hmph...
???: Some uninvited guests have arrived.



To Sol, the first to have brought the stars to our ancestors during the First Epoch.
To the Exostrider, who gave us light and warmth in the Second Epoch.

Rover: Hmm. Where did Mornye go? I'll send her a message (WavesLine).

title: Ode to the Second Sunrise
content:
To the Exostrider, who gave us light and warmth in the Second Epoch.

Rover: Hmm. Where did Mornye go? I'll send her a message (WavesLine).



[Choice]  Mornye, where are you?
(Rover): Mornye, where are you?
Mornye: Has the feast finished already?
[Choice]  Yes, it has.
(Rover): Yes, it is.
Mornye: I'm sorry if I worried you.
[Choice]  I couldn't find you. I was worried.
(Rover): I couldn't find you. I was worried.
Mornye: But... I'm the professor, and you're the student. It should be my place to worry about you.
(Rover): I thought I was your mentor?
Mornye: ...I see. Sorry to make you worry.
Mornye: (Attachment: a picture of the night sky)
Mornye:
Mornye: I'm here. Right beneath the 13th planet of the Norma constellation.
Mornye: I'm afraid I'm unable to move at the moment. Please, I'll need you to come find me here.}}

title: Ode to the Second Sunrise
Ode to the Second Sunrise
content:
[Objective: Find Mornye]
Mornye: Mentor?
Rover: We can drop the act now, right? Or do you think we should continue?
Mornye: Someone might be listening. We should keep it up to prevent us from being exposed.
Mornye: Do you... want to sit for a while?
[Dialogue Option]  How're your legs holding up?
Mornye: Oh, you noticed.
Mornye: They've been running all day, so their power is low. I planned to wait until they finished charging before coming back.
Mornye: While they charge, I can't move. I feel a bit, er... embarrassed having you see me like this.
[Dialogue Option]  Does it hurt?
Mornye: It doesn't anymore.
Mornye: Before I had prosthetic legs, I had a condition that kept me in a wheelchair.
Mornye: Now, at least I don't have to worry about being immobile anymore.
Mornye: I can finally chase after what I really want.
[Dialogue Option]  The stars here are beautiful.
Mornye: Mm, I love stars.
Mornye: Beneath Lahai-Roi's frostlands, the stars here are actually just lights created by atmospheric arrays.
Mornye: Once, someone put it like this to me...
Mornye: "It's because we see the stars that humanity imagines what lies beyond the sky."
Mornye: "Maybe the stars are humanity's muse."
[Dialogue Option]  An interesting way to put it.
[Dialogue Option]  That’s a romantic image.
Mornye: I think so too.
Mornye: But... I also believe that reaching the stars isn't enough.
Mornye: There will be a day we build a miracle that lasts longer and is more beautiful than the stars themselves.
Mornye: That's the dream I've carried all this time. And now, I'll use these two legs to take the first step.
[Dialogue Option]  For that to come true…
[Dialogue Option]  The New Solar Ceremony must succeed, right?
Mornye: Exactly! This ceremony is how we retrieve the Exostrider's core energy component.
Mornye: Then we'll use the multiphasic energy conversion model through the superconducting network to inject Rabelle energy into the neural interface.
Mornye: It will follow a three-stage activation protocol. The reverse-phase oscillation model, then excavation to finally create a phased-array energy field.
Mornye: There's still some time before my legs finish charging. Let's stargaze a little longer.

title: Ode to the Second Sunrise
content:
Mornye: There's still some time before my legs finish charging. Let's stargaze a little longer.



Buddy: Chu, Chuuu! Chuuu! Chuuu!
Mornye: Okay, little Buddy. I'll wake him up now.
[Dialogue Option]  …Mornye?
Mornye: Mentor, you're awake!
Mornye: Something isn't right. We seem to have a situation in Bjartr Woods.

title: Ode to the Second Sunrise
content:
[Objective: Investigate Bjartr Woods]
Mornye: I detect signs of a Void Storm in the woods. Waveform... analyzing now.
Rover: So this is what's causing the panic.
Tove: But the Soliskin… many have already entered Bjartr Woods!
Tove: A Void Storm would… No, I don’t want to think of it!
Herja: Children! Don’t panic, the escape route is this way.
Herja: The Roya have survived worse disasters. Take care of one another, your lives matter more than anything else!

Aksel: What is it that brings you here? With the Void Storm's fury upon us, it is no time to enter Bjartr Woods.
Aksel: This is a disaster not seen in centuries. We have always believed the  light protects the woods from such storms.
Aksel: The Rite of Return cannot be done, not in these times. I urge you both to head to safety, quickly!
[Dialogue Option]  Another Void Storm…
Mornye: Let's investigate this together.

title: Ode to the Second Sunrise
content:
[Dialogue Option]  Another Void Storm…
Mornye: Let's investigate this together.



Mornye: The signature waveform of this Void Storm matches the one that device generated before. This is no naturally occurring phenomenon.
Rover: When did you have the chance to analyze this?
Mornye: When my prosthetic legs charge, I prefer to keep my mind occupied.
Layla: Wh-what’s happening… This isn’t right. Help!
Sander: Be careful! Don’t get caught in the Void Storm!

Mornye: Be careful!
Mornye: I found the device. It’s close to the Solistree.
Rover: Solistree? I have a bad feeling about this.
Mornye: There are so many contaminated Exoswarm here. The Voidmatter concentration is also very high.
Rover: Maybe the device Astrid had was incomplete. This could be the real deal.

title: Ode to the Second Sunrise
subsection: Find out why the Void Storm occurred
content:
[Objective: Find out why the Void Storm occurred]
Mornye: Just like before. When it's disabled, the Void Storm stops.
Mornye: However...
Mornye: If this really was the work of Foreseer Yngvar, what would make him do something like this?
[Dialogue Option]  Who are you?
???: Do not worry. The path... has already been laid.
???: At last... finally...
Mornye: Mentor? Mentor! Are you alright?
Mornye: Did you see something again? It seemed worse than last time.
[Dialogue Option]  I think I saw a glimpse inside Solisylum.
Rover: This Void Storm might not have just affected the woods here, but the workings of Solisylum itself.
Rover: I think that's why I've been seeing visions of this member of the Six.
Elderly Shepherd: Greetings.
Elderly Shepherd: The Shaper once made a prediction. If a visitor from beyond Lahai-Roi protects Bjartr Woods from destruction, an invitation to Solisylum they will receive.
Elderly Shepherd: Now, the one from the prediction appears.  awaits your arrival.
Elder Soliskin: Chuuu...
Buddy: Chu... Chu?
[Dialogue Option]  Buddy?
Elderly Shepherd: They have their own missions to complete.
Elderly Shepherd: The road to Solisylum is here. Please, follow this path.
Mornye: Mentor, please... wait a moment.
Mornye: There's something I want to say to you.
[Dialogue Option]  If you're in any danger, call me.

metadata.subsection: Find out why the Void Storm occurred

title: Ode to the Second Sunrise
subsection: Find out why the Void Storm occurred
content:
Mornye: Mentor, please... wait a moment.
Mornye: There's something I want to say to you.
[Dialogue Option]  If you're in any danger, call me.



Rover: What's the matter, Mornye？
Mornye: I...
Mornye: I really wish I could accompany you to Solisylum. But I think it's best if we part ways here.
[Dialogue Option]  Are you concerned about something?
Mornye: Yes. When you touched the Solistree earlier, and even during your first vision, you looked like you were in intense pain.
Mornye: But I lack the ability to connect with them like you do. And the Spacetrek Collective's knowledge doesn't align with the ways of the Roya. In this matter, I fear... I won't be of much help.
Mornye: Instead of joining you, I think there are other ways I can contribute—such as researching the unknowns we still face.
[Dialogue Option]  Like Yngvar’s true purpose.
[Dialogue Option]  Like the true origins of the Void Storm device.
Mornye: Yes. Yngvar should have been present at the Rite of Return, were it not for that Void Storm. It's reasonable to suspect he's the one who planted the device.
Mornye: Additionally, the environment here is unusual. Investigating these anomalies should help our work here.
[Dialogue Option]  Insightful as always, Professor Mornye.
Mornye: No. You, my mentor, are still far ahead of me.
Mornye: Well then. I guess this is goodbye for now.
[Dialogue Option]  Stay in touch.
Mornye: Please take care. I'll see you when we regroup.

metadata.subsection: Find out why the Void Storm occurred

title: Ode to the Second Sunrise
content:
[Objective: Talk to the elderly Shepherd]
Elderly Shepherd: The road to Solisylum is here. Or do you have something else to ask?
[Dialogue Option]  Ask about the Heliodic Six…
Elderly Shepherd: This history, every Royan child learns from birth—
Elderly Shepherd: "The Exostrider's heart is our sun. It gives us light. Thus, we need not freeze in the eternal night."
Elderly Shepherd: "And the Six, with the Heliogyre as their tally, read the heavens. Thus, we need not fade into the void."
Elderly Shepherd: They are our prophets. They are our sacrifices.
Elderly Shepherd: More than this... that, I believe, they will tell you themselves within Solisylum.
[Dialogue Option]  About the prediction…
Elderly Shepherd: For centuries, the Six have foretold our skies. Never have they been wrong.
Elderly Shepherd: This was the first prediction so... specific. To you, proven as its subject, our people offer our highest welcome.
[Dialogue Option]  Ask about the man in your visions.
Elderly Shepherd: Black robes with golden embroidery, a headpiece shaped like two horns, and unusual eyes... It seems you have met one of the Six.
Elderly Shepherd: The frequency you felt was likely a Soliskin, carrying the message for him. It spent the last of its strength crossing Lahai-Roi to reach you.
Elderly Shepherd: Yet he chose a Soliskin, not one of our own people, to send word...
Elderly Shepherd: Could it be... some turmoil is stirring within the Roya themselves?
[Dialogue Option]  About Yngvar…
Elderly Shepherd: Chosen by the Heliogyre as a Solsworn, he was. That much is certain.
Elderly Shepherd: It is not my place to speak on other matters.
[Dialogue Option]  I have no further questions.
Elderly Shepherd: I see. Then I shall wait here.

title: Ode to the Second Sunrise
content:
[Objective: Head to the Solisylum]
So that’s the one the Heliodic Six predicted would appear…
Solisylum appeared for him too…

Angry Shepherd: Why would Yngvar be chosen as one of the next Heliodic Six?
Angry Shepherd: Yngvar never even bothered to care about the Soliskin. And he never joins the ceremonies. How was he chosen as one of the Heliodic Six's future successors?
Nervous Roya: Let's not talk about this here...
Angry Shepherd: Why is that? Are you afraid? I'm simply stating the facts. Among all the candidates, Sigrika is clearly the one who meets the necessary qualifications!

The Void Storm in Bjartr Woods has stopped.
That must be the hero who stopped the destruction…

Hello, Predicted One
Solisylum has appeared for you. Please, enter.

Shepherd: You may approach.
Shepherd: The Heliodic Six are expecting you, as was predicted.

title: Ode to the Second Sunrise
content:
Solisylum has appeared for you. Please, enter.

Shepherd: You may approach.
Shepherd: The Heliodic Six are expecting you, as was predicted.



Rover: The dim light here—It's like something I saw in those memories.
Rover: From this angle, the faint ring in the center is probably the Heliogyre they put to a halt.
Rover: My Tacet Mark... It's resonanting with this star-like object.
Rover: Seems like I'm able to move it.
Rover: Aligning the pattern on the star with the Heliogyre makes it glow. It's feeding power into it.
Rover: If I channel light from all directions... I should be able to restart the Heliogyre.

title: Ode to the Second Sunrise
content:
[Objective: Inspect the Heliodic Six]
One of the Six, holding the "Binder" seat. He resembles a vessel carved by time itself.
One of the Six, holding the "Eye" seat. She looks as if she hasn't seen the sun in a very long time.
One of the Six, holding the "Recorder" seat. Not a single speck of dust lies upon her robes.
One of the Six, holding the "Refiner" seat. Her closed eyes seem less like rest, and more like a designed state.
One of the Six, holding the "Chronicler" seat. His breath carries a strange chill.

title: Ode to the Second Sunrise
content:
One of the Six, holding the "Chronicler" seat. His breath carries a strange chill.



The Shaper: The Heliogyre has awakened. It seems the Arbiter foretold in the fractured records… is you.
[Dialogue Option]  Have you been the one attempting to reach me?
The Shaper: Yes. With great reverence is your presence here met.
The Shaper: Solisylum, as you see it, is not as it once was. Five of the Six have lost their minds, and the light of the Heliogyre no longer flows.
The Shaper: This is why I summoned you.
[Dialogue Option]  Tell me everything that has happened.
The Shaper: You witnessed the Void Storm in Bjartr Woods, yes?
The Shaper: The  shield the woods from such storms. Yet, through malice and dark intent, corrupted were the roots. And so too, the Heliogyre.
The Shaper: The others succumbed to the corruption. Only I was able to sever my link to the Heliogyre before the corruption could claim me.
The Shaper: With the last of my strength, I turned the six stars to halt the Heliogyre and prevent the corruption’s spread.
The Shaper: That, at least, ensured that when my strength failed and I fell into slumber, untouched by others the Heliogyre would remain.
The Shaper: No one, save for one.
[Dialogue Option]  Me.
The Shaper: Correct.
The Shaper: As one of the Six, I can glimpse the near future within the Heliogyre. But I am bound here, unable to act.
The Shaper: All I could do was send a Soliskin entrusted with my message to you.
Rover: (That Soliskin that vanished just outside the Academy.)
The Shaper: Because of your actions, the source of the corruption was stopped. The stars are now aligned, and the Heliogyre turns once again.
The Shaper: But the other Five are no more. They can no longer fulfill their roles within the Heliodic Six.
The Shaper: I have one final request.
The Shaper: But before that, allow me to tell you what the Heliodic Six truly are.

title: Ode to the Second Sunrise
content:
The Shaper: I have one final request.
The Shaper: But before that, allow me to tell you what the Heliodic Six truly are.



(Cutscene plays)
Centuries ago
a Calamity awoke beneath the ice
The void devoured all
erasing every trace, every existence
In darkness, the Exostrider’s blade
sealed the threat deep below
It drew its fiery Drive
a light that would never fade
lifting it high over Lahai-Roi’s sky
Under its glow
the frost did melt
life blossoming with Exoswarm aid
Yet the Calamity stirred
its remnants ravaging the living
Thus, the six wisest among us
became the Heliodic Six
The Exostrider’s lens became our Heliogyre
From the Drive’s turn, the season’s laws we discerned
We shed all idle thought
to link our minds to the Heliogyre
Our shared cognition converged
for mortals to touch the edge of the Divine
Since then, the Roya have walked Lahai-Roi
for centuries
(Cutscene ends)

title: Ode to the Second Sunrise
content:
Our shared cognition converged
for mortals to touch the edge of the Divine
Since then, the Roya have walked Lahai-Roi
for centuries
(Cutscene ends)



The Shaper: The Six shared their computational power, weaving a vast network to reach the Exostrider in a dimension beyond mortal understanding.
The Shaper: The data we provided to the Spacetreck Collective was interpreted through this network.
The Shaper: But now, the only one who can continue the calculations… is me.
[Dialogue Option]  Can you not select new members for the Six?
The Shaper: The ones chosen for the Six are born with Resonance with the Heliogyre. It cannot be forced.
The Shaper: Now the remaining Five cannot calculate, and there are not enough worthy successors. Even if the Heliogyre resumes its rotations, unable to interpret its readings we will be.
The Shaper: For this reason, the aid I seek is this…
The Shaper: With your authority, allow me to bear the calculations of the Six alone and act in their stead.
Rover: The Heliogyre was meant to be interpreted by six.
Rover: If you bear all the calculations alone, what will become of you?
The Shaper: I cannot say.
The Shaper: All I know is this: If no one remains to interpret the Heliogyre, the Void Storm’s occurrences will be unknown. Life will once more fall into peril.
The Shaper: The Spacetrek Collective’s decades of effort in preparing for the New Solar Ceremony will come to nothing.
[Dialogue Option]  To ask this of you… is too cruel.
The Shaper: Since the moment I was brought to Solisylum as a child, I have never once seen the world beyond. In the Heliogyre’s light do I glimpse the universe, and in seeing life rejoice under my protection do I take comfort.
The Shaper: This has long since become second nature to me. A part of my life.
The Shaper: So now, what I bear is not glory or burden, but duty.
The Shaper: Arbiter, please. Grant me this authority.
[Dialogue Option]  (Agree.)
Rover: I respect what you wish to persist.
"The Shaper": ……
Rover: This is…
"The Shaper": Soon, a great calamity will fall upon Lahai-Roi.
"The Shaper": I will share all that I know of the Heliogyre with you. When you call, answer I will.
Rover: (Residual Voidmatter corruption?! I need to find a way to cleanse it!)
???: CHUU—
Rover: That sound… Is it Buddy?
"The Shaper": Save your strength for the calamity ahead, Arbiter.
"The Shaper": The children will help.

title: Ode to the Second Sunrise
content:
Rover: That sound… Is it Buddy?
"The Shaper": Save your strength for the calamity ahead, Arbiter.
"The Shaper": The children will help.



"The Shaper": The Rite of Return, the ritual that once sealed the calamity deep underground.
"The Shaper": Just now, the children have offered their strength.

Mornye: Move aside. Before the Drive falls completely, I need to go back to launch Helios.

content:

Mornye: I've already alerted the Academy to evacuate the area around the impact zone. Before the Drive crashes, it is imperative that we successfully deploy and launch Helios.

Warren: I understand your concerns... but we're on the verge of a disaster. The Collective can't just sit by and watch it happen.
Warren: This is my decision as the supervisor of this project. I will bear the consequences.
Mornye: No need for that.
Mornye: We've established contact with the Roya tribe and obtained the Drive's raw data. We can proceed with the New Solar Ceremony as originally planned.
Warren: ...Professor Mornye?
Warren: Did you just say you managed to obtain the data? Wonderful news. I'll prepare the connective instruments for you—
Mornye: There's no need for us to continue pretending anymore.
Mornye: Warren... Or should I say, traitor aligned with the Fractsidus.
Warren: That is a serious accusation, Professor Mornye.
Mornye: I know. I meant it to be.
Mornye: You must be very familiar with this device, Warren.
Mornye: You handcrafted it to avoid leaving usage records... a clever idea.
Mornye: But since it is a "personal" creation... the marks left behind are like fingerprints.
Mornye: These are your marks. They've betrayed your deeds. Warren, you've desecrated the hard work of everyone involved.
Mornye: Anslem's experiment accident, your current position in the project... It seems the Fractsidus played a part in both, didn't they?
Warren: Tch, that is a lot of assumptions and conjectures. With no evidence, I could easily sue you for slander—
Mornye: You're right. All I have right now are assumptions and conjectures. But my ultimate goal isn't to have you face justice today.
Mornye: Once we've identified the suspects, we'll have plenty of time to gather the evidence.
Mornye: What I need in this moment... is for you to step down as supervisor of this project.
Mornye: The one taking over... will be me.
Mornye: One more thing. Your subordinate provided us with some key evidence already.

content:

Lynae: Professor Mornye...

[Dialogue Option]  Congrats!
[Dialogue Option]  Enjoy the sweet taste of freedom!
Lynae: And... the bad news. Since I kinda did some falsifying during the investigation, they said I breached the rules.
[Dialogue Option]  Huh?!
Lynae: But since I did it to make sure the bad guy didn't get away with anything, and I actually helped out—
Lynae: The final verdict is I'll still have to stay on the "mental health watchlist" for a while.
[Dialogue Option]  So the Academy gots its hands on solid evidence?
Lynae: Well, once you have your suspect, the rest is easy. Plus, there's one teacher whose Forte can wring out the truth from anyone.
Lynae: But I do have Professor Mornye to thank for sending an official email that explained everything. That's the only reason they believed me.
Lynae: I guess that means it'll be harder to skip her classes now.

title: Ode to the Second Sunrise
content:

Rover: A light blue ring?



Rover: Can you describe what you saw in more detail?
Mornye: I... I can't be sure, but I think she protected me.
Rover: (It sounds like the girl Mornye saw is the same one I encountered when I first got to Lahai-Roi.)
Rover: (She's able to go up against the Threnodian herself, and appear in the Reactor Drive. She's connected with the Exostrider and the Threnodian in ways we still don't fully understand.)
Rover: (Figuring out who she is and what happened to her will be the next big task.)
Lynae: Rover? Rover—Hey, stop spacing out!
Lynae: To celebrate Professor Mornye waking up and the crisis being averted, don't you think we should...
[Dialogue Option]  Should what?
Lynae: Go for a ride!
Lynae: Nothing beats the wind on your face, especially when—
Lynae: The three of us still don't have a group picture!
Rover: Heh, a photo under the new Helios? Sounds like it'll make a good souvenir.

Mornye: I used to think that when I saw this view, I'd cry because my wish would be fulfilled.
Mornye: But now, when I see Helios's light pouring over the land, with the ancient frostlands and people who've been here for only a few decades sharing the same warmth...

Luuk Herssen: Three days ago, when Helios was launched, we registered an unexpected spike in Voidmatter concentrations near Hyvatia. It interfered with the launch.
Luuk Herssen: We're still unsure what triggered the surge. But after comparing the waveforms with the device Professor Mornye brought back, we suspect it was an artificially induced Void Storm.
Luuk Herssen: And we found you unconscious close by.
Anslem: Dr. Herssen, I really can't remember anything...
Luuk Herssen: (Chuckles) You can relax. Professor Lucilla has already given you the clear. You're not a suspect.
Luuk Herssen: I'm just here for protective oversight. Acting as your personal bodyguard, you might say.
Anslem: Aren't you the campus doctor? And you're... here to protect me?
Luuk Herssen: Heh, a doctor's duty, isn't it? But there is one thing I need your testimony on.
Luuk Herssen: Before you fainted, who did you see?
Researcher?: Good day, gentlemen! Hyvatia's routine maintenance has been completed. I'll be on my way.
Anslem: Who's that?
Anslem: Never mind. No time to think about that.
Anslem: Dr. Herssen, the Academy's review committee thinks what I've said is unbelievable. But if you're willing to trust me...
Anslem: Before I passed out, I saw... myself.
???: Ah, it seems my hastily chosen pawn has proven to be utterly ineffectual. It appears I'll have to add the final flourish to push the story to its climax.
???: But no matter, no matter. I'll simply chalk this up as a poor judgment call. A band of fools who enacted a farce.
???: Such a pity, though. With this piece expended, the chapter where the girl forms her bond with the Threnodian must be delayed.
???: But that is a tale to be savored later. Right, Rover?

title: Ode to the Second Sunrise
content:
[Objective: (Sit with Mornye)]
Mornye: Mentor, the wind may have... messed your hair...?
Mornye: The wind feels nice... I could stay here a little longer.
Mornye: Do you want to join me?
[Dialogue Option]  Do you have a moment to chat?
[Dialogue Option]  I have some matters to attend to.
Mornye: Yes. The Spacetrek Collective has given me a whole month of paid sick leave. My schedule is clear.
Mornye: The last time I had this much time off... I think I was back in middle school when I tumbled down a flight of stairs.
[Dialogue Option]  Were you alright?
Mornye: Well, at the time, I dropped the book I was reading down the stairs. So I accidentally... No, I shouldn't mention such embarassing things like that in front of you.
Mornye: Now, what would you like to discuss?
[Dialogue Option]  The New Solar Ceremony.
Mornye: The Reactor Drive didn't land as the Spacetrek Collective had originally planned. But now that it's on the ground, we can finally start researching it.
Mornye: And then, someday, we'll prove that both the sun and the stars are within our reach.
Mornye: It would be nice if you could be there to witness it with me.
[Dialogue Option]  (Chat about something else.)
[Dialogue Option]  (Chat about something else.)
[Dialogue Option]  About your nickname for me...
Mornye: Oh... it's because... it prevents your identity from being exposed.
[Dialogue Option]  But that's no longer necessary, right?
Mornye: You're right. I suppose I can't call you that anymore...
Mornye: But I have a friend. She faced a medical condition, and during a difficult time, she was guided by a mentor.
Mornye: Even tho that mentor left soon after, their influence stayed with her, and well, still affects me... I—I mean, my friend.
Mornye: As long as you have something to teach, you remain a mentor.
Mornye: So... can I still call you that?
[Dialogue Option]  Did we know each other before?
Mornye: That's... a secret.
[Dialogue Option]  What?!
[Dialogue Option]  Take care of yourself. See you next time.
[Dialogue Option]  (Chat about something else.)
Mornye: It's because someone made me promise that when they left. "Only by saying goodbye can there be progress and change," they said.
Mornye: So until their goals are achieved, that "goodbye" must remain final.
[Dialogue Option]  Until when?
Mornye: Hmm... maybe until the Reactor Drive is fully analyzed, the Exostrider on the frostlands is activated again, and the disaster buried deep below is finally dealt with. Or maybe until there are no more calamities left on this planet.
Mornye: Until I can give you that answer myself... Please, hold on to that curiositiy for just a little longer.
[Dialogue Option]  Take care of yourself. See you next time.
Mornye: Okay. See you next time. Oh, one more thing—
Mornye: Stay a bit longer this time, Mentor.
[Dialogue Option]  I have some matters to attend to.

content:
[Objective: (At the Riseway, three group of students before completing Quest)]
You really think the New Solar Ceremony would work?
If you ask me, the project itself is already mature, and all the simulations check out. So yeah, it's completely workable.
Replacing the sun with that Helios thing... honestly, that's beyond what I can imagine.

metadata.subsection: (At the Riseway, three group of students before completing Quest)

title: Ode to the Second Sunrise
content:
[Objective: (After completing Quest)]
Hooray! The New Solar Ceremony actually worked! But... why the long face?
...I heard Professor Mornye got hurt during the process.
Oh, I didn't know that... How about we pay her a visit once we're back at the Academy? We can bring her some snacks too!

title: Ode to the Second Sunrise
content:
[Objective: (Institute)]
Rogate: ...Oh, it's you. You're the one who helped Professor Mornye launch Helios during the New Solar Ceremony, right? Never got the chance to extend my gratitude.
Rogate: Thank you.
[Dialogue Option]  It was a collective effort.
Rogate: Haha... I won't deny that.
[Dialogue Option]  I'm just a student. I didn't help much.
Rogate: Haha, is that so? Let's leave it at that.
[Dialogue Option]  How's Helios running now?
Rogate: Stable. Power systems, core output, and signal transmission are all in perfect sync. Not that we're letting our guard down.
Rogate: Don't worry. We'll keep our new sun safe.

title: Ode to the Second Sunrise
content:
Rogate: Don't worry. We'll keep our new sun safe.



Cody: Anslem, where were you during the New Solar Ceremony?!
Anslem: I honestly don't know...
Cody: Anslem, where were you during the New Solar Ceremony?! Hyvatia malfunctioned, and Professor Mornye still hasn't recovered from her injuries!
Anslem: Look, everyone from the Academy has already asked me this. I honestly don't know...
Anslem: Warren said Hyvatia's parameters were off and told me to go check it out downstairs. But the moment I stepped off the Starward Riseway, I blacked out.
Anslem: If I weren't in the habit of suiting up before inspecting Hyvatia, I'd have been lost to the Void Storm.
Cody: Warren? They found out he has links to the Fractsidus.
Anslem: What?!
Rover: (Looks like Warren lured Anslem away during the New Solar Ceremony)
Rover: (He lost conciousness after getting off the Riseway... but Warren was still at the Academy at that time. Couldn't have done the deed himself.)
Rover: (There are other Fractsidus players in Lahai-Roi besides Warren. Need to keep an eye out.)

title: Ode to the Second Sunrise
content:
Rover: (There are other Fractsidus players in Lahai-Roi besides Warren. Need to keep an eye out.)



Angry Researcher: See? I told you. While we were all fighting the Trenodian, Warren was in bed with the Fractsidus. The Fractsidus! It's unforgivable.
Angry Researcher: All our efforts over these years were almost completely destroyed!
Anxious Researcher: To think Warren was capable of that... Thank the stars the New Solar Ceremony proceeded as planned, thanks to Mornye's oversight...
Anxious Researcher: By the way, I hear the inquiry into Warren has already begun.
Anxious Researcher: I wonder if there are other moles in the Institute... I heard someone from another project...
Angry Researcher: ...Enough. Why the sudden paranoia?
Angry Researcher: We work in a lab, not an interrogation room. This isn't something we should be thinking about.

title: Ode to the Second Sunrise
content:
[Objective: (Bjartr Woods)]
Should I call you our guest, or... the Predicted One?

I knew it! Yngvar walks a crooked path.
To think, even one named a successor to the Heliodic Six could fall to treachery...

Are you really the hero that was predicted to come?
JOACHIM! Forgive him, my little brother's tongue runs faster than his manners...

Did you hear Yngvar is subject to disciplinary action by the Solisylum?
Serves him right! I told you he never deserved to be a successor in the first place!

title: Ode to the Second Sunrise
content:
Serves him right! I told you he never deserved to be a successor in the first place!



Herja: To think it was Yngvar who did such a thing...
Aksel: Sigh...
Herja: Ah. I felt it in my gut, but to think it was Yngvar who did such a thing...
Aksel: From the Void Storm we pulled him, Herja. And now by our own hands, to judgement he goes. It is a closed circle.
[Dialogue Option]  Hello.
Aksel: Ah, the Predicted One? We meet again. Welcome to Haldarheim.
[Dialogue Option]  So what happened to Yngvar in the end?
Aksel: Sigh...
Aksel: Everything changed the day of that Void Storm. When the sky brightenened again, a Soliskin found us. We followed it into Bjartr Woods, and there, Yngvar we found, unconcious.
Aksel: He had no fatal wounds, only signs of scorching. We brought him back to Haldarheim to recover.
[Dialogue Option]  (Sounds like Mornye gave Yngvar a good thrashing.)
Aksel: When he woke, silence he kept. But then, those from the Solisylum came. The truth of his deeds they laid bare, and he broke down and wept, confessing everything.
Aksel: To the Solisylum's custody, he has been given. His punishment will not be pleasant.
[Dialogue Option]  And the world rejoices.
[Dialogue Option]  A bitter end, at any rate.
Herja: Outcasts, both his parents were. Aksel and I brought him out of the Void Storm and raised him to manhood in our tribe. We thought... we had saved him...
Aksel: No matter how it ends, he chose this path. The consequences he must now carry.

title: Ode to the Second Sunrise
content:
[Objective: (Solisylum)]
You see the Shaper bathed in the Heliogyre's radiance, silent as an inanimate vessel. As you prepare to speak to him, he slowly opens his eyes.
"The Shaper": To lay eyes on you once more, Arbiter, is a pleasure.
"The Shaper": The Heliogyre has shown me that the Spacetreck Collective's ceremony was a success. To you and your companions, my congratulations I offer.
"The Shaper": If questions remain for me, or the Heliogyre. I, the Shaper, shall answer.
[Dialogue Option]  Ask about the Solisylum.
"The Shaper": Because of your aid, the Heliogyre turns anew. The Solisylum has returned to normality.
"The Shaper": The Helios in the sky now weaves together wisdom from both the Spacetrek Collective and the Roya. Data once seen only by the Heliogyre... now the Hyvatia Detector may also obtain.
"The Shaper": The Heliogyre's operations stand ready to perform primary verificiation tasks.
"The Shaper":  Thus, in the Solisylum, I alone am sufficient.
[Dialogue Option]  Ask about the remaining Five.
"The Shaper": After your authorization, the Heliogyre has concentrated all of its computational power within me. No longer do the Six need to bear those immense calculations in parallel, at all times.
"The Shaper": Now, the other Five may devote their energies to managing Royan affairs. Under the new sun, the Roya need new season laws.
"The Shaper": For this, I require them to gather outside knowledge. With this, I will weave into my own computations.
"The Shaper": Iselde's (The Eye) perception, Horstvald's (the Binder) foresight, Laetia's (the Recorder) curiosity, Eivind's (the Chronicler) discipline, and Freamir's (the Refiner) empathy... they are the Heliogyre's senses in the world. And to the Solisylum, they will return their findings.
"The Shaper": Before they entered the Solisylum, the Heliodic Six were but mere mortals.
"The Shaper": Now they enjoy some time to lay down their burden. I hope... their lives will unfold as they wish. At least for the time being.
"The Shaper": If you see them in Lahai-Roi, please, as a witness, offer them your blessing.
[Dialogue Option]  Ask about him.
"The Shaper": All of the Heliogyre's computational power is now concentrated within me. Wherever the sunlight touches, so too do my thoughts.
[Dialogue Option]  But this is not without cost.
"The Shaper": ...
"The Shaper": As you once said... I am now bound to the Heliogyre's will. From the Solisylum, I cannot depart.
"The Shaper": Human flesh and blood were not made to bear such vast quantitites of information in so short a span. Should this continue, my body's decay will quicken tenfold until electricity within my nerves ceases... and a final computation concludes.
"The Shaper": Yet... the Spacetrek Collective already seeks a remedy. Just as the Heliodic Six with mortal strength touched the divine, so too does their technology strive to undow the toll the gods have exacted upon me.
"The Shaper": I believe in them. Just as I have always believed in the Roya.
"The Shaper": In the future where the light shines brighter, we will one day witness together.
[Dialogue Option]  I have no more questions.
"The Shaper": Goodbye, Arbiter.
"The Shaper": Do not forget that all the knowledge of the Heliogyre is mine to share with you. Should you have need, I will respond.

title: Ode to the Second Sunrise
content:
Hyvatia Detector - A monitoring instrument installed on the surface of Sundermere by the Spacetrek Collective to oversee and maintain the Reactor Drive. At its core is a replica of the Exostrider's calibration module, enabling a dedicated data link with the Drive to transmit real-time correction parameters. Hyvatia plays a vital role in ensuring the Reactor Drive's continuous and stable operation.

New Solar Ceremony - A Spacetrek Collective project decades in the making to replace the Reactor Drive in the sky with Helios, an artificial sun engineered by the Research Institute. Its ultimate goal is to retrieve the Drive as a power source to awaken the Exostrider slumbering in the frostlands, all while keeping Lahai-Roi's ecosystem stable.

title: Ode to the Second Sunrise
content:
Helios - The artificial sun crafted by the Spacetrek Collective: Research Institute to replace the Reactor Drive in the New Solar Ceremony. For successful operation, it requires environmental data from Hyvatia and raw observational data on the Reactor Drive provided by the Heliogyre.

Heliogyre - An artifact used exclusively by the Heliodic Six to observe the Reactor Drive. During the New Solar Ceremony, it provides Helios with raw observational data on the Reactor Drive.

Exoswarm Material - Materials harvested from Exoswarm. Though still essentially parts of the Exostrider, they are widely utilized in engineering Lahai-Roi's various constructs.

Shephards - Roya chosen by the Soliskin for their pure nature become Shepherds. Their duty is to guide and care for the Soliskin. They lead the Soliskin to the best sunlit areas of Bjartr Woods and keep them safe.

title: Ode to the Second Sunrise
content:
Solsworn - Individuals gifted in calendrical calculation and a degree of resonance with the Exostrider and Soliskin are permitted into the Solisylum. There, they serve the Heliodic Six as aides and the tribe as healers and teachers, all while being groomed as the Six's eventual successors.

The Heliodic Six - Roya elders such as the Eye, the Binder, and the Shaper. Each pair in the Six is entrusted with the roles of observation, archival, and extrapolation. They reside within the Solisylum, tracing the Reactor Drive's trajectories and forecasting Void Storms.

Soliskin - A type of Exoswarm originating from the Exostrider's neural structures. They are believed to embody fragments of its consciousness.

Bjartr Woods - The forest where the Soliskin dwell. Bathed in the light of the Reactor Drive, the woods remain untouched by the ravages of Void Storms.

title: Ode to the Second Sunrise
content:
Rite of Return - A ceremony held by the Roya for the Soliskin. During the rite, the Soliskin transform into ethereal energy forms. Guided by Shepherds, they enter the Solistrees and disperse into luminescence as they rise. The Roya believe this marks the Soliskin's return to the Exostrider.

Solisylum - The sacred ground of the Roya and the dwelling of the Heliodic Six. It safeguards Exostrider parts and serves as the central archive for all Royan records. With each operational cycle of the Reactor Drive, the Solisylum calculates its stability, tracks the birth and growth of the Exoswarm, and monitors their eventual return to the Exostrider.

title: Ode to the Second Sunrise
content: Reactor Drive - The Exostrider's power core and Lahai-Roi's underground "sun." Royan records say this energy entity was removed from the Exostrider and placed underground to sustain the haven. However, monitoring data confirms a gradual but steady decline in its energy output. Both the Roya and the Spacetrek Collective are now formulating emergency contingencies in response.

title: The Star That Voyages Far
content: Quest Objective: To find the Exostrider and uncover the truth behind your frequency loss, you step into the falling snow and venture toward the silent, pale expanse of the frostlands.

title: The Star That Voyages Far
subsection: (Read the WavesLine message sent by Academic Affairs)
content:
[Objective: (Read the WavesLine message sent by Academic Affairs)]
Startorch Academy Academic Affairs System: Course Reminder The Academic Affairs System kindly reminds you that the elective Royan Culture: Historical Metaphors in the Trine Myth will begin shortly. This lecture will be delivered by President Lucilla. Please be mindful of the time and proceed to the lecture hall.}}
Rover: (My symptoms have stopped for now. But whatever drained my frequency is still somewhere in Lahai-Roi.)
Rover: (The only thing I haven't surveyed yet is the Exostrider out in the frostlands.)
Rover: (The Roya's Trine Myth likely mentions it. This lecture could be my chance to find a clue.)

metadata.subsection: (Read the WavesLine message sent by Academic Affairs)

title: The Star That Voyages Far
subsection: (Read the WavesLine message sent by Academic Affairs)
content:
Rover: (The Roya's Trine Myth likely mentions it. This lecture could be my chance to find a clue.)



Lucilla: Now, we reach the second epoch of the Royan Trine Myth, the Sacred Reactor Epoch.
Lucilla: After Baldur, the Sun's incarnation, had sealed the foreign divinity Hvedrungr, the frostlands fell into an endless dream… Assistant Nivora, would you continue?
Nivora: O-okay. T-this section...  it describes how the Exostrider used its greatsword to seal the Threnodian behind the Stridergate.
Nivora: The records say both the Exostrider and the Threnodian travelled through the  to reach Lahai-Roi. Their battle was fierce.
Nivora: The Threnodian pushed the Exostrider to the brink of defeat.
Nivora: But at that moment, for reasons unknown, the Exostrider's Reactor Drive flared with blinding light—
???: —And it found the strength to raise its sword and seal the Threnodian away. Lahai-Roi was saved. What a relief!
Aemeath: Hi, nice to meet you. I'm Aemeath from Rabelle College, same as you.
Aemeath: First time seeing you in class. Trying to collect credits from all four departments? That's ambitious. Welcome to the academic quagmire.
Rover: Aemeath?! I've been looking for you.
Rover: I never got the chance to thank you.
Aemeath: Thank me?
Rover: The day the Eye of the Threnodian appeared, you drove it back and saved me.
Aemeath: Did I? …Sorry, I don't remember that.
Rover: (She doesn't sound like she's lying. Then how...)
Aemeath: A Synchronist… Rover… Hahaha!
Rover: What's so funny?
Aemeath: Oh, don't mind me. I'm just not used to seeing you like this.
Aemeath: I mean, look at you. Something's missing, though... Oh, I know, a uniform!
Aemeath: The Academy still hasn't issued you one? They're painfully slow sometimes.
Rover: Aemeath?
Aemeath: I have to go.
Aemeath: Gotta run, Professor!
Lucilla: Rover, let's try to channel that enthusiasm into listening. Do come see me in my office after class, okay?
Lucilla: Assistant Nivora, if you would? Pick up from the Twilight Epoch's Unending Winter, please.

metadata.subsection: (Read the WavesLine message sent by Academic Affairs)

title: The Star That Voyages Far
subsection: (Read the WavesLine message sent by Academic Affairs)
content:
Lucilla: Assistant Nivora, if you would? Pick up from the Twilight Epoch's Unending Winter, please.



Nivora: Sigrika, could you come to the library with me?
Sigrika: Okay. Hey... Did you notice the new student? The one who kept talking to himself during class.
Nivora: Hmm—
Lucilla: Rover. Something happened during class, didn't it?
[Dialogue Option]  (Tell her about Aemeath.)
Lucilla: …So a girl named Aemeath just got up and left the lecture hall?
Lucilla: Heh. I never expected to hear that name again. Certainly not like this.
Lucilla: Perhaps you've just had a run-in with a "ghost"?
Lucilla: After all... You were the only one who saw her.
Rover: President Lucilla, what do you know about her?
Lucilla: Stay at Rabelle College long enough, and you'll eventually hear her name mentioned. Though it's a story from over a decade ago now.
Lucilla: Aemeath was a Synchronist. Brilliant. Popular. Professors had high hopes for her.
Lucilla: Then, during a piloting drill, she simply vanished.
Lucilla: She climbed into a simulator with the others. But when the cockpit reopened, hers was empty.
Lucilla: Intrigued? Want to go find her?
[Dialogue Option]  I am indeed intrigued.
Lucilla: Of course. You're exactly the type to get pulled into Aemeath's story.
[Dialogue Option]  She saved me once.
Lucilla: She saved you? Heh, seems the mysteries around that girl are still multiplying.
Lucilla: To see someone who vanished years ago, presumed dead, lingering around the Academy. A figment of your imagination, or is there more to it? I'm very curious to find out.
Lucilla: She disappeared from the Synchrolink Training Grounds. The very cockpit she vanished from is still there.
Lucilla: The Academy turned it inside out at the time and found nothing. But if you're interested, go take a look.
Lucilla: I expect you'll dig up some new surprises for us.
(Quest unlocked: The Star That Voyages Far)

Rover: (Soliskin? What could they be doing here?)
Rover: (That Soliskin... It's headed straight for the Synchrolink Training Grounds.)

Rover: (My frequency loss… It's getting worse!)

metadata.subsection: (Read the WavesLine message sent by Academic Affairs)

title: The Star That Voyages Far
subsection: (Read the WavesLine message sent by Academic Affairs)
content:
Rover: (That Soliskin... It's headed straight for the Synchrolink Training Grounds.)

Rover: (My frequency loss… It's getting worse!)



Aemeath: Aaaand... nope! Still on the fritz. How are you feeling?
Rover: I'm… okay. After that mech flew off, I felt less of my frequency bleeding out.
Rover: (That mech's frequency felt like the presence from the rift back in Honami City.)
Rover: Aemeath, that mech only left after it saw you. After you clashed with it.
Rover: That's twice you've saved me. Each time I'm left with more questions than answers. They say you're the Exostrider's Synchronist who's been missing for over ten years.
Rover: And your hand back there...
Aemeath: Me? I'm not the Exostrider's Synchronist now.
Aemeath: I'm its Resonator.
Aemeath: I just... died first. Call me a digital ghost!
Aemeath: Ten plus years back, the underground seal broke. The Threnodian on the other side of the Stridergate was about to swallow Lahai-Roi.
Aemeath: I was still a student. My sync with the Exostrider hadn't hit a hundred percent yet.
Aemeath: But there was no other choice. The Exostrider was still sleeping, so I had to do something... unorthodox.
Rover: So you Overclocked yourself to try to resonate with it?
Aemeath: Yup. Impressive, right? I woke the big guy up, if only for a second.
Aemeath: The seal held. The crisis averted. Everyone I cared about... they made it out okay.
Aemeath: But it was too much for me. My body couldn't take it and got totally torn apart.
Aemeath: So yeah. I died. But I'm still here... just, floatin' around. I've been a little invisible. Well, a lot invisible. To everyone until you.
[Dialogue Option]  Why am I the only one who can see you?
[Dialogue Option]  I couldn't see you before.
Aemeath: You can see me now... because of this little guy.
Aemeath: The Exostrider's Reactor Core. My existence is kinda tethered to it now. Think of it as my heart.
Aemeath: Even as a digital ghost, I never stopped trying to pull my "self" back together. To get back to reality.
Aemeath: There's something I gotta do. And I gotta be the Exostrider's true Resonator to see it through.
Aemeath: But our Resonance started with an Overclock. The power I got was unstable from the get-go.
Aemeath: I've spent years building it back up with this Core. The Soliskin have been my little helpers, too.
Aemeath: Then, not long ago, you ended up with it. That became your backstage pass to seeing me.
Rover: "Not long ago." You mean when the Reactor Drive fell?
Aemeath: Bingo! Since then, the Core has become energy stored inside you. This is the first time I managed to make it solid. Took me a bit to figure out the trick.
Rover: Then it was you. You're the one who saved Mornye when she was dying.
Aemeath: You and that junior of yours were always close. We even crossed paths a few times back when I was still... well, around. Of course I'd help.
Rover: (A junior of mine? So I really did know Mornye in the past...)
Aemeath: Oh, and by the way? When you charged in to save Professor Mornye you looked pretty cool!
[Dialogue Option]  ...
[Dialogue Option]  ...You saw all that.
Aemeath: Alright, no more teasing. But I mean it. No matter what, you always choose to save.
Aemeath: And to me... that's the coolest thing in the world. The most beautiful.
Aemeath: Anyway! Back to business. The Reactor Core is tied to Sigillum—that's the mech that attacked you.
Aemeath: It's like those Voidworms you fought. Made mostly of Exostrider parts, but corrupted. Contaminated by Threnodian Voidmatter.
Aemeath: Sigillum... stole a chunk of my power. That threw a wrench in my whole "reassembling myself" project. Now it's after the Core, too.
Aemeath: Since Sigillum holds this piece of the Exostrider's power, it can't be killed completely as long as the Exostrider and I exist. Now, it can only be me who stops it.
Aemeath: And since just touching the thing makes your frequency drain, taking it down should plug your leak, too.
Aemeath: Plus, I get my power back. Win-win.
Aemeath: But see what it's doing to me? Even with you holding the Core, I keep flickering in and out. One second I can touch you, the next I'm fading right through. So annoying—
Aemeath: So will you help? You've got the Core, and the Reactor Drive is wrecked. I can't do this alone.
Aemeath: Also, I've noticed... when the Core is in your hand, it runs faster.
Rover: I can tell you're leaving a few things out, Aemeath.
Rover: Still, you helped me and a lot of people in Lahai-Roi. That's enough for me to trust you. What do you need me to do?
Aemeath: "Existence" is the imprint life leaves behind. Being remembered, talked about, and seen...
Aemeath: All the places I went when I was alive bear those imprints. The Core's running lets me find and record those frequencies.
Aemeath: These little cuties have been my scouts, and they'll be our guides now, too.
Aemeath: Pretty easy, huh? All you gotta do is carry the Core and follow our lead.
Rover: I'll do it.
Aemeath: Alrighty! Thanks in advance, study buddy.

title: The Star That Voyages Far
subsection: (Read the WavesLine message sent by Academic Affairs)
content:
Rover: I'll do it.
Aemeath: Alrighty! Thanks in advance, study buddy.



Aemeath: The Soliskin went down the lift. Let's follow.
Rover:  Before we go, I need to contact Mornye.
Rover: The Reactor Drive was Lahai-Roi's "sun." If I'm using the Core, the Academy will want to know.
Aemeath: Go for it! No problem!

title: The Star That Voyages Far
subsection: (Read the WavesLine message sent by Academic Affairs)
content:
Rover: The Reactor Drive was Lahai-Roi's "sun." If I'm using the Core, the Academy will want to know.
Aemeath: Go for it! No problem!



Rover: (Aemeath definitely glossed over some things.)
Rover: (Like what happened during our previous encounter, what she's done since becoming a digital ghost, and the real reason why Sigillum stole her power.)
Rover: (After years drifting like this, to still hold onto that spirit... Her will must be strong. Prying answers from her won't be easy.)
Rover: (I'll bide my time. The right moment will come.)
Mornye: Has something happened, Mentor?
[Dialogue Option]  (Tell her about the Reactor Core.)
Mornye: I see. So the Reactor Drive's Core survived the crash?
Mornye: It must be the key to reactivating the Exostrider. Of course, then the official stance is that it be returned. Startorch Academy and the Roya would both agree on that.
Mornye: But, as you said, curiosity from the Institute is inevitable—
Rover: Mornye?
Lucilla: My, my. Already caused a stir in the training grounds? Color me impressed.
Lucilla: I'll have people clean up the aftermath. You can carry on as you see fit.
Rover: You were monitoring my comms with Mornye?
Lucilla: You're a person of special interest. Of course we keep an eye on your movements.
Rover: "We"?
Lucilla: Yes, "we." The Spacetrek Collective. Think of us as the annoying adults on campus.
Lucilla: I'll handle the debate between the Institute and the Academy about the Core. This is a matter of priority. They'll listen to me.
Lucilla: But when you're done with your business, I'll need you to return the Core to the Exostrider, Rover.
Lucilla: You didn't mention it to Mornye, but I suspect... your possession of it traces back to Aemeath, doesn't it?
Rover: President Lucilla, I don't appreciate being interrogated over a tapped line.
Lucilla: Heh, my apologies. As the one responsible for this Academy, matters related to the Exostrider tend to cloud my judgement.
Lucilla: After the incident with Warren, we upgraded safety protocols on public lines. No more overstepping.
Lucilla: Here is a peace offering. I've granted you full clearance: passes for the Starward Riseway, archive access, and use of Academy weaponry and equipment.
Lucilla: I'll also personally apologize to Professor Mornye for interrupting your comms and ensure her next research grant is... substantially approved.
Lucilla: How's that, Rover? More to your liking?
Rover: Why is the Spacetrek Collective pushing this so hard?
Lucilla: You should know. You have a past in Lahai-Roi, and you have some kind of connection with the Exostrider.
Lucilla: The Twilight Epoch, the Unending Winter described in Royan legend... the threat of the Threnodian Aleph-1 is growing. We need the Exostrider awakened. Returning that Reactor Core is the only way.
Lucilla: We've always trusted you to stand with us in this matter. To stand on the side of humanity.
Lucilla: You know where to find me if you need anything, Rover. And my door is always open if you just want to talk.

Aemeath: The Soliskin are leading us to the auditorium first.
Aemeath: The New Solar Celebration is almost here. I wonder what they'll put on this time.
Aemeath: By then, exams will be over, and we'll finally get a long break.
Aemeath: Ah, vacation! What's not to look forward to!

content:
Aemeath: By then, exams will be over, and we'll finally get a long break.
Aemeath: Ah, vacation! What's not to look forward to!



Outgoing Fan: Told you! There are tons of Fleet Snowfluff fans at the Academy.
Shy Fan: Oh, hello… are you here for the Fleet Snowfluff fan meeting? The venue is still being set up, but once it's ready, please join.
[Dialogue Option]  Fleet Snowfluff?
Outgoing Fan: She's a singer! A campus legend. She's only released online, but she's super popular.
Shy Fan: But… her site hasn't been updated in over ten years. She posted one last demo and then… nothing.
Outgoing Fan: Don't be such a downer. Maybe she just graduated and moved on to bigger things.
Outgoing Fan: Probably never showed her face to keep her life private. Doesn't matter, we still have her music!
Outgoing Fan: Here! Even if you're not a fan, you should give her a listen. I'm new here, but even I was hooked when I first heard her songs!
The outgoing fan shoves a poster into your hands.
Aemeath: Hm, nice print.
Aemeath: A fan meeting... huh? If they're happy, I'm happy.
Aemeath: C'mon, let's follow the Soliskin and see what's going on in the auditorium!

metadata.subsection: (Read the WavesLine message sent by Academic Affairs)

title: The Star That Voyages Far
content:
[Objective: Enter the Auditorium]
Yeah, yeah, move the poster a little more... Stop! Too far—
It's about to start! Quit being such a perfectionist!
Wait, just one more adjustment...!

Resident: After scrapping so many drafts, I finally got this poster ready for everyone in the fan meeting to see.
Resident: I hope it helps more people come to love Fleet Snowfluff—just like I did.

Resident: The fan meeting merch made it on time! Thank goodness... Yawn...
Another Resident: Go get some rest. You don't want to stay up till the Reaper comes, do you?
Resident: Impossible! I'm from the Department of Engineering. No one knows pulling all-nighters better than we do...

title: The Star That Voyages Far
content:
Resident: Impossible! I'm from the Department of Engineering. No one knows pulling all-nighters better than we do...



Resident: Thinking about how all of us are about to listen to "Fallen Petals" live makes me kinda nervous.
Resident: I've met so many friends without even trying just 'cause we all love Fleet Snowfluff. I feel so lucky.
Another Resident: Me too! Her music brought you to me, and now our lives get to cross paths...
(Triggered when approaching the designated character or object.)
Aemeath: What?
[Dialogue Option]  They… can’t see you.
[Dialogue Option]  Why bother waving?
Aemeath: Oh, just a habit of mine. Waving, chatting, going to class... it makes me feel like I'm still alive.
Aemeath: If I stop, I might forget what it felt like to be human. Call it… a self-reminder.
Rover: ...Fleet Snowfluff?
Aemeath: Yep, that's me. Ugh, but don't say my alias out loud! It's embarrassing—
Rover: So you weren't just a Synchronist. You had a whole other life here.
Aemeath: Just one of my many hobbies. I was into photography, gaming, movie nights with friends…
Aemeath: Figured you only get to be a student for a few years. And I wasn't the ambitious researcher type. I wanted to soak it all up while I could.
Aemeath: I tried a little bit of everything. I just wanted a happy, carefree life!
Aemeath: Who knew I'd end up as a ghost, stuck as a student for ten more years… How awful is that? Wait... does this mean I'm never gonna graduate?!
[Dialogue Option]  You might get the chance once you restore your body.
Aemeath: Hope so. Guess everyone needs something to hold onto. It's good to have a little hope.
[Dialogue Option]  I wish I could be a student forever!
Aemeath: Haha! I get it. School life is easier. A whole lot less complicated.
Aemeath: But I have to say... It's really moving to hear people talk about my songs after all this time.
Aemeath: I wrote those for myself, you know? Never expected so many people to care.
Aemeath: But, if they made someone feel something—joy, pain, anything—that makes me really happy!
Aemeath: Hey, listen. Hear that song playing in the auditorium? That's the unfinished demo I left on my site.
Aemeath: What a shame. I really should've finished that before the training run. Now it's my little musical... epitaph. Haha.
Rover: ...
Aemeath: Let's go! The Soliskin is calling us.

title: The Star That Voyages Far
content:
Rover: ...
Aemeath: Let's go! The Soliskin is calling us.



Past Surprised Student: Is that the student rep from Rabelle College? That's one bold speech…
Past Mocking Student: Haha, is she giving a welcome speech or recruiting for a space adventure club? Uh-oh, the professors look upset.
Past Gentle Student: But she made a good point, didn't she? Isn't that passion the entire reason we're here? To explore whatever's out there again?

title: The Star That Voyages Far
content:
Past Gentle Student: But she made a good point, didn't she? Isn't that passion the entire reason we're here? To explore whatever's out there again?



Past Impressed Teacher: Aemeath, right? I remember her sync test scores were off the charts. We might be looking at this year's prime Exostrider candidate.
Past Stern Teacher: Don't be so sure. Heard about her extracurriculars? Put nicely, she's quite the dabbler. Put bluntly, she doesn't take anything seriously.
Past Thoughtful Teacher: Potential is still potential. She's brilliant. She just needs… guidance.
Past Aemeath: May we one day walk among the stars, to touch with our own hands a universe so cold, so real, and so breathtakingly beautiful.
Past Aemeath: That's all from me. If I keep going, my credits this year might be in danger!
Past Aemeath: It's an amazing feeling to be here at Startorch Academy, and to know I'll be sharing this journey into the great unknown with all of you. As a student, I can't wait to start this new chapter of my life.
Past Aemeath: There's just one thing missing today... I wish my family could be here in the crowd to hear this.
Past Aemeath: So, to him, I want to say: I'm doing great. And I'm happy. Everything is just as you hoped it would be. So please, don't worry about me.

title: The Star That Voyages Far
content:
Aemeath: Looking back… I really do miss those days.
Aemeath: Startorch Academy is a nice place. I mean, I caused my fair share of trouble, but the professors never turned me away from lectures.
Rover: You saved Lahai-Roi, Aemeath. But you paid for it with your future, and no one even knows...
[Dialogue Option]  Do you feel lonely?
Aemeath: Maybe a little? But it's fine. Loneliness doesn't kill. Besides, I still have plenty to keep myself busy with!
[Dialogue Option]  Do you feel regret?
Aemeath: Of course not. If I hadn't have done what I did, so many people would have died. Besides, saving the world is a pretty nice feeling!
Aemeath: I just... I wish I could've been there. At graduation. To hug my friends and wish them all the happiness in the world.
Aemeath: The Soliskin headed outside! Let's catch up!
Aemeath: If it's leaving the campus, it's probably going to the frostlands. Right, we'll need to take the Starward Riseway.
Rover: That place above the sword?
Aemeath: Yes. A frozen, silent plain, white with endless snow. The place where the Exostrider finally sank into slumber.

title: The Star That Voyages Far
content:
Aemeath: Yes. A frozen, silent plain, white with endless snow. The place where the Exostrider finally sank into slumber.



We've gotta keep pushing the Snowfluff Seal figurines at this meet!
Next year's fan meeting ain't gonna fund itself. Go, go, go!
LET'S GO!
You tell 'em!
I WAS BORN FOR THIS!

Aemeath: Our next stop is the Starward Riseway. Are you ready?
[Dialogue Option]  Let's go.
[Dialogue Option]  Not yet.
[Dialogue Option]  Not yet.

Aemeath: When I was a kid, I once hid in the Starward Riseway and made it to the frostlands all by myself.
Rover: Bold even as a child…
Aemeath: Hee hee.

title: The Star That Voyages Far
content:
[Objective: (Idle dialogue)]
Resident: Ugh, I hope we won't run into bad weather again like last time…
Another Resident: Everyone confirm you've got everything?
Resident: Relax. We've packed more than enough supplies for this frostlands field trip.

title: The Star That Voyages Far
subsection: Sit and wait for the train to arrive
content:
Aemeath: Cold?
Rover: I'm fine. What about you?
Aemeath: Between you and me, ghosts can't feel the cold.
Aemeath: The snow... It's so beautiful.
Luuk Herssen: What a coincidence to run into you here, {PlayerName}. This is a pleasant surprise.
Aemeath: Oh… it's Dr. Luuk. When he's around, just pretend I'm not here. Otherwise, you look like a weirdo talking to thin air.
Aemeath: You should hide too, okay? This is our secret journey.
Rover: You know him?
Aemeath: He's the school doctor. All the students know him. I didn't super well, but I do know that he's been in Lahai-Roi for a long time, and… you can trust him.
Luuk Herssen: You came to the frostlands for the Exostrider?
Luuk Herssen: I'm headed the same way. I've got to check in on some researchers stationed out here on long-term fieldwork.
Luuk Herssen: Having a guide might make the trip a little easier. What do you say?
Luuk Herssen: Let me help you modify your bike. There are quite a few waterways, and its current setup might not handle them well.
Rover: You know how to modify bikes?
Luuk Herssen: You pick up a few things when you come here as often as I do.
Aemeath: Oh, I used to love riding! My friends even called me the Speed Queen! Though that was usually while they were white-knuckling the seat and screaming. Heh.
Luuk Herssen: Look at this place, Rover. Hard to believe it, but years ago, all of this was a lush, green forest.
Luuk Herssen: Back then, the Roya were nomads, the true natives of Lahai-Roi, who walked in step with nature itself.
Rover: Was it the Lament that changed it into frostlands?
Luuk Herssen: Yes. It triggered a magnetic pole shift. From then on, Lahai-Roi became the new pole.
Luuk Herssen: The Lament wasn't the only cataclysm stirring back then.
Luuk Herssen: In the past, we had already reached the stars. But at some point… the  spread to cover all of Solaris.
Luuk Herssen: From that moment on...
Aemeath: From that moment on, the universe locked its doors. We couldn't verify whether the sky above us was real or just a reflection.
Luuk Herssen: Countless spacecraft were lost. Our space exploration programs were abandoned. And space became out of reach.
Luuk Herssen: But times have changed. Since its founding, the goal of Startorch Academy has been to use the Exostrider to explore space—whether through the Etheric Sea or the .
Rover: I understand the Etheric Sea part, but the Stridergate…?
Luuk Herssen: You know Lahai-Roi's history. Both the Exostrider and the Threnodian first came to Solaris through the Stridergate.
Luuk Herssen: The Academy has its theories, but here are two you might find interesting:
[Dialogue Option]  An outer space gateway you say...
[Dialogue Option]  An alien Threnodian...?
Luuk Herssen: With a gateway like that, of course we want to open it. But to pass through, we must awaken the Exostrider and be prepared to face Aleph-1 head-on.
Luuk Herssen: I've long believed that Aleph-1 poses a far greater threat beyond Void Storms and Voidworms.
Luuk Herssen: With other Threnodians, we can at least glean clues of their nature from their places of origin and the civilizations they emerge from. But Aleph-1… our knowledge remains blank.
Luuk Herssen: So many dream of being the voyager who returns from the stars, the first to walk the cosmos once more. But in all these years, no one has succeeded.
Luuk Herssen: The  cast us into isolation. But it also gave birth to all our dreams of what could lie beyond.
Luuk Herssen: And those dreams… are still alive today.

metadata.subsection: Sit and wait for the train to arrive

title: The Star That Voyages Far
subsection: Sit and wait for the train to arrive
content:
Luuk Herssen: And those dreams… are still alive today.



Luuk Herssen: You've been enrolled for a while now. What are your impressions of Lahai-Roi and Startorch Academy?
Rover: It feels like a more hopeful microcosm of the world. Just… the politics are more complicated than I expected.
Luuk Herssen: The Spacetrek Collective is made up of people from all over. Balancing everyone's different agendas is just part of the package.
Luuk Herssen: I once heard a fun theory from a friend—that its predecessor, the Polar Collective, got its start because of a trick pulled during negotiations in favor of the Roya.
Rover: Dr. Herssen…
Luuk Herssen: Just call me Luuk. It has a nicer ring to it, no?
Rover: Then Luuk... you asked about my feelings on the Academy. What about yours? How long have you been here?
Luuk Herssen: About twenty years. I was a traveler before that, seeing what Solaris had to offer. But then a friend asked me to come to Lahai-Roi. To keep an eye on things here for him.
Luuk Herssen: The students make it easy. Watching them find their way is its own reward. They enjoy talking, and I enjoy listening. The work suits me well.

title: The Star That Voyages Far
content:
[Objective: (Idle dialogue)]
Resident: The snow is piled up so deep here.
Another Resident: Yeah. Keep an eye out for the Void Storm and our surroundings.
Resident: If an avalanche breaks loose...

title: The Star That Voyages Far
subsection: Ride your motorbike into the frostlands
content:
[Objective: Ride your motorbike into the frostlands]
Aemeath: You see that? Ancient life forms, frozen right into the ice walls.
Aemeath: Millennia, frozen in a single moment. Preserved so perfectly you can almost see what they used to be.
Aemeath: To be stuck like this forever... Kinda miserable, don't you think?

title: The Star That Voyages Far
subsection: Ride your motorbike into the frostlands
content:
Aemeath: To be stuck like this forever... Kinda miserable, don't you think?



???: Huff... Must be around here...
Rover: (Someone's ahead. That voice... I remember hearing it not long ago.)
Nivora: Hm? Y-you are the one who was talking to yourself in class…
Aemeath: Whoopsies...
Nivora: Oh, and Dr. Herssen! You are... traveling together? Did the Academy greenlight a new field trip?
Luuk Herssen: Just my routine checks on the field researchers. Rover here has their own business to attend to, but we're headed the same way.
Luuk Herssen: What about you, Ms. Nivora? Chasing more fallen debris?
Nivora: Yes! Exactly. I-I heard the frostlands have been experiencing changes since Helios was launched. I had a hypothesis that new debris fields might have been exposed!
Rover: Debris?
Nivora: Space equipment that fell from the sky long ago! Probes, satellites, and even space stations!
Nivora: Some previous digs unearthed wreckage containing records lost during the Lament.
Nivora: Oh, and images! Photos taken in orbit of other planets! They were absolutely, breathtakingly beautiful!!
Nivora: Huff... Huff. Oh, sorry, I-I got carried away...
[Dialogue Option]  It's okay. Passion is a good thing.
Nivora: Thank you… Sometimes, I'll just start info-dumping... I know it's not the best.
[Dialogue Option]  Hey. I'm into those things too.
Nivora: Really?! That's great! I'll... I'll show you the data I've collected next time we're in class!
Nivora: The universe… What secrets is it hiding beyond all those infinite stars?
Nivora: I really want to know.
Nivora: Anyway, in short, I came here for the fallen debris.
Nivora: The data on the instrument shows there's a high chance that close by… Huh?
Luuk Herssen: Run!

metadata.subsection: Ride your motorbike into the frostlands

title: The Star That Voyages Far
subsection: Ride your motorbike into the frostlands
content:
Nivora: The data on the instrument shows there's a high chance that close by… Huh?
Luuk Herssen: Run!



Nivora: I knew it! There had to have been undiscovered debris in this area!
Nivora: It must've been sealed in the ice wall all this time.
Rover: Luuk, Nivora. You alright?
Aemeath: Oh, I'm good! Perks of being a ghost, y'know.
Nivora: Ah! I'm so sorry... It's my fault for putting everyone in danger.
Rover: The collapse was an accident. We're all okay, so don't blame yourself.
Rover: But the way we came in is completely blocked.
Luuk Herssen: Scaling that ice wall… It's too high, too risky. I'd rather not have a student on that climb.
Luuk Herssen: I've contacted the Academy. They're sending a rescue team. Once Nivora's safely returned, we'll set out again.
Nivora: Mmm...
Aemeath: Hey, little guy here says our next stop is deep in the ice. There's a path at the bottom of the station. Wanna check it out?
Rover: What about waiting inside the station? It's freezing out here, and another collapse is possible. It's safer to wait for the rescue team indoors.
Nivora: I-I agree! I want to see what's inside too...
Luuk Herssen: With Rover on the team, a quick recon should be manageable. Up to you.
Aemeath: Hey, question. Before you came to Lahai-Roi, did you do this kind of thing a lot?
Rover: What do you mean?
Aemeath: Like traveling with a crew, seeing the sights, stumbling into trouble, then going your separate ways.
Aemeath: Like a classic road trip movie, you know?
[Dialogue Option]  Yeah, pretty much like that.
Aemeath: Nice. I happen to love those.
[Dialogue Option]  Usually more dangerous, though.
Aemeath: Oh, so more big-budget action? I can see that. Solaris is crazy.
Aemeath: Looks like this time I get a co-starring role. Amazing. Let's keep going, study buddy.

metadata.subsection: Ride your motorbike into the frostlands

title: The Star That Voyages Far
content:
[Objective: (Talk to Aemeath)]
Aemeath: It's kinda sad though, having to pick through fallen debris to advance our own tech.
Aemeath: It just shows... how much we truly lost in the Lament.

Nivora: There's a collapsed entry point over there, but… it's blocked. Some kind of barrier caused by unstable frequencies.
Luuk Herssen: The Exostrider sleeps in these frostlands. Void Storm activity can make local frequencies unstable with .
Luuk Herssen: Oh, taking this opportunity, Rover, let me grant you access to the … Hm? It's already unlocked.
Rover: (Hm? That must've been Lucilla.)
Luuk Herssen: Let's move to an area with a stronger signal so it can be deployed.

Luuk Herssen: This Module Adapter was developed by Startorch Academy for frostland expeditions. It lets you interact with frequencies disrupted by Voidmatter.
Luuk Herssen: Give it a try. You'll need it here.

title: The Star That Voyages Far
content:
Luuk Herssen: Give it a try. You'll need it here.



Luuk Herssen: Compared to other debris fields, this station is in much better shape.
Nivora: It's... amazing...

Rover: (Back in Mt. Firmament, I saw characters like this... they belonged to the Court of Savantae.)
Rover: (But I still can't make out what it's saying.)

title: The Star That Voyages Far
content:
Rover: (But I still can't make out what it's saying.)



Rover: This is...
Wenlu: Welcome aboard the SkyArk! I'm Wenlu, your guide for today's tour.
Wenlu: Teachers, please stay with your assigned groups and ensure this one-day tour goes smoothly.
Wenlu: Please direct your attention here. This containment unit holds droplets of the  itself!
Wenlu: As you know, the Etheric Sea suddenly appeared above Solaris one day.
Wenlu: During that initial event, the Court of Savantae briefly glimpsed a figure of a white-hair woman. She vanished in an instant, leaving countless puzzles in her wake.
Wenlu: What is the Etheric Sea? What does it do? And why does it appear?
Wenlu: The Court of Savantae conducts research here at  to seek answers to these questions.
Wenlu: Next, please scan your clearance with the system and follow me in an orderly manner.
Wenlu: We will now proceed to central deck. Awaiting us is this station's most significant breakthrough—a Mass Relay Device, powered by stabilized sample of the Etheric Sea.
Nivora: A sample of the Etheric Sea—? If it's part of the fallen debris, can it be... this research started before the phenomenon first appeared?
Nivora: Oh my, this is an... ABSOLUTELY... INCREDIBLE DISCOVERY!!! Thank my lucky stars I came to the frostlands today.
Luuk Herssen: That guide was probably a hologram frozen in the system's memory. Hah, those brillant minds in the Institute will be wetting themselves over this.
Aemeath: "One-day tour," huh? From the way she spoke, the visitors must've been school kids.
Aemeath: Guess hopping a shuttle into orbit wasn't a big deal back then.
Luuk Herssen: The containment unit looks custom-made, too. Transporting those samples safely would've been a massive logistical operation.
Luuk Herssen: A Court of Savantae space station, this is an exceptionally rare find.
[Dialogue Option]  How do you know how to operate the systems here?
[Dialogue Option]  How do you recognize the Court of Savantae's lettering?
Luuk Herssen: The Academy has recovered other debris from this era. The systems have enough common architecture for me to manage a basic reboot.
Luuk Herssen: As for the Court of Savantae's characters... let's just say I developed an interest in it under unique circumstances.
Rover: The characters on that pen, they're Court of Savantae letters.
Luuk Herssen: I obtained it by chance. In fact, it happens to involve you.
Luuk Herssen: But this isn't the place for that story. When we're back at the Academy, come by the infirmary. I'll explain then.
Luuk Herssen: After all... it is a long story.
Aemeath: Ooh, sounds mysterious! I wanna hear the story too. Please? Pretty please?
[Dialogue Option]  Depends on the situation.
Aemeath: Heh, I'll hang back and wait for my cue, then.
[Dialogue Option]  Like I could stop a digital ghost anyway?
Aemeath: Fair point. Don't forget I can even sneak into your Terminal!
Nivora: Everyone, this way please! The visitor registration system is here.

title: The Star That Voyages Far
subsection: Obtain your visitor's clearance from the SkyArk System
content:
[Objective: Obtain your visitor's clearance from the SkyArk System]
SkyArk System: Welcome aboard the SkyArk Space Station. It's an honor to share this vessel of knowledge with you as we journey across the stars.

Luuk Herssen: The clearance we got won't grant us access to the entire station. We'll need to register again later.
Luuk Herssen: Also, while the hull looks intact, the system is reading several parameters in the red.
Luuk Herssen: ...It could be the Etheric Sea's droplets effecting the surroundings, spreading through the station.
Luuk Herssen: That flowing sphere is the Mass Relay Device, with the Etheric Sea as its core.
Luuk Herssen: Let's check the console.

title: The Star That Voyages Far
