content:
Luuk Herssen: That flowing sphere is the Mass Relay Device, with the Etheric Sea as its core.
Luuk Herssen: Let's check the console.



Luuk Herssen: With the droplets dispersed, some space station sectors have become unstable.
Luuk Herssen: This Mass Relay Device shares the same origin as the droplets. It can stabilize them and also punch a corridor to other sectors.
Luuk Herssen: Incredible... that it has such capabilities...

Nivora: Ah, the hatch over there is back to normal...
Aemeath: Interesting... Feels different from how I usually move.

Aemeath: Pathway's blocked. Let's try the Module Adapter.
Aemeath: Look here!
Aemeath: Hello? Digital ghost, remember? Hacking this is easy!
Aemeath: "Welcome to Aemy Maps—!"
Aemeath: Wow! Solaris's rising star, everyone! What a leap!
Rover: Oh, come on...

title: The Star That Voyages Far
subsection: Use the Forceplex Board to follow Aemeath
content:
Aemeath: This track was used to transport experimental samples from space. The storage facility should be just ahead.



Wenlu: These containment unit hold star fragments and Etheric Sea Droplets, all collected in  by our very own Uncle Clemente, who just gave you a tour.
Wenlu: It's exhausting work. After each mission, he requires a full cycle in a recovery pod. Let's thank Uncle Clemente and then gather here.
Wenlu: Now, please welcome Project Director Junxi to give us an overview of the Etheric Sea Initiative.
Junxi: By now, you will have experienced our Mass Relay Device.
Junxi: It is our first major breakthrough and definitive proof of our theory that Etheric Sea can be utilized as a gateway.
Junxi:
Junxi: We haven't found the way yet, but I believe those obstacles will be solved soon.
Junxi: I have faith, not just in the Court of Savantae, but also in humanity's resolve to explore the stars, and in the budding curiosity I see before me.
Junxi: A mind that feeds on the light of distant stars will never be content to simply look. It will find a way to make the journey.
Junxi: Recently, a brilliant new mind joined . Her work was instrumental in developing the Mass Relay Device.
Junxi: Let's welcome Professor Weiying to share her vision—
Aemeath: A pity. His hopes never came true. Humanity's quest to reach the stars has only gone backward.
Aemeath: To feed on the light of stars... Pfff.
Aemeath: Venturing into the unknown beyond the Etheric Sea... Romantic idea. Though who says something ugly isn't waiting out there in the dark?
Luuk Herssen: Rover, over here. I found something interesting in the system logs.
Luuk Herssen: The station fell long ago, but according to this, the SkyArk System was briefly reactivated after years of silence.
Rover: Could someone still be alive?
Luuk Herssen: Not likely. We'd have found signs of life long before now.
Luuk Herssen: The activation sequence was used only to seal hatches and lock equipment. After that... nothing.
Rover: Can you see who activated it?
Luuk Herssen: Hold on... Yes. Clearance belonged to Clemente.
Rover: (The one who gathered the droplets...?)
Luuk Herssen: That's all I can pull for now, but the Academy will run a full investigation later. I'll keep you in the loop.
Rover: Good. Keep me posted.
Luuk Herssen: Shame the director's speech got cut off.
Luuk Herssen: I can't help but wonder what that colleague of his was going to say.

metadata.subsection: Use the Forceplex Board to follow Aemeath

title: The Star That Voyages Far
subsection: Obtain your visitor's clearance from the SkyArk System
content:
[Objective: Obtain your visitor's clearance from the SkyArk System]
SkyArk System: Welcome aboard the SkkkyyyArrrrrrk—
Luuk Herssen: The station's security grid is offline in this sector.
Luuk Herssen: The monsters... Voidmatter has made them highly unstable.
Aemeath: The frequency here is unstable too... Try using the Module Adapter to disrupt it.

metadata.subsection: Obtain your visitor's clearance from the SkyArk System

title: The Star That Voyages Far
subsection: Use the Forceplex Board to head deeper into the archive sector
content:
[Objective: Use the Forceplex Board to head deeper into the archive sector]
Aemeath: Look left!
Aemeath: I hacked the SkyArk System. This is the data archive sector. Those blocks are all storage modules.
Aemeath: And that moving one? An anomalous module gone hostile due to the SkyArk System's glitches.
Aemeath: Voidmatter levels seem to have risen...
Aemeath: It's moving deeper into the sector.
Aemeath: I'm on it!
Aemeath: Look! Lahai-Roi Blocks is complete!
Aemeath: In the Space Fantasy: Katya series, every copy included this mini-game. I love it so much! And I'm really good at it! Hehe.
Luuk Herssen: The anomalies here are more pronounced than before.
Aemeath: Rover, hang in there. I'm working on something in the SkyArk System!
Aemeath: Use the Adapter to disrupt these Error Modules!
Aemeath: Breach complete! Hey, Rover, do you know how to play rock-paper-scissors?
Aemeath: Good. Now, go "rock!"
Aemeath: Yeah! We won! Amazing play. Wish we could play another round of Lahai-Roi Blocks again!

metadata.subsection: Use the Forceplex Board to head deeper into the archive sector

title: The Star That Voyages Far
subsection: Head deeper into the archive sector
content:
[Objective: Head deeper into the archive sector]
Aemeath: These things are just like minions in the Space Fantasy: Katya series. I'll clear them out for you.
Nivora: Ah! Those modules fell and took out the hostiles...? Doesn't it feel like we've been extra lucky this whole way?
Luuk Herssen: You're right, but some modules did attack us. Hard to tell if the SkyArk System likes us or not.
SkyArk System: Welcome aboard the SkyArk Space Station. Your one-day tour has ended. Please follow your guide back to the central deck and log out of the visitor system in an orderly fashion.
SkyArk System: May we meet again among the stars.

Nivora: Uhhh, there are traces of Void Storm contamination everywhere!
Luuk Herssen: This concentration of Voidmatter should've flooded the upper decks by now. Could something be containing it down here?
Aemeath: Further in... Something's down there.

metadata.subsection: Head deeper into the archive sector

title: The Star That Voyages Far
subsection: Head deeper into the archive sector
content:
Aemeath: Further in... Something's down there.



Nivora: Huh?
Nivora: Ugh! That hurts...
Rover: Nivora!
Aemeath: Voidmatter saturation is critical! The SkyArk System is going into failure. I'm going in to try to stabilize it!
Luuk Herssen: Everything here has already been contaminated, including... that.
Luuk Herssen: From a doctor's perspective, the only healing left for what this man has become... is release.

metadata.subsection: Head deeper into the archive sector

title: The Star That Voyages Far
subsection: Defeat the Nameless Explorer - Deorbited Prisonoer in Shadows
content:
[Objective: Defeat the Nameless Explorer - Deorbited Prisonoer in Shadows]
Nameless Explorer: We... fell from the stars...
Nameless Explorer: Danger... Leave... This place...

metadata.subsection: Defeat the Nameless Explorer - Deorbited Prisonoer in Shadows

title: The Star That Voyages Far
subsection: Defeat the Nameless Explorer - Deorbited Prisonoer in Shadows
content:
Nameless Explorer: We... fell from the stars...
Nameless Explorer: Danger... Leave... This place...



Nivora: Ugh... Ah...
Luuk Herssen: Rover, I'll check her injuries. Will you patrol the area to make sure there are no more threats?
Rover: Got it. You go check on her.
Rover: (What's that...?)
Aemeath: The SkyArk System is stabilizing. Look! A log entry. Clemente. That must've been... the astronaut's name.
Aemeath: After he woke from his sleep pod many years ago, he initiated a lockdown that sealed in this entire wrecked sector, including himself.
Rover: The Void Storm had ripped through this sector. He must've been contaminated the moment his pod opened.
Aemeath: That command was a failsafe. He knew he was going to lose his mind, so he wanted to stop himself from reaching the upper decks and hurting anyone...
Aemeath: Tragic thing is, the  had already been down for years. There was no one left up there to save.
[Dialogue Option]  I think he already knew.
Rover: Even if his friends were gone, he might have thought of future explorers. Someone kind to children would've wanted to protect the innocent.
Aemeath: To wake from one long dream only to fall into a deeper nightmare... Maybe it would've been kinder to never wake up at all.
[Dialogue Option]  Maybe he didn't know.
Rover: There was nothing human left in him. But sealing himself away... that choice had to come from the man he once was.
Aemeath: I guess losing yourself in a dream where everyone's still alive is its own kind of comfort. It's not like... you can change reality.
Rover: (This file... It looks like a recording...)

metadata.subsection: Defeat the Nameless Explorer - Deorbited Prisonoer in Shadows

title: The Star That Voyages Far
subsection: Defeat the Nameless Explorer - Deorbited Prisonoer in Shadows
content:
Rover: (This file... It looks like a recording...)



(Cutscene plays)
Professor! Solaris's magnetic poles are shifting!
...Professor?
Look.
Someone's falling straight from the Etheric Sea!
(Cutscene ends)

metadata.subsection: Defeat the Nameless Explorer - Deorbited Prisonoer in Shadows

title: The Star That Voyages Far
subsection: Defeat the Nameless Explorer - Deorbited Prisonoer in Shadows
content:
Professor! Solaris's magnetic poles are shifting!
...Professor?
Look.
Someone's falling straight from the Etheric Sea!
(Cutscene ends)



Rover: (Was that... me in that recording?)
Rover: (That had to have been the station's final moments, when the " Phenomenon" suddenly spread and engulfed all of Solaris, like Luuk said.)
Rover: (But those droplets in the sky… that was . So that might've been an image of an event long ago, not part of the Etheric Sea Phenomenon itself.)
Rover: (Did I really fall from the Etheric Sea? Or what lay beyond it? Junxi did say the droplets could act as some kind of gateway.)
Rover: (Back then, could I have...)
Aemeath: Hm? What's up?
[Dialogue Option]  You look unhappy.
[Dialogue Option]  Are you angry about something?
Aemeath: Haha! Not at all.
Aemeath: I'm fine, Rover.
Luuk Herssen: I'd recommend you keep this private. Don't leave the recording for the Academy's teams to find.
Luuk Herssen: Remember what I said earlier? It's a nest of competing factions. Anything connected to your past needs to be handled with discretion.
Luuk Herssen: So, what do you think? Leader of the Black Shores.
Rover: (Very few people know about that.)
Rover: Be direct with me, Luuk.
Rover: I know you knew me before. But I acted mostly as a Bloom Bearer in the past.
Rover: You and I, what exactly are we to each other?
Luuk Herssen: Mm... friends, I'd say. Not the kind who lived in each other's pockets, but, as a Huanglong saying puts it, "True friendships are still waters that run deep."
Luuk Herssen: We met by chance, and by another twist of fate, you entrusted me with a rather long-term assignment.
Luuk Herssen: How about this: "Strangers in passing who became confidants." How does that definition suit you?
[Dialogue Option]  I need time before I can take your word for it.
Luuk Herssen: That's fine. Your work in Lahai-Roi won't be finished so soon, and we still have plenty of opportunities to reacquaint ourselves.
[Dialogue Option]  Fine... but more vague than I'd like.
Luuk Herssen: Heh, sorry, but it's the truth. We didn't spend much time together, but we got along instinctively.
Luuk Herssen: Startorch is a web of competing interests. If this video leaks, it'd create quite the cleanup operation.
Luuk Herssen: After your sudden exit years ago, people were lining up to unpack your history. Solaris's golden boy, forever a mystery.
[Dialogue Option]  Sorry for the trouble.
[Dialogue Option]  Thank you for handling the cleanup.
Luuk Herssen: Heh... You're not the same as when we first met. But let's save the reminiscing for later.
Luuk Herssen: Nivora's hurt. I've stabilized her, but as a doctor, I must stay to watch over her.
Luuk Herssen: From this point, you'll have to proceed alone. We'll wait here for the Academy's retrieval team.
Rover: Alright. I'll see you back at the infirmary.
Rover: Luuk, when you said I'm "not the same," what did you mean?
Luuk Herssen: Just my impression, I could be wrong. But you seem... lighter now.
Luuk Herssen: More hopeful. Happier.
Luuk Herssen: And that's... not a bad thing, Rover.

metadata.subsection: Defeat the Nameless Explorer - Deorbited Prisonoer in Shadows

title: The Star That Voyages Far
content:
[Objective: (Idle dialogue)]
Luuk Herssen: Hold on, Nivora. The retrieval team will arrive soon.
Nivora: Okay...

Aemeath: So our squad of four is now a squad of two... Oh wait, I don't really count, do I? Guess that makes it a solo squad now.
Aemeath: I once got accepted to work at a research outpost in the frostlands. I took a different route back then.
Rover: That's a surprise... I thought you'd prefer hobbies over field trips.
Aemeath: Well, I was really into Void Storms. Could count as a hobby, I guess.

title: The Star That Voyages Far
content:
[Objective: Go through the ice cave]
Rover: (Looks like a long way. Better take the bike.)
Aemeath: Let's follow the light ahead!

Aemeath: So it was here...
Rover: This is the research outpost you mentioned before?
Aemeath: One of them. I worked at several outposts back then. But this one wasn't so lucky. The scan shows it was hit by a sudden Void Storm surge. No survivors.
Aemeath: So that's why I never saw them again back at the Academy.
Aemeath: I thought I just didn't see them around.
Aemeath: Anything swallowed by the Void Storm slowly loses its "existence" until it's forgotten entirely.
Aemeath: If a Cassette makes it out, at least there's a record. But if that gets erased too, then even the fact that they died is erased.
Aemeath: Use the Core, Rover.
Aemeath: I want to see them again.

title: The Star That Voyages Far
content:
Aemeath: Use the Core, Rover.
Aemeath: I want to see them again.



Past Dazed Researcher: Aemeath, you were amazing! If not for you, that Glommoth would've crushed us to bloody pulp!
Past Dazed Researcher: I'm still shaking, but you're already cool as ice. Are all Synchronists from Rabelle College as composed as you?
Past Outgoing Roya: If you want to thank her, share your Void Storm research! To the frostlands came our little Aemeath for this curiosity. You should show her that thesis you've been writing for years!

title: The Star That Voyages Far
content:
Past Meticulous Researcher: Aemeath, you think Cassettes might be a breakthrough?
Past Meticulous Researcher: Hm, I'm not sure… Right now they're just for archiving. Actual transcription feels like a leap.
Past Gentle Roya: Try looking to the Exoswarm for inspiration. In Lahai-Roi, only one power against the Void Storm exists, and that all comes from the Exostrider.
Past Aemeath: Haha! Your thesis or your delicious stew, either works! I'm not picky!
Past Aemeath: As for the Void Storm… I'll try all your ideas. The problem is, we don't understand the Void Storm deeply enough.
Past Aemeath: Especially in the depths with high Voidmatter concentration. No probe survives the journey, so research is stuck. I can't shake the feeling that...

title: The Star That Voyages Far
content:
Aemeath: When I was a child, my parents were lost to a Void Storm. Soon after, I even forgot what they looked like.
Aemeath: So you see? Death hasn't been all bad!
Aemeath: Once I became a digital ghost, Voidmatter couldn't affect me anymore. Even if the whole world forgets my friends and colleagues, I still get to remember every single one of them.
Aemeath: Yep?
Rover: You don't always have to smile through everything.
Aemeath: What's that supposed to mean?
Aemeath: I'm happy. Really. It's the way I chose to live. You're too serious, always overthinking, hence the long face.
Aemeath: You wouldn't understand how happy this moment makes me.
Aemeath: Come on. I'll show you the frostlands' slumbering giant. Lahai-Roi's… Exostrider.

title: The Star That Voyages Far
content:
[Objective: Hop on your motorbike]
Aemeath: Ever since I became a digital ghost over ten years ago, I've stayed in Lahai-Roi. Can't get too far from the Exostrider.
Aemeath: You've been to many places, right? Care to share some stories?
Rover: Let me think...

(Cutscene plays)
...So the rain holding Jinzhou captive stopped, time began to flow again, and everyone got to celebrate a new beginning with the Moon-Chasing Festival...
Then you returned to the Black Shores, to the place that's always watched over you from afar.
Oh, and the archipelagos, Ragunna and Septimont... Aww, I just love how different these places feel!
It's all so wonderful. I love hearing these stories.
(Cutscene ends)

title: The Star That Voyages Far
content:
It's all so wonderful. I love hearing these stories.
(Cutscene ends)



Rover: It wasn't all smooth sailing. Plenty of emergencies along the way.
Aemeath: Still, it all sounds amazing. And I know you must care for some of the people you met.
Aemeath: Tell me, Rover, this journey you've been on since losing your memories… Have you been happy?
Rover: ...Yeah.
Aemeath: That's all that matters.

title: The Star That Voyages Far
content:
Rover: ...Yeah.
Aemeath: That's all that matters.



Look up
Rover: (This must be...?)
Aemeath: Ah... I knew the next stop would be here.
[Dialogue Option]  Why the sigh?
[Dialogue Option]  Why the long face?
Aemeath: The cabin up ahead. It's where I used to live with my family. I—
Aemeath: ...
Aemeath: Sorry. I just... I need a minute. I'm not ready yet.
Rover: (Just like before. The moment it appears, my frequency starts getting sucked out of me.)
Rover: (Aemeath said it's a Threnodian derivative, like the Voidworm. They share similar frequencies, but my gut says it's different.)
Sigillum: Go home.
Aemeath: ...!
Abby: What happened to you?!
Abby: Your frequency's been leaking everywhere! I tried plugging it from the inside, but it didn't work.
Abby: Eurgh! No, this is no good... How about this!
Abby: It stopped... it stopped... for now. I gotta... I gotta rest...
Rover: You did great, Abby. Go get some rest.
Aemeath: Don't you ever jump in after me like that again.
Aemeath: The Voidmatter concentration down there is too high. If you fall into Voidspace, even you could be consumed. Erased from existence.
[Dialogue Option]  I'm not so sure about that.
Aemeath: Always making people worry.
Aemeath: There's a theory in Lahai-Roi: Threnodian Aleph-1, the Devourer of Existence, is the embodiment of voidance. The dissolution of all things.
Aemeath: Its true form is like... a black hole.
Aemeath: And that theory is correct. I verified it myself.
Aemeath: So far, I'm the only one who's reached it. Because I'm already dead, and no living soul could withstand a place like that.
Rover: You went inside the Threnodian itself?
Aemeath: Yes. Think of a severe Void Storm as a manifestation and portal into Voidspace itself—A higher dimensional plane. It's pitch-black, but also like a kaleidoscope.
Aemeath: Inside, time and space aren't linear. Everything is warped.
Aemeath: Things the Threnodian devoured from different eras can be sitting right next to each other.
Aemeath: I know you fought many Threnodians, but Aleph-1 is different. It's already won elsewhere....
Aemeath: Wandering through the , I saw the proof... a graveyard of civilizations it's already ended.
Aemeath: The Threnodian's presence in Lahai-Roi is only a sliver of its true self. It's been trying to break through the seal on the  to devour Solaris.
Aemeath: So... Rover, don't go wandering off alone. Not until the Exostrider awakens.

title: The Star That Voyages Far
content:
[Objective: Follow Aemeath to the cabin]
Aemeath: Come, let's rest at the cabin.
Aemeath: I'll stay outside and keep watch. Just in case Sigillum comes back. You rest. Don't go anywhere, okay?

title: The Star That Voyages Far
content:
[Objective: Rest on the sofa]
You sit down, weakened by severe frequency loss. You've faced many dangers, but this exhaustion is different. It feels more like a chronic sickness wearing you away.
Darkness envelops you. After a brief rest, you wake up.
The room is empty. Aemeath hasn't returned.
---

title: The Star That Voyages Far
content:
[Objective: Investigate the cabin]
Rover: (I thought I remembered something before in the lake. I should look around this cabin while I wait for her to get back.)
Rover: (A game console. Two controllers. The screen is covered in dust. Hasn't been touched in years.)
Rover: (Space Fantasy: Katya VI, Split Stars... Most games here are RPGs or co-op games.)
Rover: (Childhood doodles. All telling stories of heroes saving the day...)
Rover: (Well. She had a... creative approach to art.)
Rover: (Stuffed toys. A big cat and a small cat. They look like they were well-loved.)
Rover: (So soft. You could probably hug these all night.)
Rover: (The Soliskin rushed towards the couch...)

title: The Star That Voyages Far
content:
[Objective: (Touch the paper plane)]
Rover: (Aemeath still isn't back, but if my hunch is right...)
Past Rover: Aemeath, have you been out terrorizing those  again? They scatter the moment they see you.
Past Rover: Keep this up, and it won't be long before there isn't anyone left in the frostlands to play with.
Past Rover: Have you finished your lessons? You start school soon. Maybe spend less time gaming, hm?
Past Aemeath: Nah-uh, they love playing with me! Why else would they crawl over and play before running away?
Past Aemeath: And my lessons—ahem, Rover, you promised me another level of Split Stars! No take-backs!
Past Aemeath: But... I want to learn how you folded that thing first. Can you show me? Pretty please?
Past Rover: You mean, the paper plane?
Past Aemeath: Yeah! Mine always nose-dives right away, but yours flew so far! How?
Past Rover: Hehe, well of course there is a trick to it.
Past Rover: I'll teach you. But first, you finish your lessons. Then we'll fold planes together, alright?
Past Aemeath: Aw, okay. You promise?
Past Rover: I promise. Cross my heart.
Aemeath: I've been wondering how to tell you this. And now...
[Dialogue Option]  We lived here together?
[Dialogue Option]  You can tell me now, Aemeath.
Aemeath: When I was little, I woke up one morning and realized I couldn't remember the sound of my parents' laughter anymore.
Aemeath: Their voices, their faces, their warmth... everything about them dissolved in the Void Storm.
Aemeath: Later, even the memory of forgetting them began to fade from my mind.
Aemeath: It terrified me... to the bone.
Aemeath: I didn't know how to fight it. I felt cold, and I knew I had to do something, anything, to make it stop.
Aemeath: So I ran away from Bjartr Woods by myself. I hid in the Starward Riseway and made my way to the frostlands.
Aemeath: My parents... One was a foreign researcher, the other a Roya. They were stationed here, during the Void Storm.
Aemeath: I wanted to return to where we once lived, but I couldn't remember the way. I stumbled around for so long... until I finally reached this lake.

title: The Star That Voyages Far
content:
(Cutscene plays)
Rover: Don't worry. Everything is okay now.
(Cutscene ends)

title: The Star That Voyages Far
content:
Rover: My past self saved you...
Aemeath: I was sinking into the lake. Choking. Everything was fading, until a pair of warm hands caught me.
Aemeath: They held on tight and pulled me out… and when I opened my eyes, I saw you.
Aemeath: But then I realized the talisman my parents had left me was gone. Probably lost to the deep. The thought alone broke my heart.
Aemeath: I cried so hard, and you had no choice but to scoop me up, comforting me as best you could. You took me back to your cabin to get warm.
Aemeath: And after that... Well, you guessed it. I stayed with you there, under your care, until the day you left Lahai-Roi.
Rover: Why did you keep this from me?
Aemeath: Because it would've been awkward.
Aemeath: Imagine someone you don't remember runs up to you, all smiles, saying, "Long time no see! I'm the kid you used to look after!"...Haha!
Aemeath: And what would I even say next? "Wanna go visit our old cabin?" "I listened to you and topped my class!" Or—"Yeah, I accidentally got myself killed, my bad!"
Aemeath: Saying any of that... would only burden you. You never asked for any of it.
[Dialogue Option]  I don't see it that way.
[Dialogue Option]  You've always felt familiar to me.
Rover: Since I woke in the Gorges of Spirits, I've met many people from my past. They've helped me recover pieces of myself. It's a good thing.
Rover: I can make my own choices. You should have a little more faith in me, Aemeath.
Aemeath: ...I see.
Aemeath: Then I'll just shoot away! My freshman speech, my first song release, the time I hit a new sync rate record. You missed all the big moments!
Aemeath: But I couldn't be mad. I knew you were busy.
Aemeath: You were always off saving Solaris from the Lament. You had to, and I do think that's a good thing.
Aemeath: So I thought, why can't I do the same? Look! I kept Lahai-Roi safe while you were away.
Aemeath: Sure, there was a cost. But not bad for your unofficial apprentice, right?
[Dialogue Option]  That cost was too steep.
Aemeath: The more you save, the steeper the cost. I've always known that. But some things, you just gotta do.
[Dialogue Option]  You did well. Really well.
Aemeath: You think so? Hearing that from a big ol' savior like you... Well, that's nice.
Rover: ...
[Dialogue Option]  How were you all those years?
[Dialogue Option]  How were you all those years?
Aemeath: You mean after you left? Well… pretty normal, I'd say. Went to school, enjoyed my days. Just like you wanted me to.
Aemeath: And then... I became a ghost. Since then, it's been drifting between the Academy and Voidspace.
Aemeath: See, there is a bright side! Dying gave me a free pass into Voidspace. I'd call that a win. Gotta explore somewhere, right?
[Dialogue Option]  There's something else I want to ask.
[Dialogue Option]  You really never saw me before?
[Dialogue Option]  There's something else I want to ask.
[Dialogue Option]  You really never saw me before?
Aemeath: Saw you? Oh, you mean that thing you brought up in class? About me helping you take down the Eye of the Threnodian?
Aemeath: Honestly, I don't remember a thing. But if the Threnodian was involved, it must've been in Voidspace.
Aemeath: Anyway, no clues from me. Threnodians having weird powers is nothing new. Or maybe you were just seeing things.
[Dialogue Option]  I have something else to ask you.
[Dialogue Option]  If that's really what you want, then...
[Dialogue Option]  I have something else to ask you.
[Dialogue Option]  If that's really what you want, then...
Aemeath: Hey, easy now. Just rest here tonight. We'll handle everything tomorrow when you're stronger.
Aemeath: Project "rebuilding myself" is going great. Once we reach the Exostrider and recharge with the Reactor, we can make for Sigillum and finish it for good.
Aemeath: I will take care of the problem for you.
Rover: We will face it together, Aemeath.
Aemeath: Of course! But for now, bedtime. You take your old room. I'll be in mine.
Aemeath: Kinda takes me back, saying good night like this. Just like old times.
[Dialogue Option]  Good night, Aemeath.
Aemeath: Good night!

title: The Star That Voyages Far
content:
Aemeath: Kinda takes me back, saying good night like this. Just like old times.
[Dialogue Option]  Good night, Aemeath.
Aemeath: Good night!



Young Aemeath: ...Huh? When did I fall asleep...
Young Aemeath: My paper plane, I have to show it to Rover...
Young Aemeath: Haaaah… I forgot to clean up my room before bed...

title: The Star That Voyages Far
subsection: Head to door before finishing tidying up
content:
[Objective: Head to door before finishing tidying up]
Young Aemeath: (It's really late now… If I go out, Rover will worry…)

metadata.subsection: Head to door before finishing tidying up

title: The Star That Voyages Far
content:
[Objective: Tidy up the room]
Young Aemeath: (This cat stuffy Rover gave me is so warm. I love cuddling it when I sleep.)
Young Aemeath: (Feels like he's right there with me.)
Young Aemeath: (Oh, nooo! I forgot to save my game! That was my best score ever...)
Young Aemeath: (Next time, I'll definitely beat Rover's record! I'll show him!)
Young Aemeath: (I drew my favorite story! The challenger fighting the dragon, and the lone hero battling the evil galactic empire!)
Young Aemeath: (But… I can't get the colors of their clothes right. Oh well, I'll just ask Rover to help me later!)

title: The Star That Voyages Far
subsection: Sit down and rest on couch
content:
[Objective: Sit down and rest on couch]
Young Aemeath: (I wonder… how long will Rover stay this time? I wish he didn't have to go deal with all those annoying people...)
Young Aemeath: (How tiring to have to work so hard every day…)
Young Aemeath: (…Ugh, but he never listens! I'm just gonna talk him ear off while I can!)

metadata.subsection: Sit down and rest on couch

title: The Star That Voyages Far
content:
[Objective: Find that person]
Past Rover: Ah, Aemeath... What's wrong? Can't sleep?
Young Aemeath: Are you sad right now?
Past Rover: No. Just... thinking about some things.
Young Aemeath: Hmph, you're lying! You are sad!
Past Rover: You see right through me, huh? I'm not sad, I just...
Past Rover: Well, to put it in your words, I guess I'm thinking about my homeland.
Young Aemeath: Then… do you wanna go back for a visit?
Past Rover: I can't go back.
Young Aemeath: Why?
Past Rover: ...
Young Aemeath: Can I tell you a secret, Rover? After Mom and Dad went away, my chest always felt all tight and heavy.
Young Aemeath: When people in the tribe talked to me, their voices always sounded really far away.
Young Aemeath: But that day at the lake... after I cried in front of you, the feeling got a little smaller. I didn't feel so bad.
Young Aemeath: I know you can't say this stuff to other people. 'Cause they all think you're super strong.
Young Aemeath: But I'm just a kid! And I don't think you're that strong! So, if you need to cry, you can cry with me. I'm really good at keeping secrets.
Young Aemeath: So, you don't have to be sad by yourself. Okay?
Past Rover: My homeland is far, far away, Aemeath.
Past Rover: The people there gave me a mission. That's why I came here.
Young Aemeath: Hm… what kind of mission? It must be really important to come so far.
Past Rover: It's complicated. Too complicated for you right now.
Young Aemeath: Then just pick a simpler way to say it! I'll listen really carefully.
Past Rover: A simpler way...
Past Rover: Put in terms of your Space Fantasy Katya games... I came here to save the world.
Past Rover: To do whatever needs to be done to fulfill the mission, for as long as it takes.
Past Rover: But was it the right thing for me?
Past Rover: Because one day I realized I would never return home.
Past Rover: I couldn't stop thinking about that faraway place. More than I ever had before.
Past Rover: In what you'd call dreams, I'd go back. Stand there, just stare at what I once called my homeland...
Past Rover: Even if staring didn't change a thing. Even if it was pointless.
Young Aemeath: Oh! I see!
Young Aemeath: You miss home, Rover!
Past Rover: Maybe.
Past Rover: But… talking with you makes it not so bad.
Past Rover: There's still a lot I have to do in this world. This won't stop me. Don't worry about me, Aemeath.
Past Rover: Yeah?
Young Aemeath: I'm your family too. Until you find your real family and can go back to your homeland, I'll be right here with you!
Past Rover: Sounds good.
Past Rover: Thank you, Aemeath.
Aemeath: Ha, a dream of the old days.
Aemeath: Homeland...

title: The Star That Voyages Far
content:
Past Rover: Sounds good.
Past Rover: Thank you, Aemeath.
Aemeath: Ha, a dream of the old days.

content:

[Dialogue Option]  Always ready.
[Dialogue Option]  I'll need a moment.

Aemeath: Hard to say. There's no precedent for my situation. It's all just theory.
Rover: But what if it works? What would you want to do then?
Aemeath: Hmm, haven't decided! But I'm definitely going on a proper tour of the Academy!
Aemeath: If that happens, can you come with me?
Aemeath: Look. It's sleeping.

content:

Aemeath: Look. It's sleeping.

Aemeath: Once I find more pieces of my existence here, I'll be strong enough to face Sigillum…
Aemeath: We take that thing down, and this is all over! Alright, let's race full-speed ahead to the finale!
Sigillum: Hand over...

content:
[Objective: Pursue Sigillum]
Sigillum: ...Complete...
Rover:  (It's throwing up barriers to block my path.)

Sigillum: Make... whole.
Rover: (Need to find a way out of here first.)
Rover: (Sigillum isn't just after the Reactor Core, it's targeting my frequency and Aemeath's piloting control of the Exostrider as well.)
Rover: (What exactly is it planning?)
Aemeath: Enough! No more of this stupid idea, Sigillum!

Aemeath: If destroying you is the only way to protect Rover...
Aemeath: Then so be it.

Aemeath: Not while I'm here. Don't even think about it.

title: The Star That Voyages Far
content:
Rover: (And then there's the Stridergate. There must be a connection.)



Aemeath: It's already speaking more clearly now. I can't let it drain any more of Rover's frequency.
Aemeath: Gotta pull it inside. Gotta end this for good.

Memories of the Stars
Vast, boundless space erodes all sense of time, where endlessly repeating moments hold equal weight. The long voyage has yet to reach its end, and the coordinates of the starting point have long since worn away.
Infinite possibilities collapse into a single next instance—still a miracle by any name, with no need to return.

Rover: Are you alright, Aemeath?
Aemeath: All good. Inside the Exostrider, I'm the one in control.
Aemeath: I'll destroy Sigillum. So, just go. Stay away from it, okay?
Aemeath: Please, I'm begging you.
Sigillum: Why refuse?

title: The Star That Voyages Far
content:
[Objective: Defeat Sigillum]
Sigillum: So lonely.
Sigillum: Open the Stridergate.
Aemeath: Shut up!
Sigillum: Go.
Sigillum: Home.
Aemeath: I said—
Aemeath: SHUT UP!
Aemeath: THAT IS NOT HOME.
Aemeath: I won't allow anyone...
Aemeath: To harm Rover.
Aemeath: Don't worry. It will end soon.
This mission has become an eternal shackle.
Rover: What exactly are you hiding from me?
Aemeath: You don't need to know, Rover. I will protect you.
Rover: Aemeath, haven't you noticed you're not yourself right now?!
(Cutscene plays)
Sigillum: Did you forget your own homeland?
(Cutscene ends)

World of Sighs
The sighs of that person still linger here. O you who are bound in chains, to whom could you ever confide such endless sorrow?

title: The Star That Voyages Far
content:
[Objective: Search for Aemeath]
Rover: (Aemeath and Sigillum are gone.)
Rover: (Is this Aemeath's old dorm? Since she can resonate with the Exostrider, even after her body was destroyed, her frequency must have merged with it.)
Aemeath: Goodbye.
Rover: (A photo album.)
You open the album to photos of Aemeath with her classmates.
You can tell she's a girl of many passions: ice-fishing in the frostlands with friends, splurging at markets, battling it out in the arcade...
But away from the camera's focus, Aemeath seems elsewhere. Quiet. Lost in thought.
At the very bottom, you find a photo of you with her as a child. Its edges are soft, creased, and worn from handling.
Rover: (A poster of Fleet Snowfluff's fan meeting.)
The poster is neatly stuck to the wall, but the bottom-right corner hasn't fully adhered. You lift it gently and see something scrawled messily on the back.
"I'll do anything. Guess that means I don't really care about anything."
"Singing, piloting the Exostrider... It's all the same. I don't care."
"But saving the world... will I ever see the day?"
Aemeath: I'm Aemeath. The Academy's star. A Synchronist. A savior.
Aemeath: Please, look at me!. (Don't look for me)
Aemeath: Piloting the Exostrider... Heh, it doesn't matter to me.
Aemeath: But if this is what it takes to lighten Rover's burden, and ease his pain...
Aemeath: Saving the world... Heh!
Aemeath: Nothing but a pair of shackles. Heavy, eternal shackles.
Aemeath: No, he can't ever know this.
Aemeath: I must... keep this secret. Bury the truth deep.
Aemeath: Why...
Aemeath: It hurts...
Aemeath: What should I do...
The One Who Sighs: I can't go back.

title: The Star That Voyages Far
content:
[Objective: Talk to Aemeath]
[Dialogue Option]  Why are you laughing?
Aemeath: Oh, are you talking to me?
Aemeath: I just heard the most hilarious story. Couldn't help myself!
Aemeath: Since you asked, how 'bout I tell you?
The Star That Voyages Far - Cat Savior.png
Aemeath: Once upon a time, there was a black cat who set out to save the world.
Aemeath: Why? Because everyone told the cat it was a savior!
Aemeath: The cat didn't get it. When it opened its big golden eyes, it was just stuck in this tiny cardboard box.
Aemeath: And inside that tiny box? It was crammed full of even tinier little creatures! The cat was shocked. It had to tiptoe around, careful not to step on anyone.
Aemeath: These tiny creatures, even living in their tiny box, had so much misery. So many disasters. Constantly just waiting for the other shoe to drop.
Aemeath: "Please save us!" they begged the cat. And, of course, the cat agreed.
Aemeath: Even if they hadn't asked, the cat would've helped anyway. Because that's who the cat believed it was: a savior!
Aemeath: And so, the cat took up its sword. Always fighting, always talking, always roving...
Aemeath: Saving the world, over and over. Until one day, it realized the cardboard box had been sealed shut.
Aemeath: Hahaha! Isn't that kind of laughable?
[Dialogue Option]
Aemeath: Right?! It's just a cat! Why did it have to do all of that?!
[Dialogue Option]  I don't think it is.
Aemeath: Where's your sense of humor! Isn't it absurd? The sheer ridiculousness of everyone ignoring the fact that it's just a cat?
Aemeath: But in such a laughable story, somehow, everyone else gets to be happy.
Aemeath: The ones who relied on the cat, the ones who hated the cat, they all got exactly what they wanted.
Aemeath: But what about the cat?
The Star That Voyages Far - Aemeath crying.png
Aemeath: It wants to go home, but no one remembers. The box is sealed shut, and the ones who put the cat in there have already turned their backs on it.
Aemeath: Even the cat itself has forgotten.
Aemeath: Heh... isn't that... so absurdly laughable?

title: The Star That Voyages Far
content:
Aemeath: Even the cat itself has forgotten.
Aemeath: Heh... isn't that... so absurdly laughable?



Aemeath: My head's been loud.
Aemeath: There's this question that just spins and spins up. I still don't have the answer.
Aemeath: Now that you're here, I want to ask you what you think.

title: The Star That Voyages Far
content:
Aemeath: Now that you're here, I want to ask you what you think.



Aemeath: That person is my family.
Aemeath: Family us supposed to look out for each other. Protect each other.
Aemeath: So I want to do something for him.
Aemeath: He doesn't say it, but I can see it. All the stuff piled up inside him.
Aemeath: The more you hide, the less you share.
Aemeath: But I saw Rover recently. And I think he seems more carefree than before.
Aemeath: The sunlight in Jinzhou, the flowers in the Black Shores, the winds of Rinascita... He told me all about this new journey.
Aemeath: It made me happy. Truly happy for him.
Aemeath: I guess... forgetting can be a blessing. If you don't remember something, it can't hurt you.
Aemeath: So I started thinking, maybe I shouldn't tell him what I saw in Voidspace.
Aemeath: All that pain he carried about him home, it's gone now. Why bring it back?
Aemeath: If not knowing is happier, why ruin it?
[Dialogue Option]  But people need to know the truth.
Aemeath: Even if the truth destroys that happiness? I... I can't. I don't want to see him hurt.
[Dialogue Option]  You're right. Happiness is what matters.
Aemeath: Right? Happiness is so fragile. It should be protected.
Aemeath: I want to protect Rover.
Aemeath: We all need a little hope to keep going, right? I want him to hold onto that hope.
Aemeath: What Sigillum said is unnecessary.
Aemeath: It's been feeding on Rover's frequency, trying to complete itself, spouting things that should have stayed unsaid—things that would ruin his peace.
The Star That Voyages Far - Aemeath hiding the truth from female Rover.png
The Star That Voyages Far - Aemeath hiding the truth from male Rover.png
Aemeath: I must destroy it before it spills the truth.
Aemeath: I brought it into this world. I'll be the one to take it out, too.
Aemeath: Nothing truly matters. Not even saving the world.
Aemeath: But you have to believe what you're doing has meaning. That's the only way to keep moving forward.
Aemeath: And that's why...

title: The Star That Voyages Far
subsection: Leave the classroom and stop Aemeath
content:
[Objective: Leave the classroom and stop Aemeath]
(Triggered after activating the designated mechanism.)
Rover: Stop, Aemeath.
Aemeath: I told you to stay out of this.
Rover: I know you did this for me. To protect my happiness. And I'm grateful. But it's over now.
Aemeath: ...
Rover: I need to hear it. All of it. Whatever the truth is, it's my burden to carry. My choice to make.
Aemeath: ...
Rover: Carrying this on your own hasn't been easy, has it?
Aemeath: Do you really want this? Even if it changes nothing? Even if... it only weighs you down?
Rover: Things only weigh on us because they matter.
Aemeath: Alright then.
Aemeath: Back when we lived together, you once told me you'd come from a faraway place. That you were on Solaris to carry out a mission.
Aemeath: Current research suggests the Exostriders and Sentinels were made with technology from the same civilization. I think that civilization... is the faraway homeland you spoke of.
Aemeath: You never spoke of it to me or anyone else again. So I kept it to myself... until I died and slipped into Voidspace as a digital ghost.

metadata.subsection: Leave the classroom and stop Aemeath

title: The Star That Voyages Far
subsection: Leave the classroom and stop Aemeath
content:
Aemeath: You never spoke of it to me or anyone else again. So I kept it to myself... until I died and slipped into Voidspace as a digital ghost.



(Cutscene plays)
Aemeath: As I wandered through the ruins devoured by the Threnodian, I stumbled upon a faint frequency. Your frequency.
Aemeath: Time is chaotic inside Voidspace. There's no telling when it had been devoured.
Aemeath: But... I could feel your warmth in it. After so long without you, I couldn't let it go. I kept it with me.
Aemeath: Guided by its strange connection to other frequencies, I traced my way through countless overlapping spaces until I found the remains of an Exostrider.
Aemeath: That was when I realized that Exostriders were built to transport Sentinels.
Aemeath: They trekked through stars to deliver Sentinels to Solaris. Until, during one jump, the Threnodian Aleph-1 must've noticed them.
Aemeath: Its hunger had festered for so long that not even devouring the entire universe could sate it now.
Aemeath: That frequency then led me to another relic consumed by the Threnodian—a creation built by the same makers of the Exostriders.
Aemeath: It was beyond my understanding. I could only guess its purpose: a communication satellite.
Aemeath: And within its ruined shell, I discovered frequencies tied to you.
Aemeath: From those fragments, I saw the messages you sent home. Not about your mission, but full of longing.
Aemeath: You said you wanted to go home. Even if just to lay eyes on it, one more time.
Aemeath: But their reply was... a rejection. Because it wasn't part of your mission. Because it was "unnecessary."
Aemeath: They were the ones who cut communications! They ignored every wish you had outside your mission! They forced you into this life of roving!
Aemeath: And still, you... you...
Aemeath: You crossed the stars to fulfill their wish! How could they... HOW DARE THEY TREAT YOU LIKE THAT?!
Aemeath: In that moment, I was... drowning in pain.
Aemeath: I didn't know how to help you. I didn't know if I should tell you. I didn't know what future you'd even want.
Aemeath: That's when your frequency I'd been carrying with me... it was corrupted by the Voidmatter. It tore through my power, and Sigillum was born.
(Cutscene ends)

metadata.subsection: Leave the classroom and stop Aemeath

title: The Star That Voyages Far
subsection: Leave the classroom and stop Aemeath
content:
(Cutscene ends)



Aemeath: It was born from my mind. From all my worries, my fears, everything I imagined you'd suffered.
Aemeath: At first, it acted on nothing but instinct to go home.
Aemeath: It craved your frequency, trying to make itself whole, trying to seize access to my piloting control...
Rover: ...So it could reactivate the Exostrider and cross the Stridergate to get back home.
Aemeath: Exactly. The more of your frequency it consumed, the more coherent it became. I couldn't let you hear those words, so I... I tried to destroy it.
Aemeath: This is what I've been keeping from you... I'm sorry.
Rover: I'm glad you chose to tell me this, Aemeath.
Rover: Hearing this... it's a lot to process. I'd be lying if I said it wasn't.
Rover: I just need time to figure out my next move. This "homeland" of mine, even saying it feels strange to me.
Rover: But don't worry. The journey I've had since losing my memories, the hope I found... that's mine to keep. No one can take that.
Rover: "Saving the world"... I never saw it that way. The people and civilizations I met, they saved themselves. I was just there to help.
Rover: Jinzhou's soldiers fought through Retroact Rain till dawn.
Rover: The Black Shores Bloom Bearers ran themselves ragged across distant lands.
Rover: Rinascita's factions all dared to defy the Dark Tide.
Rover: Lahai-Roi's people never stopped reaching for the stars.
Rover: I'm no savior who fell from the sky. And no one ever saved themselves by waiting for one. There's been plenty I couldn't do. Losses I couldn't prevent. Sacrifices I had to accept.
Rover: But I'd do it all again. Every bit of it.
Rover: If this was a mission from my past, I'd be lying if I said I didn't care what they thought of me now. But that's a question for later. Right now, we have more important threats to face.
Rover: The fact that I'd choose this path even without my memories. That tells me this is who I am. I can't stand by while the Lament brings suffering. I care about this world too much.
Aemeath: But... I'm afraid you'll feel alone.
Rover: With everyone here? With you here? Not a chance.
Rover: I will be there for everyone... As we head toward our shared future, leaving the past behind.
Aemeath: ...

Rover: I will be there for everyone... As we head toward our shared future, leaving the past behind.

Sigillum: So, this is your (my) choice.
Sigillum: Is it worth it?
[Dialogue Option]  I'll decide the worth of this mission, not them.
[Dialogue Option]  The meaning of the path ahead is mine to decide.
Rover: I know where I'm going now. That's what matters, not where I started.
Sigillum: Then keep going.
Sigillum: No matter what.
Aemeath: The Core... it's returned to the Exostrider. It's one step closer to finally awakening.
Rover: And you? Your power should be restored now that Sigillum is gone.
Aemeath: It's more than restored. The Core's return has rebuilt my frequency from the ground up. I'm a full Exostrider Resonator now.
Aemeath: My original body is still gone, of course. I'll always be a ghost in the machine. But my "existence" is now strong enough to be detected.
Aemeath: It's like a faint current turning into a bright, flickering spark!
Rover: So will others be able to see you now?
Aemeath: That's right! Guess our little road trip movie's come to an end. Time to head back to Startorch Academy. Together!

content:
Aemeath: That's right! Guess our little road trip movie's come to an end. Time to head back to Startorch Academy. Together!



Luuk Herssen: All good on your end, golden boy? Lucilla mentioned the Exostrider in the frostlands just moved. Please tell me that was you?
Rover: That was Aemeath. Given how well you know me, I assume you know her, too.
Luuk Herssen: You found her?
Rover: I brought her back to the Academy. It's a long story. I'll fill you in when there's time.
Luuk Herssen: Understood. But I do have to ask, on Lucilla's behalf: what's the status of the Core?
Rover: It was returned to the Exostrider.
Luuk Herssen: That explains it. The Research Institute is reporting a spike in Voidmatter concentrations over Lahai-Roi. Void Storm activity is kicking up again.
Luuk Herssen: Back when the Reactor Drive was in the sky, its annual self-diagnostics caused the Exostrider's Greatsword pointed at the Threnodian to weaken.
Luuk Herssen: The Exostrider is probably running the same procedure now to integrate what you returned. Best for you both to stay within the Academy until peak season passes.
Rover: Alright, I'll be careful.
Luuk Herssen: Next time you're in the infirmary, we should revisit your old plan. The one tied to the Exostrider, the Stridergate, and the Threnodian.
Luuk Herssen: For now, just be with Aemeath. It must be a great relief to have her back. I'm happy for you.
Luuk Herssen: You've earned a break, Rover. Get some rest.

Rover: Why do I feel like someone's about to get in trouble when you talk like that?
Aemeath: Hey! That's a totally unfair stereotype from when I was a kid playing with !

[Dialogue Option]  It sure does.
[Dialogue Option]  Your fans would lose their minds.
Aemeath: I know, right! You have to come too!
Aemeath: You have to see this star perform, Rover! Forget all your worries for a night and just enjoy the young energy of Startorch Academy!

title: The Star That Voyages Far
content:
Hey, what's this? Have you seen it before?
Looks like a fan meeting poster.
Fleet Snowfluff... Interesting name. Let's go check it out!



Aemeath: For years, the little website I threw together to post songs kept getting comments.
Aemeath: They'd talk about how much they loved a song, or share problems they were having in their lives. And then... they started connecting with each other.
Aemeath: I never saw myself as a hitmaker. I was just an amateur, singing what was in my heart.
Aemeath: But over time, they stopped being just my songs. They became... a melody that connected people.
Aemeath: If my listeners want a complete song, I'll finish it for them. Or maybe for me, too.
Rover: You really do care about the people of Lahai-Roi, don't you, Aemeath?
Aemeath: I guess I do now. Wouldn't have said that at the start, though.
Aemeath: To be honest, I never had some grand passion. Before I became a ghost, I just wanted to live an easy, happy life and try a little bit of everything.
Aemeath: And my whole "I want to be a savior" thing? Well, that was just me trying to copy you.
Aemeath: But after I died, I had all this time. Time to notice the people and things in Lahai-Roi I'd overlooked before.
Aemeath: So many people here dream of becoming stars themselves, but that was never my dream.
Aemeath: I'd rather be the one who looks up at the stars. The one who watches over them.
Rover: Really? But the way I see it...
[Dialogue Option]  You're already shining like one.
[Dialogue Option]  You've already watched over Lahai-Roi
Rover: Go on then, Aemeath. I want to hear you sing.
Aemeath: You'd better! 'Cause you're my most important audience today.
Aemeath: But first… hmm, you need a better look for the show.
Aemeath: There! Brand new, just like I remember you wearing. Looks good, right? A new place calls for a new look.
Aemeath: Ah, this brings me back...
Aemeath: I remember when you used to wear this around the Academy. You'd leave a whole trail of swooning admirers in your wake, Solaris's great savior!
[Dialogue Option]  ...
[Dialogue Option]  Alright, that's enough out of you.
Aemeath: Haha! What, are you blushing? Since when is having charm a bad thing?
Aemeath: Now, go grab that seat over there. Best view in the house. I scouted it myself back when I used to nap through lectures.
Aemeath: As for me, it's showtime.

We're here sharing the same time and space
In your eyes
the sparks look like
thousands of bright stars I have gazed at for thousands of time

Our dreams glowing brightly

The stream of shimmering daily moments returned weight to my soul
And stopped me from drifting
Gave my feet the solid ground to stand
So let's sing together
Every light I'm giving all comes back to you
comes back to you

Joyful Fan: I'm getting her autograph later! Of all the songs she's posted online, my favorite is "Indigo Universe." What's yours?

Shocked Fan: B-because she was the social butterfly of the Academy! The professors' headache and their golden student all in one!
Confused Fan: I still don't see why that's upsetting. It all sounds great to me.
Shocked Fan: Her song "Fallen Petals"...after hearing it, I always picture Fleet Snowfluff as a tender, gentle soul. But now...
Confused Fan: Umm... I mean, she never really seemed that way from her online replies? Maybe your impression of her was a little too personal?

title: The Star That Voyages Far
content:
[Objective: Listen in]
Steady Fan: Aemeath from Rabelle College. She's been missing for years. Why would she be here?
Curious Date: Aemeath? The same one Professor Sakya always talked about?
Steady Fan: Yeah. She always wanted her as a mentee. She still brings her up to us.
Steady Fan: "I thought the biggest problem would be that little rascal refusing to finish her studies, or me finally losing my mind from her antics. I never thought she'd just... vanish."
Steady Fan: Professor Sakya is going to be over the moon to see her.
What are you doing?

title: The Star That Voyages Far
content:
Aemeath:  You know, I found something interesting in the Exostrider's Reactor Drive.
Aemeath:  A message left by my future self.



Aemeath:  Years ago, while sailing the stars toward Solaris, an Exostrider caught the attention of Aleph-1.
Aemeath:  Both of them tore through the Stridergate, clashing in the caverns deep below.
Aemeath:  The Exostrider has combat features, but it was still no match for Aleph-1.
Aemeath:  Its body was shattered, energy nearly depleted. And Voidmatter kept pouring through the Stridergate. Aleph-1 kept pushing, desperate to squeeze its whole disgusting bulk into this world.
Aemeath:  It was almost successful. It would've ended everything.
The Star That Voyages Far - Aemeath emerging from the Threnodian.png
Aemeath:  But then a girl named Aemeath emerged from inside the Threnodian itself. The great savior, making her dramatic entrance at the final moment!
Aemeath:  The Exostrider watched her touch its greatsword, the one pinning the Threnodian. Their resonance sent a surge of power back into the Reactor Drive.
Aemeath:  It turned the massive blade, forcing the Threnodian back through the Stridergate and driving a seal over it.
Aemeath:  But the human girl who had resonated with the Exostrider? She was dragged through the Stridergate with the Threnodian, vanishing from Solaris forever.
Rover:  (Aemeath was the key? She helped the Exostrider seal the Threnodian?)
Aemeath:  I was shocked at first. But the moment I stepped into Voidspace it all made sense.
Aemeath:  This distorted, black hole of a realm where time and space are warped... it appeared when the Threnodian came to Solaris.
Aemeath:  Anything lost inside can exist in multiple moments at once. Things caught in it can be thrown into junctures of time they were never part of.
Aemeath:  And I… I can move through it all. The Voidmatter can't touch me!
Aemeath:  Haha... Do you have any idea what this means?
Rover:  (Aemeath, where is this going?)
Aemeath:  It means…
The Star That Voyages Far - Aemeath's Time Loop Female Rover.png
The Star That Voyages Far - Aemeath's Time Loop Male Rover.png
Aemeath:  Time, cause, effect, a perfect, closed loop. But my meeting with Rover all those years ago.... that wasn't the cause. It was the effect.
Aemeath:  Only by resonating with the Exostrider and dying as a Synchronist all those years ago, could I later become the Exostrider's true Resonator as a digital ghost.
Aemeath:  And only in this form could I cross Voidspace, return to the past, and power the Exostrider to save Lahai-Roi.
Aemeath:  And only because Lahai-Roi survived, could Rover have ever come here, rescue my younger self, and let me grow up here to become the chosen Synchronist in the first place.
Rover:  (No, I have to get Sigillum to move! I need to stop—)
Aemeath:  Only I can do this. It has to be me. Just like Rover, I can't turn away from a responsibility like this.
Aemeath:  There's just one thing. One last wish.
Aemeath:  Just one more time, I want to…

title: The Star That Voyages Far
content:
Aemeath: For over ten years now, I've tried the same thing.
Aemeath: Every time the Reactor Drive ran its self-diagnostics during peak Void Storm season, I tried to reverse time. And every time, I failed. I just wasn't strong enough.
Aemeath: But now, further along the timeline, the edges of Voidspace are beginning to collapse. I don't know why the Threnodian is changing, but I know there won't be another chance.
Aemeath: I have to make the jump now, during this peak season, while Voidspace is still stable.
Aemeath: I'm not that child who needed protecting anymore. I have a duty to fulfill. Lahai-Roi is my responsibility.
Aemeath: So if I can help, I will. I have to.
Aemeath: But before I go… I want to see him again. That's my one, selfish wish.
Aemeath: I want to talk to him. To know how he's really been. I want to spend a little more time with my family.
Aemeath: I was always afraid that when He finally discovered the truth about himself, he'd feel so alone.
Aemeath: But... it's alright now.
Aemeath: He told me about his journey after losing his memories. It was… meaningful.
Aemeath: He met people. People who care for him. Who miss him. People He formed connections with.
Aemeath: So even knowing the truth about his homeland now, He won't be alone. He has a reason to keep living.
Aemeath: That's enough for me. Now, I can finally... let go.
Aemeath: You…? How…?

title: The Star That Voyages Far
content:
Etheric Sea - A planet-wide phenomenon born from an anomalous Lament event. It now blankets Solaris's sky. Research suggests it is composed of extremely high-density Remnant Energy. Since its appearance, all of Solaris's space exploration has been brought to a complete standstill.
Fluctuating Voidmatter Levels - A phenomenon unique to the surface of the Roya Frostlands. Scholars theorize that this anomaly emerged when the Threnodian's power there attempted to devour the Exostrider, triggering abnormal Voidmatter transformations. Affected objects enter a state of unstable "existence," becoming impossible to observe directly.
Retroact Rain - High-density Remnant Energy from the Etheric Sea that projects past events with uncanny fidelity. The Retroact Rain unfolds in three distinct phases: natural descent, near-ground suspension, and reverse flow.
Module Adapter - A specialized device developed by the Spacetrek Collective for research operations in the Roya Frostlands. It forces entities with fluctuating Voidmatter levels back into the observable state for practical use. In areas with stable signal coverage, the device can be deployed directly to the user's location.
SkyArk Space Station - A Court of Savantae space station launched into near-Solaris orbit before the Etheric Sea fully enveloped the planet. Its primary mission was the study of Etheric Sea Droplets, research intended to pave the way for further space exploration.
Snowfluff Seal - A species of seal native to the Roya Frostlands, named for its snowball-like, round, white body. Docile in nature, Snowfluff Seals show little reaction to people or their surroundings, spending most of their time either eating or lying still. Only when facing extreme danger will they rear up and bare their fangs as a deterrent. If intimidation fails, they will promptly retreat to a safer area.
Stridergate - The entry point formed when the Exostrider and the Threnodian Aleph-1 entered Solaris. Researchers in Lahai-Roi widely believe it leads to outer space. The overlying Soliskin root network holds Aleph-1's power at bay, the "sealed doors" of the Stridergate.
Voidspace - A high-dimensional domain embedded deep within high-density Voidmatter, existing "inside" Aleph-1. The fundamental laws of time and space descend into total chaos here. Any living entity entering this domain suffers a rapid loss of frequency, eventually leading to the total dissolution of their existence.
