title: Starlights from Yesterdays
subsection: Leave the Research Institute and head for the Dimmr Plains
content:
[Objective: Leave the Research Institute and head for the Dimmr Plains]
Lucilla: Here. This is the Dimmr Plains map, updated with the latest intel.
Lucilla: Be mindful of the contamination. It's not just the Exoswarm or local lifeforms being affected. It's sealing off the terrain itself.
Lucilla: That said, where there's a will, there's a workaround. Hiyuki found one, though it took her some time.
Rover: That miko?
Lucilla: Yes. She's been investigating the Dimmr Plains in secret. You'll meet her there.
Lucilla: She also asked me to tell you that she's run into the Fractsidus there, including the missing girl, Denia.
[Dialogue Option]  Why would she want me to know that?
Lucilla: Mm... let's just say honesty is in her nature.
Lucilla: She just thought you might want to know. Perhaps her way of showing she has no hidden agenda?
Rover: Noted. I'll be leaving then.
Lucilla: Wait.
Lucilla: Look me in the eyes.
[Dialogue Option]  ...Lucilla?
Lucilla: Relax. It's my Forte. You've seen it before.
Lucilla: I will temper this moment into a bullet of memory, carved with your name, your face, and all you have been.
Lucilla: What carries you is not only your own strength.
Rover: Thank—
Lucilla: Uh. Save that for when you come back.

title: Starlights from Yesterdays
content:
[Objective: Follow the white bird]
Rover: (...Where is it leading me?)
Rover: ...Someone there?
Hiyuki: She hasn't gone far. Probably watching us from the shadows.
Rover: She seemed... like her grip is slipping.
Hiyuki: She was already like this when I last encountered her. Shortly before the Voidmatter surge.
Rover: Hiyuki, when you fought Denia, did you see anything like a shadowy hand?
Hiyuki: Yes.
Rover: (Then Denia was behind the incident beyond the Stridergate.)
Rover: (Could she also be responsible for the Academy's Voidmatter surge...?)
Hiyuki: Lucilla contacted me. She said you intend to return beyond Stridergate.
Hiyuki: The roads here have been swallowed by Voidmatter. There is no direct passage.
Hiyuki: Lucilla must have told you of the rift that appeared over a decade ago. Thinking back now... that was likely the Fractsidus's doing.
Rover: (Luuk said the Grand Architect caused that rift. That... was what led to Aemeath's death in the simulator cockpit.)
Rover: If they used a Threnodian frequency extracted from here to influence Denia... then the Spacetrek Collective was already infiltrated from the beginning...
Hiyuki: The Threnodian's surge now could be their attempt to force the girl to master that power.
Hiyuki: Or... perhaps that power within her has simply broken its leash.
Hiyuki: Long ago, I sealed a portion of my own power there to help aid the Solvein Heartwood resist the Threnodian.
Hiyuki: Break the seal, and you will pass through the rift to reach the Voidmatter depths beyond it.
Rover: Understood. I'm relying on you.
Hiyuki: Let's go. Time isn't on our side.
Hiyuki: Savior... who has always walked with victory. This time, have you come to save Lahai-Roi?

title: Starlights from Yesterdays
subsection: Head to the seal that Hiyuki left behind
content:
[Objective: Head to the seal that Hiyuki left behind]
Rover: Do you know Denia?
Hiyuki: Lucilla asked me to watch over the students. I observed her. She did act strangely at first...
Hiyuki: But in time... I could see her effort to belong. She did seem happy at the Academy.
Rover: Have you been watching over Denia here?
Hiyuki: Yes... After I sensed the Threnodian's breach, I sent my Shiratori to trace it. That led me here, to her, in the Dimmr Plains.
Hiyuki: She remains under the Fractsidus's sway, but her actions just now betray her own will.
Hiyuki: She always hid in the Void Storms. I have no wish to harm her… So I did not find the right moment to intervene.
Hiyuki: Wait here. This seal is wrought from the "Futures' Tithe." To put it simply, I drew upon countless versions of my future self and anchored them here to suppress the Voidmatter.
Hiyuki: To break the seal is to reclaim those futures. That task is mine alone.
Rover: I understand. I'll leave it to you.
Hiyuki: There is one thing... with Aleph-1 active, I may not be able to restore this seal once it is broken.
Hiyuki: You choose the most perilous path at the most perilous time.
Hiyuki: I know your strength. I know your history of victory.
Hiyuki: To take such a risk… is it because you remain confident you will not fail? That you cannot lose to the Threnodians?
Rover: No. I've failed before. I don't think anyone can win forever.
Rover: If I'd never lost, maybe... I'd still have my memories. I wouldn't need to start over and Solaris would be free from the Lament.
Rover: I do this because I can. And because someone has to.
Hiyuki: And what if you fail...?
[Dialogue Option]  Then you evacuate immediately.
[Dialogue Option]  Then Duskveil will proceed as planned.
Hiyuki: I meant what becomes of you?
Rover: Maybe I'll be lost to Voidspace. Maybe I'll find a way to turn the tide. I can't know right now.
Rover: But if I don't try, there's no way I'll ever know.
Rover: What makes me scared isn't coming up short. It's the thought of not giving it my all.
Hiyuki: The cost of this attempt is steep, and you bear the weight of many. I expected more caution.
Hiyuki: To fail even once against a Threnodian is to invite apocalypse.
Hiyuki: Even knowing this... you would still go?
Rover: Hiyuki. Lucilla told me you fought a Threnodian in Ashinohara for a long time.
Rover: I don't know how you did it, but I can only imagine what it took to hold the line in a place already so destroyed. So I'll ask you...
Rover: Did you fight in Ashinohara because you were certain you would win?
Hiyuki: ...No. I was not.
Hiyuki: I never was.
Rover: Then you understand why I'm doing this. You would make the same choice in my place.
Hiyuki: I see.
Hiyuki: I will attend to the . It will not take long.

title: Starlights from Yesterdays
subsection: Head to the seal that Hiyuki left behind
content:
Rover: Hiyuki!
Rover: Let me help!
Hiyuki: No need. I must do this myself...
Grand Architect: Oh… Why not choose the easier future?
(Cutscene ends)



Hiyuki: The girl...
Grand Architect: It's been a while, Miko of Flaming Sakura. And you as well, Rover.
Hiyuki: I burned my future as a Threnodian Resonator. Your plan holds no meaning now.
Grand Architect: Every step in our dance has its purpose, Lady Miko.
Grand Architect: Our paths have crossed often, but in my design, this is our true introduction to each other.
Grand Architect: Because at last, I have a "masterpiece" worthy of your attention.
Rover: You infiltrated the Collective for Denia and Hiyuki. You wanted  Leviathan's power... to merge them into one.
Grand Architect: Denia was always a Fractsidus creation. She is honored to be used as intended.
Rover: A creation...?
Grand Architect: The Mya disappointment made me think. If I could just create a superior vessel, one refined by a Miko's spirit, perhaps it might bear the full might of a Threnodian's power.
Grand Architect: As for the outcome... you would know better than I, Lady Miko.
Hiyuki: ...Wordplay won't change your failure. Leave, you tedious avatar.
Grand Architect: Failure? No. Listen you two, I'm just showing Solaris another "possibility."
Grand Architect: If we made one Denia, we can make another. And another. Until we hold a complete, obedient Threnodian Resonator in our hands.
Grand Architect: Your own borrowed future showed you that. A true Threnodian Resonator will exist.
Denia: Help... help me...
Grand Architect: Tsk, tsk. All that desperate running on the wheel, and you still came up short. I'll have to throw you away.
Denia: ...
Grand Architect: She can deny it all she likes, but the void in her heart is the same as Aleph-1's. That emptiness... it will always pull her toward the Threnodian's power.
Grand Architect: Chase her if you must. You do so love playing the "savior," Rover.
Grand Architect: As for this avatar... I'll spare you the trouble.
Rover: Wasting time on one of their avatars is pointless...
Rover: Come on, Hiyuki. The seal is open. We have a job to do... Denia needs us.
Hiyuki: If you wish, I can tell you about my history with the Fractsidus. But of course, Denia is the more pressing matter.
Rover: It's not hard to guess... The Grand Architect wanted your power as the Miko of Flaming Sakura, didn't they?
Rover: But like you said, you burned that one future as a Threnodian Resonator. You can be done with them.
Rover: Right now, Denia's state is what worries me.
Hiyuki: I fear... that child may already be...

metadata.subsection: Head to the seal that Hiyuki left behind

title: Starlights from Yesterdays
content:
[Objective: Find Denia]
Denia: Can't... go inside...
Hiyuki: Rest now.
Hiyuki: Do not worry. The Voidmatter frequency within her has weakened. She will recover.
[Dialogue Option]  Thank you for looking after her.
[Dialogue Option]  Good. That handles things here.
Hiyuki: Forgive me, but I believe waiting for the Voidmatter to spread would take too long. This will be faster.
Hiyuki: Allow me to handle this. There is not much time left in your deadline with Mr. Chase.
Hiyuki: My Shiratori can guide you through Voidmatter, but the concentrations here go beyond its strength.
Hiyuki: So I will draw upon a future where I learned to fully channel its power.
Hiyuki: It will protect you and help you find the path you seek.
Hiyuki: The rest... is yours to face.
Rover: Thank you, Hiyuki.
Hiyuki: Rover, I've read the Spacetrek Collective's report on Aemeath.
Hiyuki: She wrote that her intention is... "Saving the world."
Hiyuki: Lucilla said you are her family. I suppose you must be the reason she held that vision.
Hiyuki: Do you regret it? Leading her to the "savior's" path? To a life of pain and struggle?
Hiyuki: One must walk this path alone in order to protect.
Hiyuki: And those who walk it out of admiration will lose themselves in the mire...
Rover: No, Hiyuki. I don't seek Aemeath to confess my regrets.
Rover: I want to find her, so I can tell her...
Voice from the Silence: I hope to make you proud. I hope I haven't let you down...
Rover: I've always been proud of her.
Rover: She chose to walk this path with me, so I know I'm not alone. Should I ever fail, I know there will be someone who'll continue to protect Solaris.
Hiyuki: With your extraordinary strength, that is indeed possible.
Hiyuki: But for those who are too weak to save others, there is only futility waiting at the end.
Hiyuki: ...As I learned when I failed to save Ashinohara.
Hiyuki: All I can do now is hold my Suzu tightly, to ensure that after Hiyuki... there will be no more Miko of Flaming Sakura.
Hiyuki: That... is all that remains.
Rover: From Lahai-Roi to the distant lands of Jinzhou and Rinascita, people rise up to fight the Threnodians.
Rover: I've been part of that fight. But to pretend I'm the only reason they're standing? That everything fails if I do? That's arrogance. It's an insult to everyone else choosing to stand their ground.
Rover: My victories were never mine alone.
Rover: If even one person makes it to the end of this road, then we're still winning.
Rover: Hiyuki. When you're walking alone and feel that weight... Just stop for a moment. Look around.
Hiyuki: Stop...
Rover: You'll see that there are people who draw strength from you. People out there who are proud of you.
Rover: And when you finally reach the end of your journey, you'll know it was never futile.
Hiyuki: ...How enviably brilliant.
[Dialogue Option]  Huh?
[Dialogue Option]  Come again?
Hiyuki: It is nothing. I will tell you when you return.
Rover: All right. I'll be back soon.
Hiyuki: I will hold the line here until Duskveil initiates. I will wait for you... together with everyone.

title: Starlights from Yesterdays
content:
Rover: All right. I'll be back soon.
Hiyuki: I will hold the line here until Duskveil initiates. I will wait for you... together with everyone.



(Cutscene plays)
Exostrider...
Someone consumed by Voidmatter...?
Come here. The Exostrider's power is nearly spent, but I'll do my best to protect you.
This frequency...
No. Your existence is already nearly—
"Where... am I?"
"Did the Void Storm consume me? Am I... dead?"
"Is this Voidspace? A higher dimension?"
"Our existence... is fading..."
"Did you just say that time and space... have no meaning?"
"Who's speaking?"
"I can't see you... but I can feel you."
"Sound doesn't travel here. But thoughts do."
"The Exostrider?"
"Why is the Exostrider here?"
"What happened?"
"The light?"
"...What should we do?"
"What are you doing?"
"This is meaningless."
"That's enough!"
"It's futile..."
"Our lives already ended in the void."
"I heard the Exostrider's cry for help (frequency). I want to find it."
"Time and space don't mean a thing."
"You'll never reach it."
"I know what the Exostrider means to Lahai-Roi, but..."
"You want to save it? How?"
"Nothing makes sense here!"
"..."
"But I... we..."
"We made it to the stars to reach for the unknown, didn't we?"
"Just another step on a long road of discovery."
You...
"This is where we came from."
A spacetime coordinate with the Exostrider as the origin? But that's impossible inside a black hole...
"Now, we will mark the past with the future."
...Thank you.
You charted the unknown with your lives. I'll make sure it's not in vain.
The light of the Origin Point... We (The Exostrider and I) will bear it.
Aemeath?
I'm here.
Aemeath, can you bring the Drive Replica here? It's the "heart" they built for the Exostrider.
Don't worry. This time, we'll save the world together.
...Okay. I'll bring you back humanity's hope.
So... wait for me.
(Cutscene ends)

title: Starlights from Yesterdays
content:
Exostrider: Alert: Arbiter. Mech ascension complete. Systems at peak. Ready to reengage enemy.
Aemeath: Exostrider... you're awake?
Exostrider: Assessment: A "human heart" is now operational within me. I can now speak with their voice.
Exostrider: In frostlands where civilization should not have taken root, a collective will was born. A will to explore what lies beyond.
Exostrider: They... have chosen me.
Aleph-1 (Voice of the Cosmos): Annihilation... Certain. Voyage... Futile. Beginning... Will?
Exostrider: Directive: I voyaged here to fulfill my mission. Life on this planet has the right to explore the vastness of the cosmos.
Exostrider: You see the civilizations across the stars only as food to quiet your hunger. You cannot comprehend the will that drives them.
Aleph-1 (Voice of the Cosmos): The end... Void. Meaning... Suffering...
Exostrider: Opinion: Even if humanity's final frontier is an endless void, it is not proof of a meaningless pursuit, Aleph-1.

title: Starlights from Yesterdays
content:
Exostrider: Opinion: Even if humanity's final frontier is an endless void, it is not proof of a meaningless pursuit, Aleph-1.



Exostrider: Confirmation: Battle concluded. Voidmatter responses within this sector have dissipated.
Aemeath: But... Threnodian Aleph-1 wasn't destroyed.
Exostrider: Analysis: Resonator Aemeath. Under current parameters, the permanent termination of Aleph‑1 is impossible.
Exostrider: Therefore, I exercised autonomous judgment and exiled it to the furthest reaches of this universe.
Exostrider: Request: Arbiter, permission to remain. Before your final judgement, allow me to submit a log of my experience in Lahai-Roi.
[Dialogue Option]  Go ahead.
Exostrider: Log Retrieval: On multiple return transits, I was detected by Aleph‑1. It pursued me, its objective to enter Solaris through the Stridergate.
Exostrider: It attacked. I fell... but Resonator Aemeath answered me with her power, and I was able to banish a part of Aleph-1.
Exostrider: I should have initiated a full system seal to await repairs. But I saw countless pairs of terrified eyes.
Exostrider: Discovery: The Roya in the frostlands stood helpless before the Threnodian's Voidmatter calamity.
Exostrider: I saw panic and dread. Following the protocol shared with the Sentinels, I extracted my Reactor Drive and encased it deep within the ice. Then I powered down to slumber.
Exostrider: Exception: A momentary reactivation occurred. Resonator Aemeath resonated with me a second time.
Exostrider: She required my power to mend the Stridergate rift. I complied.
Aemeath: That was when I became a digital ghost. But was that the "second time" we resonated... or the "first"?
Exostrider: Initial Assessment: Upon reactivation, standard procedure was to request your retreat. Direct engagement with Aleph-1 was a tactical irrationality.
Exostrider: But the "human heart" granted me a voice. The will of this civilization gave me the strength to stand with you.
Exostrider: Component Analysis: This Drive Replica forged by humans is crude and fragile compared to my original Drive.
Exostrider: I can feel each one of its pulse cycles. Violent, eroding itself with every beat.
Exostrider: The shrill, grating friction of wear...This is the first time I have ever heard "myself." A heartbeat bestowed upon me by "them."
Exostrider: With this heart installed, I have acquired capabilities previously undocumented outside the Sentinel mech series.
Exostrider: Projection: Given Threnodian Aleph-1's abilities, we must assume it retains the capacity to return.
Exostrider: Once the Stridergate is fully sealed, I will remain on this side as its guardian. I will bar its re-entry into Solaris.
Exostrider: Request: Arbiter. I was born from humanity's hope. Please permit me to remain here and protect them until this heart ceases to beat.
[Dialogue Option]  ...Very well. Permission granted.
Exostrider: Query: Resonator Aemeath. Are you willing to accept a portion of my power?
Exostrider: When I first arrived in Lahai-Roi, your assistance allowed me to seal the Threnodian beyond the Stridergate.
Exostrider: Your current state is a consequence for which I bear responsibility. While I slumbered, you safeguarded Lahai-Roi in my stead.
Exostrider: Now, the death that once drew near has been severed. Henceforth, your companion will be an enduring "life."
Exostrider: Summary: I am experiencing the state defined as "guilt."
Aemeath: Hah! Oh Exostrider, you're really wearing your "heart" on your sleeve, aren't you?
Aemeath: But hey, I chose this path myself. Made my peace where it ends a long time ago.
Aemeath: As for your question... This savior's got a career to uphold. Gotta level up if I'm gonna keep kicking bad guy butt, right?
Aemeath: So your power? Hell yeah, I'll take it.
Exostrider: Authorization: Resonator Aemeath's agreement confirmed. Synchronization limit removed. Commencing Resonance.
Aemeath: Suggestion: Don't you dare feel "guilty." Thank you for living up to my hopes. So... let's make our goodbye a happy one, okay?
Exostrider: Detection: Arbiter. You have brought your Cassette.
Exostrider: Proposal: Please, allow me to take it. I wish to burn a frequency onto the tape, for you to return to Lahai-Roi.
[Dialogue Option]  What frequency is that?
Exostrider: Briefing: While traversing the stars at high velocity, my trajectory once intersected with a slow-moving probe.
Exostrider: Its hull was marked with Solaris script. Its launch date is estimated to have occurred a long time ago.
Exostrider: I intercepted and recorded the signal it has been continuously transmitting to Solaris. Its name is "The Farwatcher."
Exostrider: Objective: I wish to offer this recording as a gift to the people of Lahai-Roi.
Exostrider: Status: Stridergate closure imminent. Preparing to return the Arbiter and Resonator to Lahai-Roi.
Exostrider: Query: One last thing, Arbiter. Will you permit me to alter my designation to bear the name "Lahai-Roi"?
[Dialogue Option]  Of course.
Lahai Roi: Designation change complete. Thank you, Arbiter.
[Dialogue Option]  Why?
Exostrider: Objective: I wish to always be reminded of my heart's origin.
Rover: As you wish.
Lahai Roi: Designation change complete. Thank you, Arbiter.
Lahai Roi: Valediction: Farewell, Arbiter. Please deliver my temporary goodbye to the people who forged this heart.
Lahai Roi: Prediction—We will meet again in the boundless sea of stars.
[Dialogue Option]  Until we will meet again, in the boundless sea of stars.

title: Starlights from Yesterdays
content:
Lahai Roi: Prediction—We will meet again in the boundless sea of stars.
[Dialogue Option]  Until we will meet again, in the boundless sea of stars.



Aemeath: It's been so long since I last saw Solaris. Feels weirdly nostalgic.
Aemeath: Now that Aleph-1's been kicked to the cosmic curb, Lahai-Roi can finally breathe easy.
Aemeath: I was gonna say we saved the world this time. But honestly...
Aemeath: It was the explorers who fell into the Voidmatter. They're the ones who mapped that data on me and the Exostrider inside the Threnodian's black hole. All I did was burn their findings onto a Cassette for you.
Rover: And it was the people of Lahai-Roi who decoded the Cassette and forged the Drive Replica. That's what let the Exostrider finally cast the Threnodian out.
Aemeath: So... this wasn't a story about heroes saving the world. It was the world saving its heroes. Right?
Rover: Yes. And now… we're home.
Hiyuki: You're back?
Rover: Yeah, I'm back now.

title: Starlights from Yesterdays
content:
Rover: Yes. And now… we're home.
Hiyuki: You're back?
Rover: Yeah, I'm back now.



(Cutscene plays)
Spacetrek Collective Broadcast: During Aleph-1's recent activity, impact was successfully contained to the Dimmr Plains.
Spacetrek Collective Broadcast: Within the Plains themselves, Voidmatter concentrations have dropped significantly across most sectors.
Spacetrek Collective Broadcast: Monitoring data from the Spacetrek Collective confirms that Threnodian markers within the region of Lahai-Roi have now fallen to near-zero levels.
Spacetrek Collective Broadcast: Exostrider activity has fully ceased. However, related research into its technology will continue.
Spacetrek Collective Broadcast: Mech units deployed by Startorch Academy have successfully neutralized all anomalous constructs activated by the Threnodian across Lahai-Roi.
Spacetrek Collective Broadcast: The experience gained through this mission will carry forward.
Spacetrek Collective Broadcast: In Bjartr Woods, the area closest to the Threnodian's attempted breach, partial structural damage has been confirmed. Overall, the situation remains well within control.
Spacetrek Collective Broadcast: As Voidmatter levels continue to drop, the Roya will regain access to a broader and more stable range of territory.
Spacetrek Collective Broadcast: Once shrouded in Voidmatter, Lahai-Roi now stands restored. This was made possible by the choice of every last explorer.
Spacetrek Collective Broadcast: The road ahead is vast. We will reach the stars. And then, we'll keep going.
(Cutscene ends)

title: Starlights from Yesterdays
content:
Spacetrek Collective Broadcast: The road ahead is vast. We will reach the stars. And then, we'll keep going.
(Cutscene ends)



Aemeath: You made it!
Aemeath: Turns out, decoding what the Exostrider burned into your Cassette was way tougher than the Institute thought. They only just finished today!
Lynae: Over here, Rover! Everyone's waiting for you!
Sigrika: What could it possibly be... Oh, I can't wait to find out.
Lucilla: The Farwatcher.
Lucilla: I have to admit, Rover, I was genuinely surprised when you handed me this tape and said that name.
Rover: You said it was one of the nine interstellar space probes launched before the Etheric Sea engulfed Solaris.
Lucilla: Correct. The nine stars on the Spacetrek Collective's emblem represent those probes.
Mornye: Ever since then, Solaris never received another signal from them. Not a single one.
Mornye: ...Until today.
Lucilla: Professor Mornye, you may begin playback.
Lynae: This... Sounds like white noise...
Mornye: Judging by the Cassette's data, they're sounds the Farwatcher recorded while drifting through different galaxies.
Lucilla: Sounds that have been lost to us for centuries, silenced by the Etheric Sea.
Rover: So that's why... the Exostrider wanted to give these recordings to the explorers of Lahai-Roi today.
Aemeath: Because this is a gift from light-years away. Sent by the explorers of Lahai-Roi's past...
Aemeath: ...Echoes from the sea of stars.

title: Starlights from Yesterdays
content:
Aemeath: Because this is a gift from light-years away. Sent by the explorers of Lahai-Roi's past...
Aemeath: ...Echoes from the sea of stars.



Cristoforo: The Spacetrek Collective has taken in that Denia girl. Just as you wished, Grand Architect.
Grand Architect: Good. Just let them care for the little doll for now. Such an extraordinary performance. I'm sure I can find another role for her later.
Voice: All retrieved data has been processed. Awaiting review at your leisure.
Voice: May I ask what you plan to do next?
Grand Architect: Plans are progressing everywhere it seems. I've dallied in Lahai-Roi long enough. Time to stretch my legs.
Grand Architect: Cristoforo, be a dear and run a message to Eris in the New Federation for me.
Cristoforo: Understood. Though I suspect the Vice Architect will begrudge, once more, your sending me to disturb their precious quiet.
Cristoforo: Oh... and will you require me to draft a prologue for your characters?
Grand Architect: No need. I'll pay Phrolova a visit myself first. That will be all for now. This body tires so easily. Remember to give her a silent ending...
Voice: Grand Architect, with this phase of verification complete and full production proceeding… do we still have use for that miko?
Grand Architect: That won't be necessary. Her future as a Threnodian Resonator has been taken. She no longer requires our attention.
Grand Architect: Besides, she's failed one too many times. Drawn one too many futures from herself. And she still insists on walking the path of saving Ashinohara alone, with no intention of stopping.
Grand Architect: Every step she takes only deepens that obsession.
Grand Architect: After countless cycles of failure, she too will be reduced to ashes by her own vow. Just like her sister.
Grand Architect: Ah... that reminds me. Zashiki‑warashi has brought us some rather interesting news.
(Quest complete: Starlights from Yesterdays)
(Obtained Trophy: A Savior Is Everyone)

title: Starlights from Yesterdays
subsection: (One time interaction) North-West, end of the road from Ginnungamere Resonance Nexus
content:
[Objective: (One time interaction) North-West, end of the road from Ginnungamere Resonance Nexus]
Aemeath: Hehehe, look who's here... Now be good. Pats incoming!
You see Aemeath crouching near some Snowfluff Seals. Her smile is soft as she reaches out to ruffle the fur on one of their heads.
The Snowfluff Seals look dazed, their eyes squinted as they remain still, as if knowing resistance is futile by Aemeath's aura alone.
[Dialogue Option]  Are you messing with them again, Aemeath?
[Dialogue Option]  They don't dare budge an inch...
Aemeath: Puh-lease. This is just how we get along!
Aemeath: By the way, why didn't you message me on WavesLine before coming all the way here? I could've picked you up.
[Dialogue Option]  Just felt like dropping by.
[Dialogue Option]  I'll message you next time.
Rover: Are you looking at where Lahai-Roi (the Exostrider) disappeared?
Aemeath: Yeah... I don't know. I feel a bit conflicted about it.
Aemeath: It's still out there, beyond the Stridergate. Guarding this world all alone, day after day. It's gotta be wearing down. Who knows how much longer it can hold on.
Aemeath: Can't help worrying... What if it just breaks down one day?
Rover: I think, before that day comes, the people of Lahai-Roi will find a way to cross the Etheric Sea.
Rover: We already promised "Lahai-Roi" we'd meet again in the boundless sea of stars, right?
Aemeath: Haha. When you put it that way, I do feel more confident. That's our Savior of Solaris for you.
Aemeath: You're right. We  will  meet again someday.
Aemeath tilts her head in thought, then smiles at you.
Aemeath: Since you're here, why don't we head back home to rest for a bit?
Aemeath: I'm fine, obviously. But you're probably freezing in this wind.
Aemeath: Come on! A quick nap does wonders, I promise.

title: Starlights from Yesterdays
subsection: (One time interaction) Returned to the Cabin with Aemeath
content:
[Objective: (One time interaction) Returned to the Cabin with Aemeath]
Aemeath: Us lounging on the couch, doing nothing, listening to the snow fall outside... It's nice, isn't it?
Aemeath: I come back every now and then to tidy up. That's why it always feels kinda lived-in.
Aemeath: Soft couch, fire crackling in the fireplace, neat bookshelves... See, I haven't just got my saving the world thing under control. I'm taking care of my home life, too.
Aemeath: Pretty impressive, right?
[Dialogue Option]  Yeah, our Aemeath is something else.
[Dialogue Option]  I'll give you credit for that.
Aemeath: Hehe...
Aemeath: I think this little place is perfect now. When you're tired, you've always got somewhere to come back to.
Aemeath: See? You're already looking sleepy.... Nap for a bit? If you're worried about missing something, I can wake you up later.
[Dialogue Option]  That'd be great, Aemeath. Thanks.
[Dialogue Option]  (Close your eyes)
With Aemeath's gentle humming nearby, you drift into a light, peaceful sleep.
In your dream, the spring sun warms the windowsill of your home. Your family is there beside you, and for a moment, everything is as it should be.

title: Starlights from Yesterdays
subsection: Cabin in Ginnungamere - Pernament as of 3.4
content:
[Objective: Cabin in Ginnungamere - Pernament as of 3.4]
Aemeath: Welcome home!
Aemeath: I came back to spend the night, and here you are! Talk about being in sync, huh?
Aemeath: No matter how nice other places are, there's nothing like sleeping in your own bed. If you'd come any later, I'd already be asleep!
Aemeath: Since we're both awake on a snowy night like this, wanna... tell me a bedtime story? Just like old times.
Aemeath: What kind of stories have you picked up on your travels lately? C'mon, tell me! I really wanna hear.
[Dialogue Option]  (Tell a story of joy.)
Aemeath: Aww, that's how it should be! Gotta be enjoying the view, no matter where you go. That's what counts.
Aemeath: Besides, that's exactly what road-trip movies are all about. Looking forward to the next stop, but always soaking in the sights along the way.
Aemeath: Next time, bring me a souvenir? Hehe, I want something YOU picked out yourself. Something you think is worth keeping!
[Dialogue Option]  (Tell a story of anger.)
Aemeath: ...Really? Someone actually upset you that much?
Aemeath: Well, I'm committed to this whole savior thing, but I can drop that for you.
Aemeath: Whenever you need me, I'm here. So... Rover, do you want me to take care of those annoyances for you?
[Dialogue Option]  (Tell a story of sadness.)
Aemeath: I see... So that's what happened.
Aemeath: Like I've said before, you're just like everyone else. You don't have to carry more than your fair share... even though you always do.
Aemeath: If you're hurting and need a shoulder to cry on, that's okay. I'll be right here. Always.
You share your joys and sorrows with Aemeath, and her expressions shift with your words—delight and anger, excitement and concern.
The sights from your journey become easy conversation. In this quiet haven, the noise of the world fades away.
Outside, snow drifts down in whispers. Inside, spring has made its home.

subsection: (One time interaction) Ceased Court, West from Sealed Fissure Resonance Beacon
content:
[Objective: (One time interaction) Ceased Court, West from Sealed Fissure Resonance Beacon]
Rover: What are you doing...?
At your voice, Hiyuki stops her quiet muttering and discreetly closes her fingers around a note in her hand.
Hiyuki: Some of the Threnodian's influence has yet to fully fade. The Spacetrek Collective wishes to gather more intelligence as well, so I will accompany them. From the shadows.
Hiyuki: Their people conduct field surveys here during the day. At night, with fewer eyes about, it is easier to clear away the "debris." Easier to draw a blade, too.
[Dialogue Option]  You're doing this alone?
Hiyuki: I am sufficient on my own.
[Dialogue Option]  If you want my help...
Hiyuki: Do not worry. This is how I have always done things.
Hiyuki: There are greater tasks that require your attention, and more people who need you. Matters such as swinging a blade… leave those to me.
Hiyuki: Truly. If I need it, I... I will ask you for it.
Hiyuki: Aleph-1 made me understand the strength that lies in "everyone".
Hiyuki: I was foolish in the past. I believed I had to bear everything alone, or else I would be unworthy of this power.
Hiyuki: But how far can one person truly walk alone? Not nearly as far as when all move in step.
Hiyuki: If I can do a little more before I depart, I will do it. Though sometimes,  what they gather to discuss is difficult to follow...
Rover: Scientific jargon?
Hiyuki: They know I am nearby, so some request protective charms and talismans for good fortune. Most of all, they seek a blessing for their research to bear fruit.
Hiyuki: But sometimes the full titles of their projects are so lengthy I suspect they were designed to be forgotten.
Rover: So that muttering earlier was... studying?
Hiyuki: Reading, memorizing terms... Rover, do you...
[Dialogue Option]  Not my forte, either...
Rover: Sorry. That's one area I can't help you with.
Hiyuki: I see... No matter. The night is long. I will remember what I can.
[Dialogue Option]  Another one of my strengths.
Rover: That's easy. Leave it to me.
Hiyuki: Oh? Then when you are free, I will take you up on that.

Dagdir Chin up! Chest out! Where's your fire?!
Dagdir You're a Synchronist, aren't you? What's with this sniveling?
Hiroyuki B-but what's going to happen to Rabelle College...
In the Tactical Proving Grounds, an instructor is giving a dejected student a brutal dressing-down.
[Dialogue Option]  (Listen)
Dagdir: Answer me, Hiroyuki! Who are you? What are you doing here? Why did you come to this place?
Hiroyuki: I... I'm Hiroyuki! A first-year at Rabelle College! I came here to learn! To gain skill! To make my ideals real!
Dagdir: Good energy! Wrong answer!
Dagdir: Burn this into your skull! You are a SYNCHRONIST of Rabelle College, Startorch Academy!
Dagdir: No matter where you go, no matter what happens! Even if the Exostrider leaves, even if the Synchronist program changes. YOU. ARE. STILL. A. SYNCRHONIST!
Hiroyuki: But Dag... wasn't the Synchronist Development Program created so we could pilot the Exostrider...?
Dagdir: Answer me this, Hiroyuki. Have you ever stopped to ask why both the Exostrider and the Mechascouts are humanoid?
Hiroyuki: Because... frequency control is easier that way? Let's us adapt to combat more naturally?
Dagdir: Wrong! With a Synchronist's abilities, you really think you couldn't pilot a quadruped robot? Or a dreadnought gun?
Dagdir: The Exostrider is humanoid because it carries the human spirit! Its creator meant for it to stand. On this earth. As we do. Forever.
Dagdir: The moment you get used to sitting behind heavy artillery, pouring fire from a safe distance, you stop being a person. You become a weapon. And a weapon doesn't search for a way forward.
Dagdir: The Exostrider's limbs. Its armament. Each one is a symbol of humankind. An extension of the human spirit!
Dagdir: So when you inherit that spirit as a Synchronist, what difference does it make whether the Exostrider is here or not?!
[Dialogue Option]  (Leave)

title: Starlights from Yesterdays
content:
Ms. Yuki During the rune search, your frequency readings spiked past the safety limit several times.
Ms. Yuki Your resonance patterns are still within the safety range, but...
Ishida Wasn't me. Didn't happen. I swear on my credits.
In the infirmary, a student fresh out of his medical check-up seems to be trying very hard to explain himself to a teacher.
[Dialogue Option]  (Listen)
Ms. Yuki: I understand. Most Synchronists would stay behind in their mechs and hold the line, buying time for everyone else.
Ms. Yuki: Maybe you can fool I.R.I.S. and N.A.N.A., but you can't fool me... This isn't the first time you've pushed yourself toward Overclocking, is it?
Ishida: How did you know...? Is it because you're from Ashinohara too, Professor?
Ms. Yuki: Wrong. It's because this technique originated from Rabelle College.
Ms. Yuki: Listen to me, Ishida. You're just an ordinary person who happened to develop a Forte. You are not obligated to throw your life away for the Synchronist Program.
Ms. Yuki: I understand how you feel. But the closer you get to Overclocking, the easier it is to trigger an accident no one can control.
Ms. Yuki: And besides... the Synchronist Program itself may not be around much longer.
[Dialogue Option]  (Leave)

Halvad: Perception that can pass through the Stridergate... How would that even work? A new form of Resonance? Huh. A hypothesis worth digging into...

title: Starlights from Yesterdays
content: Keystone - An "anchor" left behind when the Exostrider first came to the lands that would one day be called Lahai-Roi. The Spacetrek Collective mounted expeditions to its location, but returned with nothing worth recording.

title: Starlights from Yesterdays
content: Seal of Flaming Sakura - Ashinohara has long relied on the "miko system" to resist the Threnodian, with each miko organization assigned to a specific territory. The Miko of Flaming Sakura is unique, her responsibility spanning all of Ashinohara. The Seal of Flaming Sakura is one of her line's secret arts, said to have been created by the very first Miko of Flaming Sakura . It is the only secret art passed down in written form. The seal draws power from the miko herself: the more power she channels into it, the longer it lasts. The seal's form changes with its caster. It is said that Hiyuki sealed away part of "her own future" within it—including, some say, a future that cannot be named.

title: Starlights from Yesterdays
content: Duskveil - The actual details of the plan are not elaborated upon in any great detail, but much can be inferred. In essence, Duskveil is an Antivoid Canopy, a kind of Voidmatter Barrier which will seal off both Lahai-Roi and the deeper Dimmr Plains from the rest of the world.

title: Wishes in the Bell: Epilogue
content:
[Objective: Complete the final Purge]
Hiyuki: (Gyokuro must be just ahead...)
Hiyuki: (This was Honami's last Rite of Purging.)
Hiyuki: (All is settled. Only one final thing remains.)
Hiyuki: (I have truly... kept you waiting for too long, Gyokuro.)

Gyokuro: Finally came to see me?
Hiyuki: Yes. I have come.
Gyokuro: Made up your mind?
Hiyuki: I have.
Gyokuro: Ready to kill me, then?
Hiyuki: ...Yes.
Gyokuro: Oh? Has my little Hiyuki grown so confident that she can best me without even drawing her blade?
Gyokuro: Now, now... Don't forget who taught the Miko of Eternal Flaming Sakura. Can't show a little respect to your elder?
Hiyuki: You call what you did to me teaching, Gyokuro?

title: Wishes in the Bell: Epilogue
content:
Hiyuki: You call what you did to me teaching, Gyokuro?



(Cutscene plays)
Come then, Miko of Eternal Flaming Sakura.
...
Calm yourself.
A restless heart makes for unsteady hands.
But... I do not wish to learn this.
Then what do you wish to learn?
This girl will become a great archer.
No, look at her hands... they're a swordsman's hands.
Not in this life.
Her hands aren't ones to hold a blade. Isn't that right?
Well now. You have refined your technique.
Hmph.
Hiyuki...
Do not let the Suzu bind your fate.
Go seek a future of your own.
Focus, Hiyuki.
Survive this strike—
And reach your tomorrow.
(Cutscene ends)

title: Wishes in the Bell: Epilogue
subsection: Hiyuki tells Gyokuro how much she still misses her—the longing, the resentment, and finally her wish :  to become the Miko of Flaming Sakura who defeats the Threnodian, so that Ashinohara will never need another miko after her. But Hiyuki admits that meeting Rover changed something in her. She no longer despairs over countless failures. Though she knows a future awaits where she burns to ash, knowing she once had a companion on this path makes the pain easier to bear. Before Gyokuro fades away, she tells Hiyuki that she has always been proud of her.

subsection: Hiyuki tells Gyokuro how much she still misses her—the longing, the resentment, and finally her wish :  to become the Miko of Flaming Sakura who defeats the Threnodian, so that Ashinohara will never need another miko after her. But Hiyuki admits that meeting Rover changed something in her. She no longer despairs over countless failures. Though she knows a future awaits where she burns to ash, knowing she once had a companion on this path makes the pain easier to bear. Before Gyokuro fades away, she tells Hiyuki that she has always been proud of her.
content:
Gyokuro: Tsk, tsk. You have mastered many skills from others, but have yet to master the bladework of your own Flaming Sakura clan.
Hiyuki: The last Miko withheld too much. She refused to teach me a single technique.
Gyokuro: Do you resent her?
Hiyuki: I do.
Gyokuro: Even now?
Hiyuki: Every moment.
Hiyuki: I resent that she did not step down long ago. Instead, she burned every future she had and left nothing behind. Not even ashes.
Hiyuki: I resent that she did not pass her skills to me. That she sent me away each time she trained. Now... there is nothing of her left in me.
Gyokuro: Hiyuki...
Hiyuki: I resent that she always told me to "be myself," yet chose a death that was nothing like herself.
Gyokuro: And you resent that even after dying, she lingered as a spirit, waiting only for you to send her on.
Gyokuro: Ah. I was being cruel, wasn't I?
Gyokuro: It's just... I couldn't let my fear go. No one understood the scale of your gift, Hiyuki. Your potential to tame even a Threnodian.
Gyokuro: If you drew such a future, would everything not become much easier?
Hiyuki: Gyokuro, I...
Gyokuro: As long as it comes from your own heart and will, any future you choose is acceptable.
Gyokuro: But if our little Hiyuki truly became a Threnodian Resonator... Well. I'd have no choice but to follow "family law" and send us both on our way.
Hiyuki: I have already burned that future.
Hiyuki: I accepted the Suzu of my own will. I chose to become the Miko of Flaming Sakura.
Hiyuki: I know why you refused to teach me your swordsmanship. You never wanted there to be another Miko after you.
Hiyuki: I will fulfill that wish, Sister.
Hiyuki: After Hiyuki, there will be no more Mikos of Flaming Sakura.
Gyokuro: The Miko of Eternal Flaming Sakura... That is a heavy title to bear.
Hiyuki: It is.
Gyokuro: The future ahead is long. Very, very long.
Hiyuki: I know.
Gyokuro: Through the Suzu, we draw strength from countless possible futures.
Gyokuro: But each time you do, you see yourself draw closer to Miko's destined end. A future burned to cinders, leaving nothing behind.
Hiyuki: Yes. And before that destined end arrives, I will find a way to drive back the Threnodian.
Hiyuki: So that Gyokuro may simply be Gyokuro. So that Hiyuki may simply be Hiyuki. So that Ashinohara will no longer need a Miko of Flaming Sakura.
Gyokuro: You have grown up, our little Hiyuki.
Hiyuki: ...
Hiyuki: I met someone, Sister. Unlike me, who failed Ashinohara, he always finds a way to save.
Gyokuro: That must be difficult for you to bear, little Hiyuki.
Hiyuki: Yes. At first... it was.
Hiyuki: Hearing tales of his exploits, I felt a deep admiration. No, perhaps it was closer to jealousy.
Hiyuki: I thought, if only I possessed his strength. Then my days would not be filled with regret. Ashinohara would be saved.
Hiyuki: And I... in the peace that followed, could have lived an ordinary life.
Hiyuki: But upon meeting him, I came to understand. Even a great "savior" carries many pains and failures.
Hiyuki: And the path of a savior is walked not alone, but alongside countless others.
Hiyuki: Gyokuro.
Gyokuro: Yes?
Hiyuki: I have always admired you as the Miko of Flaming Sakura. And I have always... held you in the highest honor.
Hiyuki: Even if one day I am burned to ashes...
Hiyuki: Because of you.... because of him... because they all exist... I am never truly alone.
Gyokuro: I take great pride in you, too.
Gyokuro: Go on, Shiratori. Fly to where your heart desires.
Gyokuro: May the day come when you, too... step into spring as freely as anyone in this world.

Though she knows a future awaits where she burns to ash, knowing she once had a companion on this path makes the pain easier to bear. title: Beneath a Melting Night Sky
content: Quest Objective: Not long after the Stridergate incident, the Spacetrek Collective informs you that Denia is awake and being kept in isolation. To learn the Fractsidus's next step and open new directions for future research, you head to the infirmary to negotiate with Denia. There, she offers you a "deal." In exchange, you'll need to stay with her for her birthday...

title: Beneath a Melting Night Sky
content:
[Objective: Read Sigrika's WavesLine message]
Sigrika: Senior, do you remember Denia? You met her at the New Solar Celebration. She was the one who got us those tickets.
Sigrika: She's been in the infirmary since the last incident. They're saying she's still not in any condition to take visitors.
Sigrika: If it's not too much trouble, could you check on her for me? I've been asking N.A.N.A. for updates, but she tells me the same thing every time... I'm worried.
[Choice]  Got it.
(Rover): Got it.
Sigrika: Appreciate you, Senior! ヾ(ﾟ▽ﾟ)ノ}}

title: Beneath a Melting Night Sky
content:
[Choice]  Got it.
(Rover): Got it.
Sigrika: Appreciate you, Senior! ヾ(ﾟ▽ﾟ)ノ}}



Nivora: She's right, little one... You might still have a way out.
Nivora: Because your suffering is nothing like hers. It cannot make you stronger, but neither will it last...
Nivora: Enough staring at the dead bird, Denia.
Denia: Why did you kill it?
Nivora: What's worthless doesn't deserve to continue, see? That was mercy.
Nivora: Just hours ago, you accepted Aleph-1's gift, the first in this world to do so. Now tell me, how did it feel?
Denia: I felt... nothing.
Nivora: So, nothingness. The void. The dark... Our good old friends.
Nivora: But why do you tremble, Denia? Everything begins in the void. And you, most of all, should find it cosy...
Denia: Why... did you kill it?
Nivora: Heh... Self-awareness. A lamentable flaw in the course of evolution.
Nivora: Now, look up, Denia. What do you see?
Denia: ...The void... and the dark.
Nivora: Good. Remember what you've seen.
Nivora: You will accept them, Denia. Become one with them. This is the world's first gift to you, and its last.

title: Beneath a Melting Night Sky
content:
Nivora: You will accept them, Denia. Become one with them. This is the world's first gift to you, and its last.



In time, we will all meet again in eternal darkness.

Denia: No...
N.A.N.A.: Vital signs indicate sustained recovery. Voidmatter activity remains within normal parameters. Target frequency has not yet returned to the syntony level. Initiating secondary protocol.
N.A.N.A.: Can you hear my voice, Denia?

title: Beneath a Melting Night Sky
content:
[Objective: Check WavesLine]
Arman: Hi Rover. This is Arman from the Spacetrek Collective. Can you come by now?
Arman: Denia is awake and being kept in isolation at the infirmary. We'd like to work with you on her case.
[Choice]  Sure.
(Rover): Sure.
Arman: Much appreciated. See you soon.}}

title: Beneath a Melting Night Sky
content:
[Objective: Head to the infirmary]
Abby: So, Denia... You think she's alright?
Rover: (Denia... The Fractsidus made no move while she was unconscious. Have they really abandoned what they worked so hard to achieve? Or are they biding their time for something else?)
Rover: Let's go see for ourselves.

title: Beneath a Melting Night Sky
content:
[Objective: Head to the infirmary]
Arman: Impossible. We will not agree to that condition...
Arman: Please relay this message, Madam President. I'll take full responsibility.

title: Beneath a Melting Night Sky
content:
[Objective: Accept the commission]
Arman: Rover is here. Yes, I understand. Please rest assured.
Arman: Sorry to pull you in on such short notice, Rover. I'm Arman, I sent the message. The situation's worse than we anticipated, so I'll keep it short.
Rover: How's Denia?
Arman: She's... awake. But just as we feared, the Fractsidus did something to her.
Arman: After waking up, her frequency deteriorated rapidly into systemic failure. According to Rabelle College's estimate, she has... one week. At best.
[Dialogue Option]  What's gone wrong?
Arman: No idea. There's not enough time to even determine whether it's physiological... or caused by the Threnodian.
Arman: The New Federation is pressing charges over the Stridergate incident and the residual frequency on the Dimmr Plains. They want Denia handed over immediately.
Arman: We didn't comply, of course. Denia was a Startorch Academy student. Sending her there would turn her into a mere research subject... and cost us our only chance to reach the truth or contest the charges.
Rover: I see the picture... When you say "contest the charges," are you suggesting Denia is the key to breaking this stalemate?
Arman: Exactly. First, her connection to the Voidborne Threnodian has enormous research value. Even with the Stridergate sealed, she could open new directions for Voidmatter science.
Arman: And based on I.R.I.S.'s review of our prior interactions, Denia likely knows the source of the Threnodian frequency on the Dimmr Plains. The reason why her condition is worsening, too.
Arman: If she is willing to cooperate, we can resolve this before the New Fed forces our hand. We treat her. She helps with the report. It'll be a win-win, ideally.
Rover: Sounds like that didn't go very smoothly.
Arman: No. She's been... resistant. To any form of contact.
Arman: This is where we need you, Rover. I'm sure you understand, mental stability is a prerequisite for frequency control. You have prior contact with her, and... your experience with Threnodians also makes you a safer anchor in the negotiation.
Rover: (Denia might be a viable opening. But until I figure out what the Fractsidus is planning and where they are now, I shouldn't commit to anything reckless.)
Rover: I will speak to her and make my judgment from there.
Rover: Also, I want this meeting kept off the record. No files, not even in I.R.I.S.'s archive.
Arman: ...Understood. Then I'll leave this in your hands, Rover. Her identity is only known to very few now, I can assure you.

title: Beneath a Melting Night Sky
content:
[Objective: Talk to Arman]
Arman: Anything else you want to confirm, Rover?
[Dialogue Option]  Any progress on tracking the Threnodian frequency?
Arman: We've narrowed down the location, but Voidmatter contamination there is heavy, so cleanup and investigation will be slow. That said, recent spectral analysis points to a direct correlation between the frequency and Denia's physical condition.
[Dialogue Option]  How was Denia acting when she spoke with you?
Arman: "Cold" is the word. So cold that even N.A.N.A. can't establish any meaningful contact. We are still not sure if the Threnodian did this, but she is not the Denia we knew.
Rover: You've met Denia before?
Arman: I have. Back then, I was teaching a required course in Voidmatters Science, and she slept through a good portion of it, so I remember her.
[Dialogue Option]  That call earlier, was it Lucilla?
Arman: Yes. The President is busy smoothing things over with some big names. She asked me to send her regards.
Arman: Oh, and she also has a message for you: "Only the kids who make it out alive get to grow up."
Rover: Is that supposed to be about Denia?
Arman: I honestly don't know. But that's her... always leaving you guessing.
[Dialogue Option]  That's all.

title: Beneath a Melting Night Sky
content:
[Objective: Enter the Academy infirmary]
Rover: (Whatever her reason was for saving me and Hiyuki back then... she still carried out the Fractsidus's plan.)
Rover: (And the Grand Architect's next move is still unclear... Have to stay cautious.)

title: Beneath a Melting Night Sky
content:
[Objective: Talk to Denia]
Rover: Denia.
Denia: I just saw Sigrika. That was crazy, Rover. I didn't think you'd actually... you know, drive that thing off.
Denia: So... you're just gonna keep staring? Do you always come empty-handed when you visit patients?
Rover: (Looks like she's free of the Threnodian's influence now... but that way of talking...)
[Dialogue Option]  Are you aware of your condition right now?
Denia: Yeah. I'm dying, right?
Denia: That person gave me a gift a long time ago... Said when the time comes, I'd finally get a nice sleep.
[Dialogue Option]  A gift?
[Dialogue Option]  What is it exactly?
Denia: Who knows. But it's not hard to guess, is it? Just like a collar you put on cats and dogs, in case they get ideas.
Denia: Mm, no. "Cats and dogs" might be too generous. At least they can still bite. I'm probably closer to a lab mouse now.
Denia: So, Rover, did they send you to sweet-talk a lab mouse?
Rover: Denia, I'm here because I chose to be.
Rover: We've been on opposite sides before, but...
Denia: There you go, still all serious...
Rover: But I want to try trusting you.
Denia: Right... In that case, am I supposed to look more excited?
Denia: Too bad, Rover, I can't trust you in the same way.
Denia: You saw me at my worst there, and you're still playing this game... You want answers. That's why you're here.
[Dialogue Option]  I won't deny it.
Denia: How honest. I don't hate that.
[Dialogue Option]  You did save me once.
Denia: Hah... don't get the wrong idea... If you'd died back there, it would have been game over.
Denia: If you really want answers, how about we make a deal?
Rover: A deal?
Denia: Yes, a fair exchange. The Collective can't get what they want from me, but you just might get what you want.
[Dialogue Option]  What's your condition?
Denia: Maybe you could stay with me for my birthday? This weekend. I'd like to have a good stroll in the Academy again.
Rover: Your birthday is this weekend?
Denia: It could be, or not. Doesn't matter. What matters is... you are there.
Denia: I'm running out of time. Some things deserve a proper ending—with a good day.
Rover: (An ending... What is she planning to do? But in her current state...)
Denia: What, doesn't feel safe even if you're around? Then put another collar on me, or a bomb. What's one more, right?
Rover: ...I'll see what I can do.
Denia: You mean that? But people at the Academy, do they know...
Rover: Spacetrek Collective never made your identity public. So for that day, you'll still be the Academy student Denia.
Denia: (Always the busybody.)
Denia: ...Fine. Then it's a deal, right?
Denia: Relax. I'll cooperate with their research for the next few days. Just don't get your hopes up...
Denia: ...The Grand Architect wouldn't be sloppy enough to leave me unhandled.
Denia: Anyway, no point worrying about it now. I'll see you this weekend, Rover.

title: Beneath a Melting Night Sky
content:
[Objective: Keep talking to Denia]
Denia: Rover... Something's still bothering you?
[Dialogue Option]  What do you know about the Grand Architect?
Denia: I've never seen her true face. Wouldn't be surprised if the real one's already dead.
Denia: You care about that, do you? I'll tell you more once you've kept your side of the deal.
[Dialogue Option]  Do you miss life at the Academy?
Denia: Miss my life at the Academy? What made you think that?
Rover: You keep staring out the window. That's where the dorms are.
Denia: ...When you put it that way, maybe I do. The president once said that everyone ends up missing their school days when they grow up.
Denia: I guess that really was my golden age.
[Dialogue Option]  Why did the Grand Architect leave you there?
Denia: Trash gets dumped, you know... And those little tricks of mine? She probably noticed long ago.
Denia: Or maybe... she simply decided it was better if I died here.
Denia: Because you always try to save everyone, even someone like me... Heh. That kind of stubbornness must have gotten to her.
[Dialogue Option]  Nothing.
Denia: See you this weekend, Rover.

title: Beneath a Melting Night Sky
content:
[Objective: Report what happened to Arman]
Arman: Rover. How did it go? Is she willing to cooperate?
You pass along Denia's request to Arman
Arman: A birthday... at the Academy?
Arman: ...I see. That is an unexpected request.
Arman: But if that's the key to cooperation, the Collective will treat it as a special case.
Rover: She said she wants a "proper ending" for some things. But I don't know her true intent yet. We'd better be careful.
Arman: Noted. We'll initiate a full risk assessment immediately, and draft a comprehensive operational and contingency plan.
Arman: Thank you, Rover. Would you be available in the afternoons of this weekend? She asked for you specifically.
[Dialogue Option]  No problem.
Arman: Much appreciated. We'll ensure that all procedures and contingency measures are fully in place.
[Dialogue Option]  I'll do my best.
Arman: We really appreciate your support! I know this is a very personal request, but we'll keep everything under control. You can think of it as a special escort mission.
Arman: I'll send you the finalized plan before then. Let's stay in touch on WavesLine!

title: Beneath a Melting Night Sky
content:
[Objective: Check WavesLine]
Arman: Rover, the approvals are through. Everything is set. You can pick up Denia at the station.}}

title: Beneath a Melting Night Sky
content:
[Objective: Pick Denia up]
Arman: You're here, Rover. The procedure and contact list have been sent to your Terminal. All steps and contingency measures are included.
Rover: Very detailed. I see a Resonance suppression device and declared contact entries. Everyone's agreed on those?
Arman: Yes. At Denia's request, we used her Terminal to schedule the meetings under a recovery discharge notice. She'll be approaching them today as a student.
Arman: The suppression device was... her idea, a guarantee of cooperation. She said it would make things fair, even though she doesn't really need it in her current state.
Arman: Here, take this. If she starts feeling unwell, have her use it. It should make her feel better.
Rover: So you've found a way to relieve her frequency failure?
Arman: No... these are only tranquillizers. We've adjusted the dosage for this operation. As for a treatment plan... we'll try and work out a revised version as soon as possible.
Rover: (No wonder Denia behaved that way last time. She had already seen this coming.)
[Dialogue Option]  What's the bottleneck?
Arman: The diagnosis from Rabelle College shows that the problem doesn't lie with her Resonance ability, but a failure in her self-regulation mechanism...
Arman: We're still validating several hypotheses regarding the symptoms. Hopefully, we'll have answers soon.
Rover: (This is looking grimmer than I thought. Still, if it's related to Threnodian frequencies, the Black Shores might have better solutions.)
Arman: Don't concern yourself with the research. For now, we'll need you to focus on today's operation. Please contact us if anything arises.
Denia: Are we good to go?
Arman: Yes. Hope you both have a pleasant day.
Denia: So, I'll be in your hands today, Rover.
Denia: You promised me a birthday, remember? Why the serious face?
[Dialogue Option]  I have to keep the operation under control.
Denia: Even so, you can't walk around with that face. People will notice something's off.
[Dialogue Option]  ...You didn't sound like this last time.
Denia: Because today, I'm Denia, a proud student of Startorch Academy.
Denia: Come on... Try it like me. Loosen your mouth, relax your eyes...
Denia: There. See? You look nicer when you smile.
Rover: I can do that. But remember your situation, don't—
Denia: Yeah, yeah, I know.

title: Beneath a Melting Night Sky
content:
[Objective: Walk with Denia]
Denia: Yawn... Finally, they let me out for a walk.
Denia: Feels kind of nice being a student, doesn't it, Rover?
Denia: Hmm, funny, you'd think there'd be more people here on a weekend.
Denia: Don't tell me they heard I was coming and decided to hide?
Rover: ...
Denia: So that's a yes, then? You could at least say something nice.
Rover: Campus security is still our responsibility.
Denia: Ugh... That kills the mood.

title: Beneath a Melting Night Sky
content:
[Objective: Prepare to head downstairs]
Denia: This way leads to the Garden Zone, right?
Rover: Yes. This is where you're supposed to meet Sigrika.
Denia: ...Ah, Sigrika.
Denia: When was the last time we went shopping together...?

title: Beneath a Melting Night Sky
content:
[Objective: Talk to the Suspicious Researcher]
Suspicious Researcher: Hello. Can I help you with something?
Rover: (This guy's acting strange. I don't remember him on the contact list.)
Suspicious Researcher: Please don't mind me. Denia is the one who needs your attention.
Rover: ...

title: Beneath a Melting Night Sky
content:
[Objective: The elevator has arrived]
Denia: If the elevator breaks, do we get stuck here?
Rover: I can cut it open.
Denia: Absolutely not. That's vandalism...
Denia: Wow, the elevator was fast.
Rover: Let's go, Denia.
Denia: Sigh... This feels like walking into an exam...
Denia: You'll have my back when she starts asking questions, right...?
Denia: ...
Denia: So you'd rather do that than share an elevator with me?
Denia: Your guard's up way too high, Rover.
Denia: Sigh... Fine. Can't blame you. Let's go.

title: Beneath a Melting Night Sky
content:
Denia: Your guard's up way too high, Rover.
Denia: Sigh... Fine. Can't blame you. Let's go.



Elska: You are... Denia's friend, right? I think I just saw you with her.
[Dialogue Option]  Yes.
Elska: That's good news. So she's been discharged already.
[Dialogue Option]  No.
Elska: Oh, sorry, my bad. We must have been mistaken.
Rover: Were you looking for her?
Munson: Yep. Nothing urgent. It's just that the prize money from last time is still with the club. We were waiting to talk it over with her.
Banlu: And honestly, things just don't feel the same without her.

title: Beneath a Melting Night Sky
content:
[Objective: Meet Sigrika]
Denia: Hey, Rover, uh... Want to swing by the Arcade first?
Rover: Are you trying to avoid Sigrika?
Denia: Oh, so you saw...
Rover: This is your own request. Give me a reason to cancel it.
Denia: The reason is... I-I'm not feeling so great. Maybe we should just—
Sigrika: Senior, Denia!
Denia: ...!
Denia: Wow, hi, Siggy. Did I keep you waiting?
Sigrika: No, I just got here too... Hmm? Why are you with Denia today, Senior?
[Dialogue Option]  The doctor asked me to keep her company.
Sigrika: Oh, I see. I heard Denia's been in the ward for quite a few days.
[Dialogue Option]  She wanted to go for a walk with me.
Denia: You...
Sigrika: I didn't realize you were that close... But... but that's nice. At least Denia finally gets some fresh air.
Sigrika: Every time I went to the infirmary, Dr. Luuk said you still needed some rest... So, are you feeling better now?
Denia: Oh, I was better a while ago... Yawn... Guess it's just bad sleep. I mean, a ward's never as comfy as your own room.
Sigrika: Bad sleep... Have you been having nightmares again? I heard what happened last time really affected a lot of people...
Sigrika: You don't think it's because of the Voidmatter contamination, right?
Denia: Of course not... I just pretended to be sick for a bit longer so I don't have to get back to class so soon.
Denia: Relax. Having Rover watch over me is plenty. Come on, Siggy, didn't you want to go photograph the white bird in the garden? It'll be off duty if you don't hurry...
Sigrika: Okay then... Make sure you catch up with us later on, Senior.
Sigrika: Did you know, Nia? The Photography Fan Club is planning to apply for a studio!
Denia: They have budget for that? Was it the prize they won from the campus event?
Sigrika: Yeah. They won't stop talking about how much they owe you.

title: Beneath a Melting Night Sky
content:
[Objective: Talk to TARD-E Unit]
TARD-E Unit: Greetings, Rover! No suspicious individuals detected. Frequency readings are normal. Please proceed with your mission.
Rover: Keep it down...
TARD-E Unit: Understood. However, based on TARD-E's logic functions, if you don't want Denia to notice, then you should not be speaking with TARD-E!

title: Beneath a Melting Night Sky
content:
[Objective: (Idle)]
Shh, don't look this way, Rover. We have to pretend we don't know each other.

title: Beneath a Melting Night Sky
content:
[Objective: Take the picture]
Sigrika: You're yawning more than usual today. Are you sure it's not some kind of aftereffect?
Denia: No way. I've just been inside too long. Got a little sensitive to sunlight...
Sigrika: No, no, no. You can't stay shut in all the time. A little sunlight is good for you.
Denia: Oh, too bright...

title: Beneath a Melting Night Sky
content:
[Objective: Take a group photo]
Sigrika: Look, the Photography Fan Club's here. Wanna go say hi?
Denia: I'll pass... a bunch of camera-obsessed weirdos. Their prize money has nothing to do with me anyway.
Sigrika: What are you talking about? Without you, they would've shut down by now.
[Dialogue Option]  Prize money?
Denia: It was for an academy promo thing... The theme was "Startorch: Moments of Happiness." Why?
[Dialogue Option]  You're good at photography?
[Dialogue Option]  So you're a pro?
Denia: I was the model, actually. Someone came to me and said they'd buy me a luxury buffet if I agreed to pose for a couple of photos while eating... For a moment, I genuinely believed they were being generous.
Denia: I even skipped a meal on purpose. Turned out their "luxury buffet" was the cafeteria.
Sigrika: But the photos came out beautifully. They even made it to the F.U.E.L.'s "A Seal-Proof Guide to Enrollment."
Denia: It's just marketing for freshmen. You smile no matter what you're eating. That's what being a model feels like, I suppose... Besides, you know I never really liked taking photos.
Sigrika: Yeah, you're right. The only time we took a group photo was when Nivora insisted.
Sigrika: Sigh... Speaking of Nivora, I wonder how she's doing now.
Denia: ...Siggy.
Sigrika: Hmm?
Denia: Let's take another photo together.
Sigrika: Really? That's a first for you!
Denia: Come on, Rover, you too. And... can I borrow your camera?
[Dialogue Option]  So this is what it's about?
Denia: Alright, ready... three, two, one—
Sigrika: Cheese!
Denia: I'll save the photo on Rover's Terminal for now. We can print it someday.
Sigrika: Look, in the photo! It's the white bird... It flew that way!

title: Beneath a Melting Night Sky
content:
[Objective: (Idle)]
First time we nail this area... It's really quiet today.
I heard there's a special arrangement. A lot of people weren't allowed over here this afternoon...
Hold on... Did I just see a pink-haired girl?

title: Beneath a Melting Night Sky
content:
[Objective: Take a stroll]
Sigrika: An unidentified rare species... the fabled pure white bird.
Sigrika: It's been a year since we first saw it, and we still haven't gotten a close look.
Denia: Heh... calm down. For all we know, it could just be someone's Resonance ability...
Sigrika: As if. You and your dry humor, Nia.
Sigrika: I'm pretty sure it flew this way... where did it go?
Denia: Why don't we split up? You head that way, Siggy. Rover and I will check this way.
Sigrika: Okay! Ping me on the Terminal if you find anything!
Denia: Could you come this way for a while, Rover...?

title: Beneath a Melting Night Sky
content:
[Objective: Look for the white bird]
Denia: Hey... can you imagine her face if we told her the white bird is just Hiyuki's ability?
[Dialogue Option]  You noticed it too?
Denia: ...So it really is her. That kind of cold frequency is hard to forget.
[Dialogue Option]  I don't think it'd be a big deal.
Denia: It definitely would! Hiyuki is... well... kind of scary, isn't she? Always popping up out of nowhere with a blade...
Denia: Will she be watching us like this the whole time today?
Rover: Hiyuki is just doing her job. And she's kinder than she looks.
Denia: I know... She sometimes reminds me of you.
Denia: But unfortunately, that's my least favorite kind of person.
[Dialogue Option]  Why?
Denia: What... Are you saying you care about my opinion, Rover?
Denia: Sorry. Being straightforward doesn't do it for me.
[Dialogue Option]  ...
Denia: Okay, okay. I'll stop... I wonder how Sigrika's getting on. Let's go find her.

title: Beneath a Melting Night Sky
content:
[Objective: Search for Sigrika]
Denia: She headed this way, right? Where did she go?
Denia: Is Sigrika running faster than me?
Denia: I'd like to be able to do that too...
Rover: You can.
Denia: And... I'm dead.

title: Beneath a Melting Night Sky
content:
[Objective: Beneath a Melting Night Sky]
Sigrika: Senior, I lost track of you guys. I'm at the communications area right now.ヾ(✿ﾟ▽ﾟ)ノ
[Choice]  Got it.
(Rover): }}

title: Beneath a Melting Night Sky
content:
Sigrika: Senior, I lost track of you guys. I'm at the communications area right now.ヾ(✿ﾟ▽ﾟ)ノ
[Choice]  Got it.
(Rover): }}



Sigrika: You can't find it, either? Maybe not today then.
Denia: Seriously, Siggy. If you went into biology, you'd be a legend by now...
Sigrika: Hehe, I just want to confirm a new species before I graduate.
Sigrika: And you really don't come out enough, Denia. A little more activity would be good for you.
Denia: Please, give me a break. I'm not exactly built for running or fighting like you are...
Rover: (Since when are you bad at fighting?)
Denia: Oh, right. Didn't you say you wanted to call home? The booth looks empty right now.
Sigrika: Oh it is! That's rare. There's usually a line here...
Denia: Go on, before they start worrying. I've got some "family matters" to handle too, using Rover's Terminal.
Sigrika: Okay then... See you in a bit!

title: Beneath a Melting Night Sky
content:
[Objective: (Idle)]
Sigrika: Yeah, I'm doing great today. Don't worry!
Sigrika: Denia's out of the ward, so I'm taking a walk with her...

title: Beneath a Melting Night Sky
subsection: Talk to Denia about the phone call
content:
[Objective: Talk to Denia about the phone call]
Denia: I know what you're worried about. I remember everything from back then... Why would I ever contact those people?
Rover: ...Then who are you calling?
Denia: This'll do. I'll just open the comm, and you can wait here with me for a while.
[Dialogue Option]  You've been doing this all along?
Denia: Yeah. It was all made up. To keep her happy. But I didn't realize how much effort it takes to keep a simple lie going.
Rover: This will only complicate things.
Denia: But I can't be honest with her, can I? She's all cheerful on the outside, but she bears more than enough worries for her size... As her friend, that's the least I can do.
Denia: And besides... having a sweet, trusting friend like her around is a great cover, isn't it?
[Dialogue Option]  That's self-deluding.
Denia: ...I thought you'd put it more gently.
Denia: Alright. Looks like she's finished her call. Let's head over.

title: Beneath a Melting Night Sky
content:
[Objective: Mention ordering a cake]
Sigrika: Perfect timing! We should go check out the new desserts!
Denia: This part, finally...
Sigrika: What made you want to buy cake today, Denia?
Denia: You'll find out soon enough.

title: Beneath a Melting Night Sky
content:
[Objective: Buy snacks at F.U.E.L.]
Denia: Today's new desserts include: Frostwort Dumpling, Fern Spore Kelp Biscuit, Pine Needle Lichen Roll, and—on special—Jarred Fish Muffin...
Sigrika: Those names sound... intense.
Denia: Do you think you could assemble them into a cake?
Sigrika: What a terrifying thought, Nia...
Rover: (Taste aside, the operational procedure was very clear about food intake. I should check with Arman...)
[Dialogue Option]  Patients need to be careful about food safety.
Denia: I'm just going through the motions... She can eat it for me.
Rover: I happen to know a team that specializes in desserts. We could order a cake from them if you want.
Rover: What kind of style are you thinking of?
Denia: Oh, really? Then can I add Rainbow Bean Pop Rocks? And Creeping Torchpine nuts. Oh, and some Fruit Crackle too?
Sigrika: Denia, you can't put Pop Rocks on a cake. You need to start with a base flavor...
Denia: Hm... okay. Let me think...
Denia: Let's get an orange cake. I promised Sigrika we'd celebrate together. She likes oranges.
Denia: But make sure you add everything I mentioned earlier, okay?
Sigrika: Have you decided yet? What's it going to be, Denia?
Denia: Keeping it a secret for now.
[Dialogue Option]  The cake will be ready by tonight.
Denia: Tonight...
Sigrika: Tonight might not work for me... I... I promised Professor Mornye I'd help out at the Reactor Drive today...
Denia: ...
Denia: Well, that's a shame, Siggy. I was hoping to share the birthday cake with you, but I guess you'll just have to make do with the leftovers.
Sigrika: Birthday cake...? Wait, today's your birthday? So that's why Rover is...
[Dialogue Option]  Denia wanted to surprise you.
Sigrika: Then I... I'll leave Professor Mornye a message...
Denia: It's alright, Siggy. I'm sure you've got something really important to do with Professor Mornye.
Sigrika: Well, asking for a day off once in a while wouldn't...
Denia: Nope. No running away from it.
Denia: How can you become the kind of person you look up to, if you run away from something like this?
Sigrika: But... aren't you the one who's been telling me "it's okay to run away" this whole time, Denia?
Denia: It was just to make you feel better. I say it to everyone.
Sigrika: No. You're acting super weird today.
Sigrika: All of a sudden you asked me to come out, had me take pictures with you, revealed it's your birthday, and... told me not to run away... This... It's not like you at all...
Denia: Siggy, I...
Sigrika: Are you hiding something from me?
Denia: Oh, couldn't you be a little less perceptive at a time like this, Sigrika?
Sigrika: If you want me to keep playing dumb, I can do that, and I'll leave it there. As usual.
Sigrika: But, there's only one thing I want to make sure... Will you still be celebrating your birthday this time next year?
Denia: I will...
Sigrika: Then next year... we'll celebrate your birthday together. Promise?
Denia: Promise.
Sigrika: How about we make a cake together when the time comes?
Denia: I thought you said there's only one thing you wanted to make sure of...
Rover: Denia still has some check-ups to do tonight. Maybe after she's fully recovered in a few days...
Sigrika: You sound just like Dr. Herssen, Senior.
Sigrika: It's fine, we've made a promise... Right, off I go to sort out some files.
Denia: You go get those files, Sigrika...
Sigrika: Happy birthday, Denia!
Denia: Phew, that was tough... I'm never good at this with her around.
Denia: Well, that made things really awkward at the end... If you'd just listened to me and moved on...
[Dialogue Option]  Sigrika really cares about you.
[Dialogue Option]  You'll regret it.
Denia: Oh, sneaky you, being so nice and kind all of a sudden.
Denia: To be honest, I'm really impressed hearing those words from you, Rover... I suppose you must've gone through plenty of farewells, haven't you?
Denia: Strong, caring. Keep it up and I might actually fall for you.
[Dialogue Option]  ...
Denia: All right, break time's over. I almost died of boredom being stuck in the sickbed these past few days. How about you and I go play some video games, Rover?

content:
