Denia: Look at all those games... What do you have in mind, Rover? I was thinking Lahai-Roi Blocks...
[Dialogue Option]  Catchow.
Denia: Wait, really...? I even gave you the hint.
Denia: Don't tell me you're the type who during a date wants to watch separate movies and just meet up afterward.
Rover: Playing Lahai-Roi Blocks with you brings back bad memories.
Denia: Ugh... You have such a good memory, Rover... Alright, let's start with your game.

title: Beneath a Melting Night Sky
content:
[Objective: Play Catchow with Denia]
Denia: Wait, that character you're using... Is that me?
Denia: That feels a bit... odd. And is that Sigrika next to you?
Denia: Oh, there's a cake coming down!
Rover: Keep the joystick steady.

Denia: I guess Sigrika and I don't make much of a tag team... Shame.
[Dialogue Option]  You know what they say: Get good.
[Dialogue Option]  What does that have to do with it?
Denia: I haven't figured out these new games yet. Let's just go play Lahai-Roi Blocks, Rover.
Denia: How about we compete for high scores? I've been really good at it since I was a child, you know.
[Dialogue Option]  Sure.
Denia: Awesome! Thanks, Rover.
[Dialogue Option]  Is this why you threw blocks at me?
Denia: Still holding grudges, are we? Or is this your way to get my attention?

title: Beneath a Melting Night Sky
content:
[Dialogue Option]  Is this why you threw blocks at me?
Denia: Still holding grudges, are we? Or is this your way to get my attention?



Denia: I didn't know you were this good... Well...
Denia: Anyway, I was wondering, how did you and Siggy get acquainted, Rover?
Rover: We met during the New Solar Celebration.
Denia: Ah, I heard Siggy mention you were a great help... Any stories you mind sharing?
Rover: You know what happened. Weren't you the ones behind it all?
Denia: That wasn't my plan at all...
Denia: ...Don't overthink it. Let's go over there for a moment.

title: Beneath a Melting Night Sky
content:
Denia: That wasn't my plan at all...
Denia: ...Don't overthink it. Let's go over there for a moment.



Rover: You were gonna say goodbye to her, right?
Denia: I suppose... I wanted to treat her to some cake, and then get it off my chest when the moment was right.
Rover: You mean the birthday, the goodbye, or you've been lying to her the whole time?
Denia: All of it, I guess... I actually hoped she'd be angry.
[Dialogue Option]  You want her to be mad at you? Why?
Denia: That way... by the time she realizes I'm gone, she won't feel as upset...
Denia: Knowing your ex-friend died is better than losing an actual friend, right?
[Dialogue Option]  She won't see it that way.
Denia: Sigh. That is why I hate people like you.
Denia: Keeping all the burdens on yourself when you know you can ignore them... The exact way of life I loathe.
Rover: But you still encouraged her.
Denia: Oh, sneaky you, beating my score while I was distracted talking.
[Dialogue Option]  How else am I supposed to beat you?
[Dialogue Option]  It was you who used this trick first...
Denia: Messing up little things like this every now and then can actually make you more likable, okay?
Denia: Anyway, it's getting late, we should keep moving... The Archive is usually my favorite place for pastime. I'd like another visit.

title: Beneath a Melting Night Sky
content:
[Objective: Talk to Nastasha]
Nastasha: Denia? I heard from Arman that you've been hospitalized in the infirmary for the last few days. How are you feeling?
Denia: I'm fine. There's nothing to worry about.
Nastasha: Well, you look paler than you were before. A patient should get plenty of rest.
Nastasha: And this is... Oh, wait, you must be Rover, right? I'm surprised to see Denia with you. She didn't cause you any trouble, did she?
Rover: No, not at all. It's her birthday today, and the infirmary asked me to take her out for some fresh air.
Nastasha: Did they now? That makes it sound even more suspicious.
[Dialogue Option]  Have you known each other long?
Nastasha: Sure. She wasn't hard to miss for taking naps here in her first week of school.
Nastasha: When she heard I needed data on the Void Storm at the time, she just rushed out of campus with that sketchy bubble of hers... What were you thinking, really?
Denia: That was ages ago... Can we please move on?
Nastasha: Well, I feel I should pass it on to as many people as possible before I graduate. And you—try not to be the hero all the time. Just learn to lean on the people around you more often.
Denia: Graduate?
Nastasha: Here, this is for you. I never got the chance to give it to you.
Nastasha: You were always nagging me about that Royan fairytales collection. I had a friend print it in color.
Nastasha: I had no idea it's your birthday today, so consider it a birthday gift from me, Denia.
Denia: Nastasha, your hands...
Nastasha: Just a minor issue from that incident earlier. Don't worry, Dr. Herssen said I'll barely notice it in a few years.
Denia: It's from that Voidmatter contamination...
Denia: But if it can heal as you said, then... there's really no need for you to leave, right? With all those advanced techs of the Spacetrek Collective...
Nastasha: Well, that's exactly why they deemed it's no longer safe for me to stay here. Something about Lahai-Roi's environment makes the contamination even worse for the nervous system.
Denia: B-But...
Nastasha: Who would've thought my own thesis would set me up for early retirement?
Denia: But you once said... your dream is to...
Nastasha: "Unveil the secrets of Voidmatter particles for all mankind?" I recall saying something like that, yeah... But listen, Denia, dreams are sometimes just...
Denia: No. That's not it. Even someone like me can tell... Everyone here...
Denia: Everyone here signed the agreement. If they choose to leave Lahai-Roi, that means...
Nastasha: Calling it quits? Not even close. Who knows, maybe I'll come back from the New Federation in a couple of years. It's too bad that you'd have already graduated by then.
Denia: That's not what I meant. You've always been a great student, Nastasha... It shouldn't have ended like this.
[Dialogue Option]  Calm down, Denia.
Denia: Everything that's happened, it's all my fault...
Nastasha: What's with you today? How is this your fault?
Rover: I'm sorry, Nastasha. Denia's not fully recovered yet. You'll have to excuse us.
Nastasha: I see. Keep your eyes on the road. She seems a little off today.
Nastasha: Oh. And happy birthday, Denia!

title: Beneath a Melting Night Sky

content:
[Objective: Take a break by the bench]
Rover: You okay, Denia?
Denia: ...
Rover: Your frequency is very unstable now. You should take your meds. Come with me.

title: Beneath a Melting Night Sky
content:
[Objective: Talk to Denia]
Rover: Feeling better?
Denia: ...
Rover: (Based on the frequency shown during her complications, things are worse than what Arman said.)
Rover: (At this rate, she won't even last a week... Is this why she chose today?)
[Dialogue Option]  Try to comfort her.
Rover: Nastasha's got talent. The Collective won't give up on her.
Denia: ...
[Dialogue Option]  Try to sit closer to her.
Denia: ...
[Dialogue Option]  Hand her Nastasha's present.
Denia: ...You're right... I've been lying to myself all along.
Denia: I'm sorry. I lied to you. It's actually not my birthday today.
[Dialogue Option]  Why use this as your excuse?
Denia: That's because... a birthday is supposed to be proof that you were born. That's what they always say, right?
Denia: Everyone has a birthday... Sigrika has one, so does Nastasha... Even those TARD-E Units manufactured in factories have their own birthdays.
Denia: But I don't. The Fractsidus has no record of my birth. Nothing to prove my identity.
Denia: There's only this image burrowed inside my head, playing over and over again in my dreams...
Denia: In it, I would always step into the same lake. A woman sways her arms in the wind, crying.
Denia: She stares from afar, calling out to me: Denia, Denia... Dasvidaniya.
Denia: So if I truly had a name and a birthday, maybe I could then die as a real person, no?
[Dialogue Option]  What makes you think so?
Denia: Because I'm running out of time.
Denia: I'm out of time for so many things. But I can at least... try to die with a little dignity, right? I should get to act like a real person. Face what I've done, say a real goodbye... and then just end it the right way.
Denia: What a shame. I even picked a good day to do it, but I never practiced how to properly say goodbye to them.
Denia: Lying... is the only thing I'm good at.
Rover: Is this the ending you're happy with?
Denia: Of course not. But at least I was able to see their goofy smiles as I had them completely fooled just like before... Something to die happy about, I guess.
[Dialogue Option]  But you're crying.
Denia: It's just... a reaction. That's all. The idea that everything will just vanish, that it'll all go back to the void... it makes me cry. Instantly.
Denia: Just like years ago... When I touched it for the first time...
Rover: Even after you die, tomorrow, the sun still rises.
Denia: Of course I know that. It's not like I think the world will change once I die.
[Dialogue Option]  It will change.
Rover: Sigrika and Nastasha's lives will change. They'll lose an important friend. No matter how they ultimately break from the shadows, what is lost... is lost forever.
[Dialogue Option]  Ever thought about continuing your life?
Denia: Do I deserve to?
Rover: That's not for me to judge.
Rover: But in Rinascita... I've met people just like you.
Rover: In the lives forced upon them, happiness was always fleeting, leaving only pain and fear that never dissipate.
Rover: Yet, even so... they fought for those brief, gifted moments of happiness till the very end.
Rover: You once joked how the great Rover is a savior, but in Rinascita...
Rover: I failed to save them.
Denia: But it sounds like... they made their own choices.
Rover: True. Just like when you tried to drive me away. You also made what you thought was the best choice... You all hoped for more people to survive.
Rover: And so did I.
Rover: So, if the boundaries between humans and creations are already obscure, what is it that determines who we are?
Denia: I... I don't know.
Rover: It's the heart, Denia.
Rover: What you are isn't defined by where you're from, but by your heart.
Denia: The heart.
[Dialogue Option]  Are you willing to trust me?
Denia: This right here. A gift from the Grand Architect—the page buried within my frequency... is here.
Rover: (Could this be... Leviathan?)
Denia: ..."Do find your way home more often"?
Denia: Ha, just as I thought...
Denia: You can really work wonders, Rover.
Rover: Denia?
Denia: You are... literally my least favorite type of person.
[Dialogue Option]  Now, can you tell me why you loathe me?
Denia: Hmm... Where do I start—
Arman: Rover, we've detected a severe frequency fluctuation! Is everything all right?
Rover: Everything's fine. We'll be back soon.
Arman: Very well... I'll see you soon.
Denia: Sounds like Professor Arman is getting a bit impatient. We should head back.
[Dialogue Option]  What about your answer?
Denia: Ahuhuh... No need to get ahead of yourself now, Rover. You're not quite there yet. I'm keeping it secret for now.
Denia: Plus, we still haven't fulfilled our agreement yet. Can't let the cake go to waste.
Denia: Would you want to come out with me again after tomorrow, Rover?
[Dialogue Option]  I would.
Denia: Hmm... Well, that makes things trickier. I... still have things I have to do, after all.
Denia: ...If only today could be a bit longer.
[Dialogue Option]  I wouldn't.
Denia: Is that so? Then I'm relieved... I still have things I have to do, after all.
Denia: However, did it ever cross your mind, Rover, that my being alive and staying here might be an even bigger problem?
Rover: ...If you feel you don't belong here, then some day in the future, would you be willing to—
Denia: Stop right there—it was just a joke. I don't want to put you in a tough spot.
Denia: Easy. Today is my birthday. I won't be going anywhere.
Denia: At least to you... this will be my last lie.

title: Beneath a Melting Night Sky
content:
[Objective: Talk to Arman]
Arman: N.A.N.A. is conducting a thorough checkup on Denia. I imagine this must have been a very long day for you, Rover.
Arman: Her conditions have greatly improved since this morning. As for the frequency fluctuation earlier... Did something happen?
Rover: About that...
You tell Arman about the book page left by the Grand Architect.
Arman: Residual energy of the Threnodian from Rinascita? Could there be some form of interaction between the Threnodians? Is the Fractsidus actually manipulating her and suppressing her abilities through such means?
Arman: It's no wonder we couldn't find the source of the symptoms. Fortunately, you were here to assist, Rover.
[Dialogue Option]  What will happen to Denia after tomorrow?
Arman: ...It'll be the same as the past few days. Although she won't be sent to the New Federation, she'll still be kept under containment and assist with our research.
Arman: I know what you're thinking, Rover... I've been monitoring your itinerary and field reports all day.
Arman: But even if everyone recognizes her as a victim, the Spacetrek Collective's work and responsibilities will not change for her.
Arman: We don't have better solutions now. This is the fact.
[Dialogue Option]  What about her birthday cake?
Arman: We haven't had a chance to get it yet. It's still with Zahira. You can only get that specific Fruit Crackle she requested from Zahira...
Arman: But since she hopes you can accompany her on her birthday, I believe you should be the one to personally bring her the cake... We'll be waiting for you here.

title: Beneath a Melting Night Sky
content:
[Objective: Talk to Arman]
Arman: Back when I taught at the Academy, there was a student who would always sleep in my lectures.
Arman: I would wake her up to answer questions on purpose, because she had no idea what she was wasting.
Arman: Later, a TA named Nastasha asked me to go easy on her, saying she could only sleep in a place where she felt secure, and that her grades in my class were still doing well.
Arman: ...I knew that girl had helped collect data for many people in the Department of Voidmatters, but the issue was that I couldn't understand her behavior at all.
Arman: While everyone else was out pursuing their scientific dreams, how can you be here sleeping? Is your dream to be a research assistant for the rest of your life?
Arman: It was after the Threnodian incident that I finally knew the answer.
Arman: To be honest, when I just sent you the message, for a moment I even fantasized a reply in which you plan to take her far away from Lahai-Roi... to somewhere no one could find.
Arman: Haha... I'm glad you didn't do that, Rover, or else we'd all be done for.

title: Beneath a Melting Night Sky
content:
[Objective: Retrieve the cake from Zahira]
Zahira: Are you here to pick up the birthday cake? One moment please...
Rover: (Denia... She said she had to take care of something. But what, exactly? Does it have something to do with the Threnodian's frequency in the Dimmr Plains?)
Rover: (If the Spacetrek Collective finding Denia was part of the Grand Architect's plan, then what about removing that page from her? Or maybe...)
Rover: (If I were in Denia's shoes...)
Denia: "Easy. Today is my birthday. I won't be going anywhere."
You see the time shown by the Terminal: 00:15 a.m.
It's past Denia's birthday.
Zahira: Here it is... I know it's a bit late, but I believe it's more than enough to convey your heart.
I.R.I.S.: Rover, Denia has left the Academy and is heading towards the Dimmr Plains.
[Dialogue Option]  ...How did she leave?
I.R.I.S.: With her Forte. We've detected residual Voidmatter particles at the platform. Professor Arman was trapped inside a bubble. Luckily, no broken bones.
I.R.I.S.: She hasn't removed her Resonance suppression device and tracker yet. Should we initiate the emergency protocol?
Rover: ...No, give me her location.
I.R.I.S.: Understood, coordinates sent... Good luck, Rover.
[Dialogue Option]  I thought you'd stop her.
Hiyuki: I tried.
Hiyuki: But with her condition now... she would die if I tried any harder.
[Dialogue Option]  That doesn't sound like you.
Hiyuki: Trees will grow tall, and leaves will turn green, Rover...
Hiyuki: That child simply made a grown-up decision.

title: Beneath a Melting Night Sky
subsection: Find the way to the control room
content:
[Objective: Find the way to the control room]
Denia: The Solvein Heartwood... Spectacular, no matter how many times I see it.
Denia: Will this be my last visit?
Denia: Just as I thought... the Voidmatter here is going on a rampage.
Denia: I must get to the "bedroom" quickly.
Denia: Leaving just a few words inside that page, "Do find your way home more often"... Ha, I knew it...
Denia: Sorry, Rover, but just like in the fairytale, the magic wears off past midnight...
Denia: At least this time, I wasn't lying, right?
Denia: Back to this place... Once more.
Denia: Is the elevator locked? Could it be...
Denia: Let's try to go around from the other side...
Nivora: Denia...
Denia: Where did you come from? And aren't you annoying to look at...
Nivora: Denia... I told you a long time ago, didn't I?
Denia: What was that...?
Nivora: The world is a cliff, and civilization a train with carriages of different times.
Denia: My attacks don't do anything... Does it not have a physical form?
Denia: I see, as long as I keep my eyes on it, it'll behave...
Denia, I told you—
A kid can't fight against this world wielding a candy bar—
Nivora: The moment it falls into the abyss, everything will also fall one after the other...
Denia: Tsk, locked... But there should still be an emergency key.
Nivora: First, people abandon their morality, then emotions, and finally faith...
Denia: ...
Denia: ...!
Nivora: In the end, all that's left is an empty shell. The ruins.
Denia: What a pestering ghost.
Nivora: You've been there before. You know how it feels.
Denia: ...Hah.
Nivora: You reach out, yet you fail, even to grab something to end your life.
Denia: Calm down, stop shaking, Denia... I should be able to go around from the other side...
Nivora: There, is where you will finally sink and rest.
Denia: Okay, straight through it.
Nivora: Lives rise and fall like the winter wheat. But agony… agony is the name that never dies.
Denia: (Panting)... (Panting)... So what?
Nivora: ...Let them say, "I walked with the crib of the void."
Denia: Pfft, in your dreams.
Denia: Come on, I'm not hiding from you again.

Denia: Ugh... this experimental Terminal is getting on my nerves.
"Denia": I still feel the abnormal neural reflexes even after an injection lately.
"Nivora": Oh, really? Sounds like you can properly feel pain now.
"Nivora": Remember this feeling, Denia. Pain compels us to live.
Denia: To hell with that feeling... That bastard tried to fool me with saline as a painkiller.
"Nivora": The food here has been left untouched. Why is that, Denia?
"Denia": At Startorch Academy, there's something called dessert.
"Denia": Eating it brings back that scene in my dream.
"Nivora": ...Starting tomorrow, come home for dinner.
"Nivora": You're awake? I prepared a present for you, Denia. I've put it in your heart.
"Denia": What's a present?
"Nivora": A present is... a commodity without a fixed price. You'll be a nice little rule-follower with it.
Denia: Rules? What, "Do find your way home more often" and "Don't bring strangers home"? Hah...
Denia: A broken table I picked up from somewhere... Spent quite some time here.
Denia: When was the last time I read a book? What was I reading? Hmm, "A Professional Guide to Emotional Performance"?
Denia: Oh, it became my draft paper anyhow...
Denia: A textbook for Voidmatters Science, "A Seal-Proof Guide to Enrollment," and... the "Lahai-Roi Meteorology" I borrowed from Nastasha?
Denia: She even snuck a copy of the exam sheet inside... But she never mentioned it was from the previous year. I used all the wrong answers on the real thing, and she teased me about it for ages...
Denia: Those Academy courses were brutal... Barely ever scored above a D besides Voidmatters.
Denia: Strange. They just come rushing back at times like this...
Denia: And what's this... A memory album from the Photography Fan Club?

Abby: How's that for teamwork? I'd sniff out Leviathan's frequency even in a pile of ashes, and snatch it right up!
Rover: Great work, Abby.
Abby: You're very much welcome. Quick, let's go inside and check it out.
Abby: I hope Denia's okay...

metadata.subsection: Find the way to the control room

title: Beneath a Melting Night Sky
content:
[Objective: Read Terminal]
You can read past entries from this Terminal recording experiment data and logs. It seems it hasn't been updated for quite a while.
"...After Phase 2 of the clinical trial, significant differences in Voidmatter particle tolerance were observed between the experimental and control groups. During this period, the experimental target's physiological activities remained normal, with frequency states experiencing intense fluctuations, but no irreversible collapse occurred."
"Towards the end of the trial, all physiological indicators of the experimental group were normal, with no tissue abnormalities and no significant weight changes. This concludes Phase 2."
Aside from the staggered experimental records, the Terminal only has a pre-installed game called Lahai-Roi Blocks.

title: Beneath a Melting Night Sky
content:
[Objective: Inspect cabinet]
A cabinet filled with various medicines, predominantly from the New Federation, including nutritional agents, antibiotics, suppressants, and other drugs...
Some of the labels have been replaced with handwritten tags like "Painkillers: Gross but work", "Sedatives: Somewhat sweet", and "For fevers."

title: Beneath a Melting Night Sky
content:
[Objective: Inspect refrigerator]
An ordinary refrigerator. It's stuffed with tightly wrapped compressed food in the same packaging.
Looks a bit creepy... Want to try it?
[Dialogue Option]  Give it a try.
There is absolutely no texture or taste to it. It can hardly be qualified as food, though fortunately, you feel no discomfort after consuming it.
[Dialogue Option]  No, thanks.
A wise choice.

title: Beneath a Melting Night Sky
content:
[Objective: Inspect operating table]
An operating table with restraining devices. Beside it is a table placed with various surgical cutlery and sterilization tools, and an IV stand with a Fleet Snowfluff sticker.
A pillow is tied to the head of the operating table... Would anyone really sleep on something like this?

title: Beneath a Melting Night Sky
content:
[Objective: Inspect books]
A desk stacked with books, including Startorch Academy textbooks. All books are carefully labeled, showing the owner's efforts to understand the knowledge stored inside.
A carefully preserved photo album sits right in the center of the desk. Take a look?
[Dialogue Option]  Take a look.
It's filled with photos of Denia. She's smiling in every picture.
[Dialogue Option]  Not now.
You wonder if more photos will be added to this album.

title: Beneath a Melting Night Sky
content:
[Objective: Inspect notice]
You see a notice on the door: "Denia's Room. Keep Out!"
Denia might be on the other side of this door... Open it?
[Dialogue Option]  (Open the door.)
speakers: You see a notice on the door
You see a notice on the door

title: Beneath a Melting Night Sky
content:
[Objective: Touch the bubble]
A bubble containing weak fluctuating frequencies. Looks like someone left a message for you.
[Dialogue Option]  (Touch the bubble)
Denia: I assume by the time you get here, Rover, everything will have ended. Sorry I had to say goodbye this way.
Denia: This is where it all started. The Fractsidus's Lahai-Roi plan... where the Grand Architect first made contact with Aleph-1. And... where I was created.
Denia: I took the Threnodian fragment the Fractsidus left here. Leaving it here would only cause more suffering... As for the experimental data, consider it a parting gift from me to the Spacetrek Collective.
Denia: To be honest, I did think of telling you everything about this place.
Denia: But sometimes gifts can be incredibly inappropriate. Your worries were correct. When the book page was removed, I received the Grand Architect's final message.
(Story image: T_Main_03_03_C_03_Male)
(Story image: T_Main_03_03_C_03_Female)
Denia: Now, I am the last anchor point between Aleph-1 and Solaris. If I die according to plan, its fragment will disappear, along with me.
Denia: I used to tell myself that was karma. But what does an ending like that mean for Sigrika? For Nastasha? For someone like you, who always tries to save everyone?
Denia: You're the Grand Architect's greatest rival. So, making you betray your own heart is a bigger prize to them than the Threnodian fragment.
Denia: It would mean that after all the frustration and failure, you're no different from them. You'd end up going down the same path.
Denia: But if you had removed that page, the fragment would've lost control after receiving the message... It would've tried to find me, attempting to connect with Aleph-1 out of instinct.
Denia: So, when I think about it... it's a good thing you never got to finish what you wanted to say back there.
(Story image: T_Main_03_03_C_02)
Denia: I was a child who showed up at the Fractsidus's door out of nowhere. Became their Threnodian lab mouse by accident. Ever since I can remember, they told me I existed for one reason... to make that moment happen.
Denia: I've questioned myself countless times: What is the point of everything that I've been through?
Denia: The answer is always the same. There is no point. Birth, pain, struggle, death... None of these have meaning.
Denia: That's why when I first heard your story from the Grand Architect, I absolutely hated you, Rover.
Denia: If someone like that is actually out there... then where were they during the longest, most painful days of my life?
Denia: And why... why would you appear before me just as everything was about to end?
Denia: You know what I hated most? Why did everything about you have to be so impossible?
Denia: Our encounter was... never fair.
(Story image: T_Main_03_03_C_01_Male)
(Story image: T_Main_03_03_C_01_Female)
Denia: So, I hope you can forgive me for not saying goodbye. This is something I must put an end to on my own.
Denia: It's just... it hurts to watch the way you live, Rover... I can't even imagine a day when someone like you runs out of miracles.
Denia: They call you Rover, but you don't even know where you started or where you're going... Even if you made your ideals real... where would that leave you? Where is your happiness in all of that?
Denia: I never understood what the Grand Architect was mumbling. The future, evolution, or what's going to happen eons later—
Denia: But at that moment, in front of Aleph-1, I didn't want you to die. At least not at the hands of the Grand Architect, who's got nothing left but mere survival.
Denia: What surprised me was that... despite hating you so much, I actually spent such an unprecedented day with you.
Denia: For the first time, I had my own birthday. For the first time, I forgot about the fear brought by the void. For the first time... I met someone I can truly open up to.
Denia: How should I describe this emotion? It's a kind of hate, isn't it?
(Story image: T_Main_03_03_C_04)
Denia: I don't know where Voidmatter particles will take me next... if I could start over, I'd like to visit the cities Nastasha talked about, to visit places where there are no Void Storms and Soliskin.
Denia: Maybe I'll try picking a different major, try napping in different classes, and taste different cakes in every cafeteria I go to...
Denia: Then, no matter how many times it'll take, I'll come back to Lahai-Roi, back to all of you.
Denia: Whatever you wanted to say, you can tell me the next time we meet.
Denia: Oh, I almost forgot something important... Actually, all those powers the Grand Architect displayed, including shapeshifting, are not her true Forte.
Denia: Those are derivatives at best... And the shapeshifting has a catch: she needs long-term observation and analysis of her target to pull it off.
Denia: It's just... the idea of her using my face to talk to you... it makes me sick. So let's have a code word. Just between us.
Denia: Next time, if it's truly me... all my old "hates" will become "likes."
Denia: Oh, and could you help me enjoy half of my birthday cake? You can save the whole thing for me, of course. But don't you throw away any of the toppings.
Leave Denia's cake here?
[Dialogue Option]  Yes.
[Dialogue Option]  No.
Abby: Rover... Will we ever see Denia again?
Rover: We will.
Abby: Okay... But, what about the thing you didn't get to say, Rover?
Abby: "If you feel you don't belong here, then some day in the future, would you be willing to..." And? What about the rest?
Rover: Secret. For now.

title: Beneath a Melting Night Sky
subsection: Return to Startorch Academy and gather your thoughts
content:
[Objective: Return to Startorch Academy and gather your thoughts]
You can feel your eyelids sinking. In a haze, you seem to have returned to that familiar scene again.
Rover: Denia... Do you have any clues about that scene in your memory?
Denia: Nothing.
Denia: It was just a scene. Maybe from some movies I watched as a kid?
Rover: But maybe... in my opinion... you still have a chance to...
Denia: Now you're reminding me of what Nastasha once said.
Rover: Huh?
Denia: "Raise your head, what do you see?"
Rover: Lahai-Roi's night sky.
Denia: True enough. But my reply was "The void. The darkness."
Rover: What was her reaction?
Denia: She said it was actually light fighting against darkness.
Denia: "But it looks like darkness has the upper hand," I said.
Rover: But there was only darkness in Lahai-Roi at the beginning. Then came the light.
Denia: Haha, you answered exactly the same way as she did.
Rover: So light actually prevailed.
Denia: You're right, Rover.
Denia: I guess if you never give up, the story will one day have a good ending, no?
(Quest complete: Beneath a Melting Night Sky)
(Obtained Trophy: Amanojaku)

title: At Dream's Edge
content: Quest Objective: A Somnoire door has suddenly appeared in the Academy. Mornye has asked for your help investigating it.

title: At Dream's Edge
content:
[Objective: Read Mornye's WavesLine message]
Mornye: Mentor, there's been an emergency.
Mornye: Half an hour ago, a door materialized out of nowhere on campus. As a precaution, the Academy has evacuated students and initiated an investigation.
Mornye: The door itself poses no direct threat. However, an abnormal frequency leaking from behind it is slowly contaminating the surrounding environment.
[Choice]  What do you mean by "contaminating"?
(Rover): What do you mean by "contaminating"?
[Choice]  Abnormal frequency?
(Rover): Abnormal frequency?
Mornye: It's rewriting the frequency of anything it comes into contact with, assimilating it as part of itself.
Mornye: ...As of now, we haven't found a way to stop it.
[Choice]  A door appearing out of nowhere, huh...
(Rover): Abnormal frequency, a door... This has the Somnoire written all over it.
[Choice]  Could it be a Somnoire door?
(Rover): This sounds like it might have something to do with the Somnoire.
(Rover): Are you at the Research Institute? I'll come now.
Mornye: ...Yes. Thank you, Mentor.}}

title: At Dream's Edge
content:
(Rover): Are you at the Research Institute? I'll come now.
Mornye: ...Yes. Thank you, Mentor.}}



Abby: Somnoire doors are only supposed to show up in the middle of nowhere! What the heck is going on?
Rover: The Ivory Gatekeeper will have answers. We'll contact it after we see Mornye and find out what's happening.

title: At Dream's Edge
content:
[Objective: Meet up with Mornye]
Mornye: Mentor, Abby. You made it.
Abby: Hey, it's been a minute—Huh?
Abby: Wait a sec. Mornye, what's up with that weird smell on ya?
Abby: Smells kinda like a Tacet Discord, kinda like a machine... but it's different from Exoswarm...
Abby: Uh... but I can't tell what it is exactly.
Mornye: ...That smell might be coming from the frequency sample I just collected.
[Dialogue Option]  The one you mentioned in your message?
[Dialogue Option]  The frequency that's contaminating the area?
Mornye: Yes. We are currently running tests on it. I hope we learn something.
Mornye: Mentor, I looked into this Somnoire you mentioned... it seems to be some kind of dreamscape, correct?
Rover: It's usually guarded by two Gatekeepers. They make sure no Nightmare Tacet Discords or other frequencies cross into our reality.
Rover: Whenever there was a problem in the past, we handled it.
Rover: But we've never come across a frequency able to rewrite space itself... Has the Academy been affected?
Mornye: At this stage, the door's area of influence remains limited.
Mornye: The Academy has cordoned off a danger zone and instructed everyone to keep their distance.
Mornye: I've asked Lynae to retrieve samples for analysis. Later, I will consult with the Collective to formulate a response.
Mornye: But... all we can do is buy time. We cannot contain the frequency's spread.
Rover: Leave the investigation of the door to me. I want this resolved quickly, before it can harm the Academy.
Mornye: ...Mm, understood.
Mornye: The door's coordinates... I've sent them to your Terminal. Mentor, please be careful.

Ivory Gatekeeper has added you as a friend. You may now begin chatting.
Ivory Gatekeeper: HEEEELLP MEOW! A little assistance, pwease? QAQ
[Choice]  What a coincidence.
(Rover): I was about to contact you... It's about the Somnoire.
[Choice]  Is this about Startorch Academy?
(Rover): Did you add me to discuss the Startorch Academy situation?
Ivory Gatekeeper: Oh meow?! How did you find out so fast!
Ivory Gatekeeper:
Ivory Gatekeeper: Oh meow... I don't really know what's happening either...
Ivory Gatekeeper: If this keeps up, the frequency will spread across the whole school.
Ivory Gatekeeper: And if that happens, everyone will get pulled into the Somnoire. And never wake up again.
(Rover): So the situation is worse than I thought.
(Rover): Professor Mornye from the Academy is looking into it. You can talk to her about what's going on.
(Rover): Hold on, I'll make a group chat.

title: At Dream's Edge
content:
Rover: We should be safe here. You alright?
???: Took a hit... But my cyberwear is still functional.
Rover: (...Cyberwear?)
Rover: (Her body bears modifications. Fractsidus work?)
Rover: (...No. On closer look, the style is different from what you see on an Artificer.)
Rover: (She might have useful intel on the problem... And she doesn't seem hostile for now. I'll give it more time to decide whether she's a threat.)
???: 'Preciate the save. But there's somethin' I gotta do...
Rover: You're still hurt. Sure you're up for it?
???: This all feels so real... But how... if not a dream?
???: David... Rebecca...
[Dialogue Option]  David?
[Dialogue Option]  Rebecca?
Rover: Friends of yours?
Rover: The Somnoire is a labyrinth. You go in there blind, and you'll only get lost.
Rover: Catch your breath first. Once you're steady on your feet, I can help you look for them.
???: Somnoire...?
???: Why help me at all, a total stranger?
Rover: Best option in front of me right now. You want to find your friends, and I want to investigate the disturbance here.
Rover: In your current state, finding them alone is… optimistic.
Rover: Think of it as a temporary alliance. If we stop seeing eye-to-eye, you're free to walk away anytime.
???: Can't say I trust you yet... but...
???: I'm Lucy, 'kay?
[Dialogue Option]  I'm Rover.
Lucy: Won't forget it. Your name... or your help.
Rover: Why was that Nightmare Tacet Discord targeting you specifically?
Lucy: What's a... "Nightmare Tacet Discord"?
Rover: The monster on your tail just before.
Lucy: Got no idea why... If David and Rebecca hadn't been there, I'd be...
Lucy: ...I gotta find 'em. Fast.
Lucy: Where should we go next?
Rover: We may be able to find something deeper in the Somnoire... Follow me.

title: At Dream's Edge
content:
[Objective: Find Lucy's companions]
Lucy: ...A train? What's a Night City train doing behind a door?
Rover: Night City?
Lucy: ...
Rover: You don't have to explain if you don't want to.
Rover: The Somnoire is where dreams gather. It's a place where anything can happen.
Lucy: Anything? Sure, makes sense...

title: At Dream's Edge
content:
[Objective: Explore ahead]
Lucy: There she is!

title: At Dream's Edge
content:
[Objective: Approach Lucy's companion]
Lucy: Rebecca!
Rebecca: Nova, looks like you made it out all right.
Rebecca: But... who's this choom? You two know each other?
Lucy: This is Rover. He pulled me out before that thing, that... Nightmare Tacet Discord could flatline me.
Rebecca: Nightmare Tacet Discord? The f*ck kinda name is that?
[Dialogue Option]  That is... what they're called.
[Dialogue Option]  I see we have a big personality over here...
Rebecca: F*ck! F*ck! F*ck! Next time I see one, I'm blastin' it!
Rebecca: Thanks for lookin' out for Lucy.
Rebecca: Name's Rebecca. Nice to meet ya, choom.
Lucy: ...Where's David? He's not with you?
Lucy: What's this?
Rebecca: After the smoke cleared, was all I could find. Guess, coverin' our backs... couldn't cover his own.
Rebecca: Didn't get a clear look, but... no one could've survived that attack. I think he...
Lucy: David's... gone?
Lucy: Agh!
Rebecca: Agh! My head's splittin'! The hell's that noise?! Is the whole place comin' down?!
Rebecca: …Lucy? Yo, gotta snap out of it!
Rover: The frequency is spreading. It's not safe here. We need to leave, now.
Rebecca: Fine, whatever! Hold on tight, Luce!

title: At Dream's Edge
content:
[Objective: Touch Lucy's memory]
Rebecca: The f*ck? Where'd you take us?!
Rover: This is Startorch Academy, in Lahai-Roi. I entered the Somnoire from here.
Rebecca: The Som-what now? Lahai-Roi? Startorch?
Rebecca: That some kinda gang slang around here?
Rebecca: Or no, wait... Are they corp names? Y'know, like Arasaka?
Rover: Arasaka? What's that?
Rebecca: You ain't never heard of Arasaka? Oh, this is bad...
Rebecca: …Gah! What the hell is going on?!
Rebecca: Nothin' around here looks even halfway familiar... Am I stuck in some kinda borked ?
Lucy: This isn't a BD, Becca.
[Dialogue Option]  How are you holding up?
[Dialogue Option]  You should take it easy.
Lucy: Head's still ringin' a bit, but otherwise seem to be fine.
Lucy: Crazy as it sounds... Not sure we're in our world anymore, if that's even the right word.
Rebecca: You skezzed, choom? Or maybe your circuits got fried?
Lucy: I also wondered if this could be a braindance. Or some other kinda sim.
Lucy: But I'm not gettin' a read on any BD gear. Memories seem fine too, no signs of tampering.
Lucy: What convinced me this is... someplace else... was this.
Lucy: This mark – it's not ink or chrome. It's giving me a… weird feeling. Can't classify it.
Rebecca: Got one on my shoulder, too... But so what? Ain't like that disproves this bein' a BD.
Lucy: Hm, you've got the same mark on your hand, Rover. Lemme guess – ain't a coincidence?
Abby: It's called a Tacet Mark. It shows up when a Resonator's power kicks in.
Lucy: Did... something just fly out of it? How's that possible?
Rebecca: I WANT ONE!
Rebecca: How many eddies for the talkin' plushie?! I'll buy one right this second.
Abby: Who're you calling a plushie?! I'm an Echo! Rover and I go way back.
Rover: Let me introduce you. Everyone, this is Abby. My very important partner. It was thanks to Abby that I found you when I did.
Rebecca: Your partner? This little puffball?
Rebecca: Dunno what you mean by "Echo," but makes you sound like kind of a big deal, huh?
Rebecca: Not bad, you little turd. You're growin' on me!
Abby: Hehe, just helping out Rover. Someone's gotta.
Abby: But you've never heard of an Echo? What about a Tacet Discord? Do you know what those are?
Rebecca: Nope... Ring any bells, Lucy?
Lucy: If I had access to the Net, might be able to dig up something...
Rebecca: Yeah, no Net access is weird, I'll give ya that. But another world? C'mon. Am I right, Rover?
Rover: (Appearing suddenly in the Somnoire. Unknown modification tech. Using unfamiliar terms. No knowledge of Echoes and Tacet Discords...)
Rover: Maybe... the two of you really are from another universe.
Lucy: Really think so?
Rover: It's hard to swallow. But it's the only explanation that fits.
Rover: That said, I'm not gonna trust you on faith... You'll need to show me proof if you want to convince me.
Lucy: Sure, I guess... What is it you wanna know exactly?
Rover: I'm looking to find the source of the disturbance and end it. To do that, I need a complete picture.
Rover: How did you get here? Where did that Nightmare Tacet Discord come from? I'm hoping you can give me some kind of explanation.
Lucy: Rebecca... This might take a minute.
Rebecca: Whatever. This crap's way over my head anyway.
Lucy: ...Thanks.

title: At Dream's Edge
content:
Lucy: Rebecca... This might take a minute.
Rebecca: Whatever. This crap's way over my head anyway.
Lucy: ...Thanks.



(Cutscene plays)
Lucy? Feels like it's been ages.
Hey, yeah... You, uh, got anything for insomnia?
Having trouble sleeping?
Don't need my tarot cards to see that.
Worry not, got just the thing – my pendulum.
First time using it over holocall, though.
Right, now think back to your fondest memories.
Find them. Embrace them.
...David?
Sweet dreams, Lucy.
(Cutscene ends)
